keys: the tool works while the pointer is on it — no button needed
look around — the view returns to the work by itself
touch: Touch and hold the red ring
the tool works while your finger is on it
look around — the view returns to the work by itself
HSIM_T.follow: Keep the pointer on the aiming ring — the work goes on while you are on it.
HSIM_T.men: Stay with the crew — keep the pointer on the man at work.
HSIM_T.potOut: {P}: pot life exceeded — the batch has set in the bucket. Mix a fresh batch.
HSIM_T.potGo: The pot life of {P} runs: approx. {m} minutes.
HSIM_T.thick: Too much material here — more than the data sheet allows in one step.
HSIM_T.thin: The coat is thin here — brush more material in.
HSIM_T.covered: Coverage {c} % · approx. {k} kg/m² (data sheet: approx. {t} kg/m²)
HSIM_T.coverNeed: Cover the whole area free of pores: {c} % so far.
HSIM_T.edge: Hold the brush at the edge of the view — the view turns with it.
HSIM_T.quizBad: Not what the data sheet says:
HSIM_T.no3d: The simulator needs WebGL and an internet connection to load the 3D library.

HSIMS.wp.mats.M30.t.name: ASOCRET-M30
steps: Put 4.5–5.25 l of water per 25 kg into a clean mixing bucket and add the powder.
Mix approx. 3 minutes to a homogeneous, lump-free mass.
Maturing time approx. 5 minutes.
Homogenise again.
Pot life approx. 45 minutes.
HSIMS.wp.mats.M30.t.note: Stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm. Do not add water or new mortar to mortar that has already set.

HSIMS.wp.mats.AQ1K.t.name: AQUAFIN-1K
steps: Put approx. 6.7 l of water per 25 kg (26–27 %) into a clean mixing bucket and add the powder.
Mix approx. 3 minutes to a homogeneous, lump-free mass.
Pot life approx. 60 minutes.
HSIMS.wp.mats.AQ1K.t.note: Stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm. Do not add water or new mortar to mortar that has already set (risk of inadequate strength development).

HSIMS.wp.mats.RB400.t.name: AQUAFIN-RB400
steps: Put the liquid component B into a clean mixing bucket and add the powder component A (A : B = 1.5 : 1 by weight).
Mix approx. 3 minutes to a homogeneous, lump-free mass.
Settling period approx. 5 minutes.
Homogenise the compound thoroughly again. Water only after mixing: max. 0.24 l per 24 kg.
Pot life approx. 45 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C.
HSIMS.wp.mats.RB400.t.note: Stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm. Do not add water or new material to material that has already set.

gate.title: Waterproof the basement wall from the inside, with your own hands
gate.desc: The concrete basement wall of the 3D sample — jetted, repaired, pre-sealed and coated twice with AQUAFIN-RB400 against pressing water from the rear. You guide the lance, the chipping hammer and the trowel, mix every material with its mixing and maturing time, brush, trowel and spray the coats yourself to the material rate of the technical data sheet, and keep the pot life. No site, no risk: repeat it as often as you like.
gate.foot: Thirteen phases from the technical data sheets of ASOCRET-M30, AQUAFIN-1K and AQUAFIN-RB400; the site clock runs through the waiting times.

HSIMS.wp.t.eyebrow: Operation briefing · Basement wall, from the inside
HSIMS.wp.t.title: Negative-side waterproofing with AQUAFIN-RB400
HSIMS.wp.t.sub: An existing concrete basement wall lets water through at a construction joint and at honeycombed zones; the old paint flakes. The outside cannot be dug up. Prepare, repair and pre-seal the wall, then coat it twice with AQUAFIN-RB400 to ≥ 3.0 mm dry film — flexible and crack-bridging, against pressing water from the negative side (WTA 4-6, up to 0.75 bar).
brief: Jet the face at > 400 bar, break out the honeycombs
Fill pockets, tie holes and the chased joint with ASOCRET-M30; sealing cove
Pre-seal with AQUAFIN-1K brushed in, ≤ 1 mm per step
The joint band of AQUAFIN-RB400, 15 cm on both sides
First coat RB400 with the trowel, second after 3 hours — ≥ 3.0 mm dry film
Keep damp for at least 3 days

phases.p: Select the jet lance and hold the pointer on the nozzle: the face is jetted from the top down at > 400 bar until paint and lime runs are gone and the concrete is laid bare, matt damp.
phases.done: Substrate laid bare, pore-open, matt damp.

phases.p: Select the chipping hammer and stay with it: the honeycombed zones are broken out to sound concrete, the edges cut square.
phases.done: Honeycombs broken out to sound concrete.

phases.p: Mix ASOCRET-M30, then guide the trowel: pockets and tie holes are filled, the chased construction joint filled flush from the bottom up (3–30 mm in one step).
phases.done: Pockets, tie holes and joint filled flush.

phases.p: Mix AQUAFIN-1K for the bonding slurry. Brush it along the wall–floor joint, then form the sealing cove of ASOCRET-M30 wet in wet, edge height ≥ 4 cm, rounded.
phases.done: Sealing cove formed on its bonding slurry.

phases.p: The cementitious cove can be overcoated after approx. 3 hours. The mixed material in the buckets goes off meanwhile — fresh batches for the next step.

Mix AQUAFIN-1K and brush it into the matt damp wall and the floor strip yourself: drag over the surfaces with the brush, pore-deep, approx. 1.75 kg/m² (≤ 1 mm per step; more than 2 kg/m² in one step can crack).
phases.done: Pre-sealed — the rigid slurry keeps the moisture from the rear off the flexible coating.

phases.p: AQUAFIN-1K is overcoated after approx. 6 hours. The site clock runs.
Mix AQUAFIN-RB400 (A : B = 1.5 : 1, 3 minutes, mature 5 minutes, homogenise). Guide the notched trowel over the construction joint, 15 cm on both sides, to ≥ 4.0 mm dry film, then smooth.
phases.done: Construction joint reinforced with the band of RB400.

phases.p: Trowel the first coat yourself over wall and floor strip, free of pores: an even thickness with the coating-thickness trowel, approx. 1.8 kg/m² (1.5 mm dry). Keep the pot life of 45 minutes.
phases.done: First coat applied, free of pores.

phases.p: The second application step follows when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking — after approx. 3 hours. Mix a fresh batch.
Spray or trowel the second coat over the first, free of pores, approx. 1.8 kg/m²: the two coats give ≥ 3.0 mm dry film for pressing water (≥ 2.0 mm would be soil moisture only).
phases.done: Second coat applied — the thick-layer coating is complete.

phases.p: Select the hose and keep the fresh coating damp; it is protected from draught, sun and direct heating. 1 bar after approx. 16 hours, pressurised water after ≥ 1 day.
phases.done: Kept damp; ventilated, no condensation.

phases.p: Kept damp ≥ 3 days. The flexible, crack-bridging, radon-tight coating holds the pressing water from the rear.

HSIMS.wp.t.res_title: The wall is waterproofed. Flexible, crack-bridging, radon-tight.
HSIMS.wp.t.res_sub: Plaster, tiles or a coating may follow once the system has cured. Clean the tools with water immediately after use. Observe the technical data sheets and the safety data sheets.

HSIMS.rc.mats.F20.t.name: FIX-20-T
steps: Approx. 200–250 g of water per kg of powder into a clean bucket — a small quantity only, what can be placed at once.
Mix at least approx. 1 minute to a homogeneous, lump-free mass. Gloves!
Solidification starts after 1–2 minutes: pot life approx. 2 minutes.
HSIMS.rc.mats.F20.t.note: Low temperatures: warm water and pre-warmed powder; high temperatures: cool water — the powder must not exceed +23 °C.

HSIMS.rc.mats.IM.t.name: ASOCRET-IM
steps: 3.75–4.25 l of water per 25 kg into a clean mixing bucket, the powder in.
Mix approx. 3 minutes to a homogeneous, lump-free mass of filler consistency.
Pot life approx. 30 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C.
HSIMS.rc.mats.IM.t.note: Stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm. Up to 10 mm per application step.

HSIMS.rc.mats.IC.t.name: AQUAFIN-IC
steps: 6.75–8 l of water per 25 kg (27–32 %) into a clean mixing bucket; add the powder while stirring vigorously.
Mix approx. 3 minutes until homogeneous and clump-free.
Maturing time approx. 3–5 minutes.
Mix again.
Pot life approx. 60 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C.
HSIMS.rc.mats.IC.t.note: Stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm; liquid consistency, density approx. 1.6 kg/dm³.

gate.title: Stop the water and make the wall crystalline with your own hands
gate.desc: The leaking basement wall of the 3D sample: the running water stopped with a plug of FIX-20-T within its two-minute pot life, the joint chased and filled with ASOCRET-IM on a screen of AQUAFIN-IC, the coved fillet, then two coats of AQUAFIN-IC brushed into the matt damp concrete to 1.5 kg/m² — you guide the tools, mix with the maturing times, brush the coats yourself and let the crystals grow.
gate.foot: Eleven phases from the technical data sheets of FIX-20-T, ASOCRET-IM and AQUAFIN-IC; the site clock runs through the waiting times.

HSIMS.rc.t.eyebrow: Operation briefing · Basement wall, negative pressing water
HSIMS.rc.t.title: Crystalline waterproofing from the inside with AQUAFIN-IC
HSIMS.rc.t.sub: Ground water presses through a construction joint of the concrete basement wall: the joint leaks, lime leaches out, at its foot the water runs in. The outside cannot be dug up. Stop the water, chase and fill the joint, form the cove, then brush two coats of AQUAFIN-IC into the matt damp concrete: the crystals grow into the capillaries and hold the pressing water back — up to 1.5 bar from the negative side.
brief: Jet both walls at > 400 bar; chase the joint 20 × 25 mm; chisel the leak to a dovetail
Wet to matt damp — no puddles
Plug the running water with FIX-20-T, pressed in by hand and held until it hardens
Screen with AQUAFIN-IC, fill with ASOCRET-IM wet in wet; coved fillet approx. 4 cm
Two coats of AQUAFIN-IC, 1.5 kg/m² in total for pressing water
Keep damp ≥ 3 days, ventilated

phases.p: Select the jet lance and hold the pointer on the nozzle: the back wall and the right wall are jetted from the top down at > 400 bar until the concrete is pore-open and absorbent.
phases.done: Substrate pore-open, free of adhesion-inhibiting substances.

phases.p: Select the chipping hammer and stay with it: the construction joint is chased 20 mm wide and 25 mm deep; where the water runs out, the opening is chiselled to a dovetail for the plug.
phases.done: Joint chased 20 × 25 mm, the leak dovetailed.

phases.p: Select the hose and dampen walls and floor with clean water: matt damp at the time of application, no puddles. Repeated moistening favours the growth of the crystals.
phases.done: Matt damp, no puddles.

phases.p: Mix a small quantity of FIX-20-T. Hold the pointer on the leak: the plug is pressed into the dovetailed opening by hand and held until it hardens — after 1–2 minutes, with a noticeable warming. Within the pot life of 2 minutes!
phases.done: The water is stopped. FIX-20-T solidifies even under water and swells against the concrete.

phases.p: Mix AQUAFIN-IC and ASOCRET-IM. Brush the screen of IC into the chased joint, then fill it flush with IM wet in wet, up to 10 mm per step (approx. 1.3 kg per metre of 20 × 25 mm).
phases.done: Joint and crack filled flush on a screen of AQUAFIN-IC.

phases.p: Guide brush and trowel along the wall–floor joint and up the corner: the substrate screened with AQUAFIN-IC, ASOCRET-IM applied wet in wet with an edge height of approx. 4 cm, rounded.
phases.done: Coved fillet formed — part of the crystalline system.

phases.p: After approx. 1–3 hours the fresh mortar is reworked with AQUAFIN-IC. The batches in the buckets have gone off — mix fresh.

Mix AQUAFIN-IC and brush the first coat yourself into the matt damp concrete — wall, floor strip, over the filled joint and the fresh fillet: evenly, worked in meticulously, free of pores, approx. 0.75 kg/m².
phases.done: First coat brushed in.

phases.p: Brush the second coat while the first is still sticky and has not dried out: approx. 0.75 kg/m² more — 1.5 kg/m² in two layers for accumulated and pressing water.
phases.done: Second coat applied; drying of the first was avoided.

phases.p: Select the hose: jute sheets are hung and the coating is kept damp, the room ventilated — no condensation, no direct heating. The crystals grow into the capillaries.
phases.done: Kept damp and ventilated.

phases.p: Kept damp ≥ 3 days. Foot traffic after approx. 5 hours; withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days.

HSIMS.rc.t.res_title: The wall is dry. The crystals hold the pressing water back.
HSIMS.rc.t.res_sub: Negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal when water reaches them. Movement and connecting joints take the ASO-Dichtband system. Observe the technical data sheets and the safety data sheets.

HSIMS.cr.mats.HSF.t.name: ASOCRET-HS-FLEX (corrosion protection)
steps: Approx. 5.5–5.75 l of water per 25 kg into a clean mixing bucket, the powder in — the consistency for the corrosion protection.
Mix approx. 3 minutes.
Activation time approx. 5 minutes.
Mix again.
Pot life approx. 60 minutes at 5–30 °C.
HSIMS.cr.mats.HSF.t.note: Approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm; approx. 1 mm per application step.

HSIMS.cr.mats.HSFB.t.name: ASOCRET-HS-FLEX (bond coat)
steps: Approx. 6.75–7.0 l of water per 25 kg — the brushable consistency of the bond coat.
Mix approx. 3 minutes.
Activation time approx. 5 minutes.
Mix again.
Pot life approx. 60 minutes.
HSIMS.cr.mats.HSFB.t.note: Approx. 1.5 kg/m² per mm. In case of interruptions the bond coat must set completely; then repeat it.

HSIMS.cr.mats.BIS540.t.name: ASOCRET-BIS-5/40
steps: Put approx. 2.8–3.0 l of water into a clean mixing bucket and add 25 kg of powder.
Pre-mix approx. 3 minutes to a homogeneous, lump-free mass.
Add the remaining water: in total approx. 3.5–3.75 l.
Mix sufficiently (forced paddle mixer for larger quantities).
Pot life approx. 60 minutes; approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm.
HSIMS.cr.mats.BIS540.t.note: Do not add water or new mortar to mortar that has already set (risk of inadequate strength development).

HSIMS.cr.mats.BIS16.t.name: ASOCRET-BIS-1/6
steps: 5–5.25 l of water per 25 kg into a clean mixing bucket, the powder in.
Mix approx. 3 minutes.
Settling period approx. 5 minutes.
Homogenise again.
Pot life approx. 60 minutes; approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm.
HSIMS.cr.mats.BIS16.t.note: Up to 6 mm per application step; on BIS-5/40 after 24 hours at the earliest.

gate.title: Repair the corroding beam with your own hands
gate.desc: The spalled reinforced concrete beam of the 3D sample: saw the edges, jet out the carbonated concrete, de-rust the bar to SA 2½, protect it twice with ASOCRET-HS-FLEX, brush in the bond coat and re-profile with ASOCRET-BIS-5/40 wet in wet, smooth with ASOCRET-BIS-1/6 and cure. You guide every tool and mix every mortar with its water, mixing and activation time — and keep the pot life.
gate.foot: Seventeen phases from the technical data sheets of ASOCRET-HS-FLEX, ASOCRET-BIS-5/40 and ASOCRET-BIS-1/6; the site clock runs through the waiting times.

HSIMS.cr.t.eyebrow: Operation briefing · Reinforced concrete beam, garage
HSIMS.cr.t.title: Concrete repair with the ASOCRET-BIS system
HSIMS.cr.t.sub: The carbonated cover has spalled off over a corroding bar. Expose and de-rust the reinforcement, protect it, bond the repair mortar wet in wet and re-profile the beam flush, then close the surface with the fine smoothing mortar — the system of ASOCRET-HS-FLEX, ASOCRET-BIS-5/40 and ASOCRET-BIS-1/6.
brief: Saw the edges square; break out and jet the carbonated concrete behind the bar
De-rust to SA 2½, rinse
ASOCRET-HS-FLEX on the steel: two coats, the second after approx. 2 hours
Pre-wet; bond coat of ASOCRET-HS-FLEX brushed in pore-deep
ASOCRET-BIS-5/40 wet in wet, ≤ 20 mm per step, compacted and levelled flush
ASOCRET-BIS-1/6 after 24 hours, 1–6 mm; keep damp 3–5 days

phases.p: Select the disc cutter and stay with it: the edges of the repair area are cut square — no feather edges.
phases.done: Edges cut square.

phases.p: Select the jet lance and hold the pointer on the nozzle: the carbonated, loose concrete is removed to sound concrete, behind the bar as well — at least 20 mm clear round the steel.
phases.done: Broken out to sound concrete, the bar exposed all round.

phases.p: Select the blaster and follow it along the bar: the reinforcement is de-rusted to SA 2½, bright metal.
phases.done: Reinforcement de-rusted to SA 2½.

phases.p: Select the hose: dust and grit are rinsed off the repair area.
phases.done: Clean and dust-free.

phases.p: Mix ASOCRET-HS-FLEX for the corrosion protection (5.5–5.75 l per 25 kg). Guide the brush: the first coat on the reinforcing steel, fully covering, approx. 1 mm.
phases.done: First coat of corrosion protection applied.

phases.p: The second coat is applied after approx. 2 hours, when the first coat is brushable. The batch goes off meanwhile.
Mix a fresh batch and brush the second coat over the first, fully covering.
phases.done: Reinforcement protected with two coats.

phases.p: The repair mortar can be applied approx. 6 hours after the second coat has hardened.
Select the hose: the mineral substrate is pre-moistened so that it is matt damp at the time of application — no shiny film of water, no puddles.
phases.done: Matt damp.

phases.p: Mix ASOCRET-HS-FLEX in the bond-coat consistency (6.75–7.0 l per 25 kg). Guide the hard brush: the bond coat is brushed into the prepared substrate in a single coat, down to the pores, fully covering.
phases.done: Bond coat brushed in pore-deep — the mortar follows while it is wet.

phases.p: Mix ASOCRET-BIS-5/40. Stay with the tool: the mortar is applied into the fresh bond coat — sprayed or thrown on with the trowel — and compacted; max. 20 mm in one step.
phases.done: First layer applied wet in wet and compacted.

phases.p: Guide trowel and straight edge: the second layer is applied fresh in fresh within the pot life, compacted and levelled flush with the surface.
phases.done: Beam re-profiled flush.

phases.p: ASOCRET-BIS-1/6 on BIS-5/40: after 24 hours at the earliest. Keep the mortar damp meanwhile.
Mix ASOCRET-BIS-1/6. Guide the trowel: a scratch coat first, then the layer of 1–6 mm over the repaired area, struck off within the pot life.
phases.done: Surface closed with ASOCRET-BIS-1/6.

phases.p: Select the sponge board and stay with it: after a corresponding waiting time the surface is treated with the felt board.
phases.done: Surface felted.

phases.p: Select the hose: the mortar is kept damp and protected from draught and sun — curing film or wet jute.
phases.done: Curing started.

phases.p: Keep the mortar damp for at least 3–5 days. The site clock runs.

HSIMS.cr.t.res_title: The beam is repaired. Steel protected, section restored, surface closed.
HSIMS.cr.t.res_sub: Clean the tools with water immediately after use. Observe the technical data sheets and the safety data sheets; the repair principles of EN 1504-9 apply.

HSIMS.pf.mats.V360P.t.name: ASODUR-V360W primer
steps: Stir component A, add component B: 100 : 20 parts by weight.
Mix approx. 3 minutes.
Stir in the water for the primer: 8–10 %, not more than 10 %.
Pot life approx. 40 minutes.
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360P.t.sliderBad: The primer is diluted with 8–10 % water (max. 10 %).
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360P.t.note: Dry substrate ≤ 5 CM-%; substrate and air 10–35 °C, 3 °C above the dew point; approx. 0.15 kg/m².

HSIMS.pf.mats.V360L.t.name: ASODUR-V360W levelling
steps: Mix component A with component B, 100 : 20 parts by weight.
Mix approx. 3 minutes.
Thicken with the fibre filler ASO-FF for the pinholes: approx. 3 %. (Unevenness up to 2 mm: 1 : 0.5 quartz sand 0.1–0.35 mm.)
Pot life approx. 40 minutes.
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360L.t.sliderBad: Approx. 3 % ASO-FF thickens the resin for pinholes and recesses.
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360L.t.note: Approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm of levelling; sanded with 100 grit and vacuumed after hardening.

HSIMS.pf.mats.V360S.t.name: ASODUR-V360W seal
steps: Mix component A with component B, 100 : 20 parts by weight.
Mix approx. 3 minutes.
Water for the seal? The seal is applied undiluted.
Pot life approx. 40 minutes.
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360S.t.sliderBad: The seal is mixed like the primer but applied undiluted — 0 % water.
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360S.t.note: Rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller, approx. 0.30–0.35 kg/m² per step.

HSIMS.pf.mats.V360A.t.name: ASODUR-V360W with ASO-Antislide
steps: Mix component A with component B, 100 : 20 parts by weight.
Mix approx. 3 minutes.
Stir the glass granulate ASO-Antislide into the premixed seal: 8–10 % by weight (max. 170 g/m²), stirred up during the work.
Pot life approx. 40 minutes.
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360A.t.sliderBad: ASO-Antislide at 8–10 % by weight gives slip class R10 with V360W; the granulate goes into the last step only.
HSIMS.pf.mats.V360A.t.note: Grain 90–150 µm; the granulate must not settle in the bucket.

gate.title: Do the garage floor over a weekend with your own hands
gate.desc: The garage of the 3D sample: shot-blast and grind the slab, read the CM test, prime with ASODUR-V360W diluted 8–10 %, fill the pinholes with ASO-FF, roll the seal criss-cross in two steps and stir ASO-Antislide into the last — each batch mixed 100 : 20 with its 40-minute pot life, each overcoat window of 16–48 hours on the site clock. You lead the crew and decide every dilution.
gate.foot: Twelve phases from the technical data sheets of ASODUR-V360W, ASO-FF, ASO-Antislide and INDUFLEX-PU.

HSIMS.pf.t.eyebrow: Operation briefing · Garage and cellar floor
HSIMS.pf.t.title: The aqueous seal ASODUR-V360W in two days
HSIMS.pf.t.sub: The garage floor dusts under the tyres, drinks the oil drip and is never clean. The slab is dry and sound; the floor must be done over a weekend. The water-emulsified epoxy ASODUR-V360W is primer, levelling compound and seal in one product: diluted as the primer, filled for the pinholes, rolled criss-cross in two steps — satin, pigmented, vapour permeable, walkable after 16 hours.
brief: Shot blasting and edge grinding; CM test ≤ 5 CM-%, dew point
Repairs, crack sealing, vacuuming
Primer: V360W 100 : 20, diluted 8–10 %, rolled criss-cross, approx. 0.15 kg/m²
Levelling: pinholes with approx. 3 % ASO-FF; sanded and vacuumed after hardening
Seal: undiluted, criss-cross, 0.30–0.35 kg/m² per step; ASO-Antislide 8–10 % in the last step
Joints with INDUFLEX-PU; driven on after 7 days

phases.p: Select the shot blaster and stay with the crew: the slab is shot-blasted lane by lane after DIN EN 14879-1, the edges ground with the H-class vacuum on the grinder.
phases.done: Slab prepared: grippy, load-bearing, dust-free.

phases.q: The CM device reads 3.2 CM-% on the slab; the substrate is 2 °C above the dew point at 65 % relative humidity. What now?
opts: Wait for the climate — V360W allows ≤ 5 CM-%, but the substrate must be ≥ 3 °C above the dew point
Start priming at once: 3.2 CM-% is dry enough
Switch to the barrier primer ASODUR-SG3: the slab is too damp
phases.why: V360W takes ≤ 5 CM-%; but substrate and air must be 10–35 °C and at least 3 °C above the dew point, humidity max. 65 %. Heat or ventilate first.
phases.done: Climate checked.

phases.p: Guide the crew: breakouts filled, the crack closed with the cartridge gun, the floor vacuumed dust-free.
phases.done: Repairs done, floor vacuumed.

phases.p: Mix ASODUR-V360W 100 : 20 and dilute it for the primer. Stay with the roller: the primer is rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller onto the dry substrate, approx. 0.15 kg/m², within the pot life of 40 minutes.
phases.done: Primed; the seal follows after min. 16 hours and within 48 hours.

phases.p: The primer hardens: overcoat after min. 16 hours, within 48 hours (beyond it the surface is sanded again).
Mix V360W and thicken it with ASO-FF. Guide the crew: pinholes and small recesses filled, unevenness levelled, sanded with 100 grit and vacuumed after hardening.
phases.done: Pinholes filled, surface sanded and vacuumed.

phases.p: The levelling hardens; the seal follows within the overcoat window of 16–48 hours.
Mix V360W undiluted. Stay with the roller: the seal is rolled criss-cross, approx. 0.30–0.35 kg/m² — pigmented, satin, vapour permeable.
phases.done: First step of the seal rolled; walkable after approx. 16 hours.

phases.p: The second step after min. 16 hours and within 48 hours.

Mix V360W and stir ASO-Antislide into it, 8–10 % by weight. Guide the crew: the last step rolled criss-cross (R10), the glass granulate stirred up during the work; then the field and wall joints filled with INDUFLEX-PU.
phases.done: Floor finished: R10, joints elastic.

phases.p: Walkable after approx. 16 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days; the garage is driven on after 7 days — tyres not turned on the spot in the first weeks.
The car drives in: oil, tyre softeners, petrol and dilute acids no longer mark the floor.
phases.done: The floor in service.

HSIMS.pf.t.res_title: The garage floor is sealed. Satin, R10, easy to clean.
HSIMS.pf.t.res_sub: Clean the tools with water at once. Observe the technical data sheets of ASODUR-V360W, ASO-FF, ASO-Antislide and INDUFLEX-PU and the safety data sheets.

HSIMS.ca.mats.MIXP.t.name: Concrete with BETOCRETE-CL170-P (plant)
steps: Dose the liquid admixture with the mixing water via the dosing system of the plant and mix for more than 45 seconds; the quantity is deducted from the mixing water.
The concrete is ready for the truck.
HSIMS.ca.mats.MIXP.t.note: Where the truck is dosed on site: BETOCRETE-CP360-WP as 3 kg water-soluble bags, approx. 1 minute of mixing per m³ of drum content, at least 5 minutes.

gate.title: Cast the watertight basement and dose it yourself
gate.desc: The basement of the 3D sample: the crystalline waterstop in the kicker, the admixture dosed at the plant — you decide the dosing level from the w/c ratio and the cement content of the recipe, as the data sheet asks — the concrete placed and compacted, cured, backfilled, and the crack that heals when the water arrives. The decisions of the data sheet, taken by you, without a single cubic metre wasted.
gate.foot: Nine phases from the technical data sheets of BETOCRETE-CL170-P, BETOCRETE-CP360-WP and the AQUAFIN-CJ joint accessories.

HSIMS.ca.t.eyebrow: Operation briefing · Base slab and walls below ground
HSIMS.ca.t.title: Watertight concrete with BETOCRETE
HSIMS.ca.t.sub: A basement stands in the ground: soil moisture and ground water press against the slab and the walls, the construction joint at the kicker is the weak point, and the cracks that every slab and wall develop would carry the water inside. Recipe: CEM II, 320 kg/m³ cement, w/c 0.50, dosed with BETOCRETE-CL170-P at the plant.
brief: The crystalline waterstop AQUAFIN-CJ5 in the kicker, AQUAFIN-CJ6 on working joints, AQUAFIN-CJ1 as reserve
Dosing level from the w/c ratio: 1.75 / 1.85 / 2.00 % of the cement weight, never above 2.25 %
Mixed in the plant for more than 45 seconds
Placed in layers, fully compacted, no water added on site
Cured to the standards; crystals on the surface are not a defect
Cracks up to 0.4 mm heal when the water arrives

phases.p: Select the joint accessories and hold the pointer on the kicker: the crystalline waterstop AQUAFIN-CJ5 is fixed to the reinforcement before the wall is poured, the swelling tape AQUAFIN-CJ6 on the working joints, the injection hose AQUAFIN-CJ1 as reserve.
phases.done: Joints detailed with the system accessories.

phases.q: The recipe: 320 kg/m³ CEM II, w/c 0.50. The dosing level of BETOCRETE-CL170-P according to the data sheet?
phases.why: Liquid BETOCRETE: 1.75 % below w/c 0.4, 1.85 % at w/c > 0.4–0.5, 2.00 % at w/c > 0.5–0.55 — never above 2.25 %. Preliminary tests always.
phases.done: Dosing level chosen.

phases.label: BETOCRETE-CL170-P
phases.q: Set the quantity of BETOCRETE-CL170-P per m³ of concrete for 320 kg/m³ of cement at 1.85 %.
phases.why: 320 kg × 1.85 % = 5.92 kg per m³; the quantity is deducted from the mixing water.
phases.done: Dosed.

phases.p: The plant mixes for more than 45 seconds. Then select the poker vibrator and hold the pointer on the pour: the concrete is placed in layers and fully compacted — honeycombs and voids are not sealed by crystals.
phases.done: Concrete placed and fully compacted, without cold joints.

phases.q: The second truck arrives stiff after a long drive. The foreman asks for 10 l of water per m³ in the drum.
opts: No — no water on site: it raises the w/c ratio beyond the recipe. Consistency is adjusted with the superplasticiser of the recipe.
Yes — 10 l/m³ is harmless, the admixture seals the pores anyway
Yes, but add BETOCRETE as well to compensate
phases.why: No additional water on site: it raises the w/c ratio beyond the recipe; the crystalline effect works in a dense concrete.
phases.done: Recipe kept.

phases.p: Select the curing sheet and stay on the slab: the surfaces are protected against drying out, wind, sun and frost and kept damp to the valid standards. Crystals on the surface are not a defect.
phases.done: Curing to the standards.

phases.p: The formwork is struck when the strength allows; the concrete hardens — the crystalline effect needs the dense concrete the curing produces.
The working space is backfilled; the ground water rises against the slab and the walls. The crystals close the pores.
phases.done: In the ground, under water pressure.

phases.p: A crack of up to 0.4 mm opens and the water reaches it: crystals grow in the crack until it is sealed. Wider or moving cracks are injected (AQUAFIN-P1, P4, IH).
phases.done: Crack healed by crystal growth.

T.how.label: Mechanism
T.how.title: How crack injection with {P4r} works
T.how.sub: {P4} is grouted through injection packers into the crack. The low-viscosity resin fills the crack, cures to soft elastic and adheres to the crack flanks.
how.steps: Drill the injection holes. Clear any drilling debris in the drilled holes using oil-free compressed air.
Insert one injection packer into each drilled hole.
Seal the inserted packers and the zone of the {defect} on the surface approx. 15 cm wide with {EKF}. Allow the crack insulation to cure.
Grout in the thoroughly mixed {P4} using a grouting device. Pot life approx. 30 minutes.
After the resin has cured, remove the injection packers and plug the boreholes flush with the surface using {M30}.

T.how.modelBdesc: Where the {defect} conducts water, an initial injection of {P1} is necessary to stop the ingress of water. {P4} follows as the crack-bridging seal.

T.m3d.microNoteGlued: Micro scale: schematic close-up of a sectioned sample, not to scale. Resin colour as supplied: AQUAFIN-P4 honey yellow.
calloutsMicroGlued: A sectioned sample of hardened cement paste: globular hydration products, air pores, plate-shaped and needle-shaped crystals, two broken aggregate grains. The crack runs through it with fine branches. Nothing is drilled: the component stays untouched.
The packers are bonded over the crack on the surface with {EKF}. The resin enters the crack from there at low pressure and runs along it into the depth of the component.

The honey yellow resin has a low viscosity (approx. 125 mPa·s at 20 °C), so it also reaches the fine branches. It adheres to the flanks and cures to soft elastic: the permanent, crack-bridging seal. Adhesive packers need a dry or damp crack that does not conduct water.
calloutsMicro: A sectioned sample of hardened cement paste: globular hydration products, air pores, plate-shaped and needle-shaped crystals, two broken aggregate grains. The {defect} runs through it with fine branches. The section follows the axis of the drilled hole, so the hole shows as a half pipe that meets the {defect} at 45°.

Only where the {defect} conducts water. The dark brown resin runs along the hole into the {defect}, reacts with the water and foams to up to 40 times its volume. The watertight, visco-plastic foam stops the ingress of water. It is a temporary seal.

The honey yellow resin has a low viscosity (approx. 125 mPa·s at 20 °C), so it also reaches the fine branches that the foam does not fill. It adheres to the flanks and cures to soft elastic: the permanent, crack-bridging seal. Afterwards the packer is removed and the hole plugged with {M30}.

SCN.wall.name: Cracks in walls
SCN.wall.problem: A crack runs through the full thickness of a reinforced concrete wall. Moisture, or water, reaches the accessible side.
SCN.wall.solution: Holes are drilled every 20 cm on alternating sides of the crack, at 45°, so that every hole crosses the crack inside the wall. {EKF} seals the crack on the surface; {P4} is grouted in from the lowest packer upwards.

SCN.hjoint.name: Construction joint in a wall
SCN.hjoint.problem: A horizontal joint between two pours, or a horizontal crack, lets water through along its whole length.
SCN.hjoint.solution: Drill packers are set alternately above and below the joint; every hole crosses the joint at 45°. The joint is sealed on the surface with {EKF} and grouted packer by packer with {P4}.

caps.intro: Reinforced concrete wall with a horizontal construction joint
caps.leak: Moisture comes through along the joint, the surface below it gets damp

SCN.wfjoint.name: Wall–floor joint
SCN.wfjoint.problem: The joint between the floor slab and the wall cast onto it is the classic leak of a basement: ground water follows the joint to the inside.
SCN.wfjoint.solution: Holes are drilled from the wall face at 45° downwards, so that they cross the joint under the wall. Joint and packers are sealed with {EKF}; {P4} spreads along the joint from packer to packer. In new construction the injection hose {CJ1} is cast into this joint and injected with {P1} or {P4}.

caps.intro: Wall cast onto the floor slab: the construction joint at its foot
caps.leak: Ground water follows the joint to the inside

SCN.honeycomb.name: Honeycombing
SCN.honeycomb.note: Schematic, not to scale. Holes at 45° into the gravel pocket; number of holes, hole diameter and packer type according to the project specification.
SCN.honeycomb.problem: Poorly compacted concrete at the foot of a wall: coarse aggregate with too little cement paste between the grains. The pocket is permeable over its whole depth.
SCN.honeycomb.solution: Holes are drilled at 45° into the pocket, its surface is sealed with {EKF}, and the low-viscosity {P4} is grouted in until the space between the grains is filled. Where water flows, {P1} stops it first.

caps.intro: Gravel pocket at the foot of the wall
caps.leak: Water passes through the pocket, the surface gets damp
caps.inject: Grout in AQUAFIN-P4: the resin fills the space between the grains

0: Drill into the pocket, clear the holes
Drill the injection holes at 45° into the gravel pocket. Clear any drilling debris using oil-free compressed air.

SCN.pipe.name: Pipe penetrations
SCN.pipe.problem: The ring joint between a pipe or shaft and the concrete cast around it leaks: the two materials shrink and move differently.
SCN.pipe.solution: Holes are set around the pipe and drilled at 45° towards the joint. The ring joint is sealed on the surface with {EKF} and grouted packer by packer around the pipe. {P4} adheres to both flanks and cures to soft elastic.

caps.intro: Pipe passing through a reinforced concrete slab
caps.leak: Water rises through the ring joint around the pipe

SCN.slab.name: Cracks in floor slabs
SCN.slab.problem: A crack through a floor slab with ground water below it, for example under a station building or in a basement floor.
SCN.slab.solution: The crack is injected from the top: holes at 45° on alternating sides, surface seal with {EKF}, then {P4}. If water wells up through the crack, {P1} stops it first.

caps.intro: Reinforced concrete floor slab with a continuous crack
caps.leak: Ground water rises through the crack, the surface gets damp

SCN.dam.name: Water-retaining structures
SCN.dam.problem: Basins, tanks, retaining walls and dams with water standing against one side. The crack conducts water under pressure.
SCN.dam.solution: The work is done from the dry side. {P1} is injected first: it reacts with the water, foams and stops the ingress. {P4} follows as the elastic, crack-bridging seal.

caps.intro: Basin wall with water standing behind it
caps.leak: Water is pressed through the crack

SCN.sewer.name: Sewers
SCN.sewer.problem: Ground water infiltrates through cracks and joints of the sewer wall, or sewage escapes through them.
SCN.sewer.solution: Injection from inside the sewer: holes at 45° on alternating sides of the crack. {P1} stops the inflow, {P4} follows for the permanent, elastic waterproofing of the crack.

caps.intro: Sewer wall with a longitudinal crack
caps.leak: Ground water infiltrates through the crack

SCN.manhole.name: Manhole shafts
SCN.manhole.problem: Inspection chambers and manhole shafts built in lifts or from rings: ground water enters through the joints between the lifts or rings and round the pipe connections; the chamber runs full at high water.
SCN.manhole.solution: Injection from inside the shaft, the flow diverted first: holes at 45° alternately above and below the joint so that each hole crosses it inside the wall. {P1} stops the inflow, {P4} follows as the permanent, elastic seal of the joint.

caps.intro: Manhole shaft cast in lifts: the construction joint between two lifts
caps.leak: Ground water enters along the joint between the lifts

SCN.cutcover.name: Cut-and-cover tunnels
SCN.cutcover.problem: A rectangular tunnel cast in an open excavation: the construction joints between base slab and walls and between walls and roof, and the joints between the pours along the tunnel, are where the ground water comes in.
SCN.cutcover.solution: From inside the tunnel, in a lane closure: holes drilled from the wall face at 45° downwards so that they cross the wall–base joint under the wall. {P1} stops the water, the joint and the packers are sealed with {EKF}, and {P4} spreads along the joint from packer to packer.

caps.intro: Cut-and-cover tunnel: the construction joint at the foot of the side wall
caps.leak: Ground water follows the joint into the tunnel

SCN.tbm.name: TBM tunnels, segmental lining
SCN.tbm.problem: A tunnel bored by a tunnel boring machine and lined with precast concrete segments: water finds the ring joints and the longitudinal joints where a gasket is damaged or a segment is offset, and the bolt pockets and grout holes.
SCN.tbm.solution: From inside the tunnel: the bolt pockets and the gasket groove are located first, then holes are drilled at 45° to the joint between them so that each hole meets the joint plane inside the segment. {P1} stops the inflow, {P4} seals the joint elastically. The gasket itself stays untouched.

caps.intro: Segmental lining of a TBM tunnel: the longitudinal joint between two segments of a ring
caps.leak: Ground water enters through the longitudinal joint and the bolt pockets

SCN.shield.name: Shield tunnels
SCN.shield.problem: A metro tunnel driven by a shield in soft, water-bearing ground: the ground water stands high against the segmental lining and enters at ring joints and longitudinal joints where the gasket no longer seals, along cracks in the segments and at the grout holes.
SCN.shield.solution: From the walkway, outside operating hours: holes at 45° to the joint on alternating sides, clear of the bolts and the gasket groove. {P1} first, until the inflow stops, then {P4} for the permanent elastic seal. Pressures kept low: the resin must fill the joint, not lift the lining.

caps.intro: Shield tunnel in soft ground: the segmental lining with its ring joint
caps.leak: Ground water under pressure enters through the ring joint

SCN.immersed.name: Immersed tube tunnels
SCN.immersed.problem: Tunnel elements cast in a dry dock, floated out and sunk into a dredged trench. The immersion joint is sealed by the Gina gasket outside and the Omega seal inside; where an element wall has cracked, or the joint zone leaks past the concrete, water enters under the head of the sea or river above.
SCN.immersed.solution: From inside the tunnel: cracks in the element and the concrete joint zone are injected at 45° on alternating sides; the rubber seals are never drilled. {P1} stops the water, {P4} gives the elastic, watertight seal of the crack.

caps.intro: Immersed tube tunnel: the element joint with its Omega seal, a crack beside it
caps.leak: Water under the head above enters through the crack

SCN.adhesive.name: Adhesive packers
SCN.adhesive.note: Schematic, crack width exaggerated. Packer spacing and injection pressure according to the project specification.
SCN.adhesive.problem: Thin components, dense reinforcement or prestressing steel do not allow drilling. The crack is dry or damp.
SCN.adhesive.solution: Adhesive packers are bonded over the crack with {EKF}, the crack between them is sealed, and the resin is grouted in at low pressure through the packers. {P4} gives the elastic, watertight seal; for a force-locking bond of dry cracks in concrete: {IH} (not for statically relevant areas).

caps.intro: Crack in a component that must not be drilled
caps.drill: Clean the crack zone with oil-free compressed air
caps.air: Clean the crack zone with oil-free compressed air
caps.packer: Bond the adhesive packers over the crack
caps.seal: Seal the crack between the packers with ASODUR-EKF
caps.done: Crack sealed without a single drilled hole

0: Remove loose parts, dust and laitance along the crack and blow the zone off with oil-free compressed air. Nothing is drilled.
1: Bond the packers centrally over the crack with {EKF}. The crack must stay open under each packer.
2: Seal the crack between the packers
Seal the crack on the surface between and around the packers with {EKF}. Allow the crack insulation to cure.
4: After the resin has cured, remove the adhesive packers. The surface seal can be removed as necessary for visual reasons.

SCN.adhesive.modelA: Adhesive packers need a dry or damp crack that does not conduct water: the adhesive must bond to the surface.

SCN_T.label: Scenarios
SCN_T.title: Where it leaks, and how it is sealed
SCN_T.sub: Select the situation on site. The 3D mechanism, the five steps and the cross-section follow your choice.
SCN_T.note: Drilling pattern according to the SCHOMBURG system “Crack repair (wall surfaces)”: holes at 20 cm intervals, offset, at an angle of 45° to the crack. What is specific to a scenario follows general injection practice; hole diameter, packer type and spacing according to the project specification.

STEP_P1.title: Stop the water with AQUAFIN-P1
STEP_P1.short: Where water flows: AQUAFIN-P1 first. It foams on contact with water and stops the ingress.
STEP_P1.overview: Where the {defect} conducts water, an initial injection of {P1} is necessary to stop the ingress of water. {P1} reacts with water to a watertight, visco-plastic foam.
points: {P1}: foaming polyurethane injection resin for the temporary sealing of water-conducting cracks
foams to up to 40 times its volume on contact with water
remove excess foam flush with the surface once it has reacted
an additional injection of {P4} is then necessary: it gives the permanent, elastic, crack-bridging seal
STEP_P1.note: Sequence on this page: once the water has stopped, the surface is sealed with {EKF}, then {P4} is injected.
STEP_P1.src: Sources: SCHOMBURG technical data sheet AQUAFIN-P4, 20/05/2026; product page AQUAFIN-P1; system “Crack repair (wall surfaces)”.

extra: Holes every 20 cm, offset to alternate sides of the crack, at an angle of 45°: each hole crosses the crack inside the wall (SCHOMBURG system “Crack repair (wall surfaces)”).
Locate the reinforcement first and drill between the bars.
Vertical cracks: start at the lowest packer and work upwards.
Change to the next packer when resin emerges there.
Packers alternately above and below the joint; every hole meets the joint at 45° inside the wall.
Locate the reinforcement first and drill between the bars.
Work along the joint packer by packer, starting at one end.
Resin emerging at the next packer shows that the section between the two is filled.
Drill from the wall face at 45° downwards, so that the hole meets the joint under the wall.
Keep clear of the starter bars that cross the joint.
Seal the joint in the corner between wall and floor with {EKF}, together with the packers.
The resin spreads along the joint: inject until it emerges at the neighbouring packer.
New construction: the injection hose {CJ1} is cast into this joint and injected with {P1} or {P4}.
Drill at 45° into the gravel pocket; distribute the holes over its whole area.
Sound the surface first: the pocket is often larger than the visible defect.
Close the open surface of the pocket with {EKF}; otherwise the low-viscosity resin runs out.
Inject from the lowest packer upwards until the space between the grains is filled.
Consumption follows the volume of voids: approx. 1.1 kg per litre (technical data sheet).
Set the holes around the pipe and drill at 45° towards the ring joint.
Do not drill into the pipe or its sleeve.
Seal the ring joint all around the pipe with {EKF}.
Work around the pipe packer by packer until the resin emerges at the next packer.
{P4} adheres to both flanks and cures to soft elastic.
Drill from the top, at 45°, on alternating sides of the crack.
Check for services and reinforcement in the slab before drilling.
Work along the crack from one end; change packer when resin emerges at the next one.
All work is done from the dry side.
Holes at 45° on alternating sides: they cross the crack inside the wall.
Water under pressure: inject {P1} until the water stops at the surface.
{P4} follows as the permanent, elastic, crack-bridging seal.
Injection from inside the sewer; keep the flow away from the working zone.
Holes at 45° on alternating sides of the crack.
Infiltrating ground water: {P1} first, until the inflow stops.
{P4} follows for the permanent, elastic waterproofing of the crack.
Divert the flow and pump the chamber down before work starts; ventilate and monitor the atmosphere.
Holes at 45° alternately above and below the joint between the lifts, so that each crosses the joint inside the wall.
Infiltrating ground water: {P1} first, until the inflow stops.
{P4} follows along the joint packer by packer for the permanent, elastic seal.
Work from inside the tunnel in a lane closure; keep the walkway clear.
Holes drilled from the wall face at 45° downwards, so that they cross the wall–base joint under the wall.
Ground water running along the joint: {P1} first, until the joint is dry at the surface.
{P4} spreads along the joint from packer to packer; resin at the next packer shows the section is filled.
Locate the bolt pockets and the gasket groove first; drill between them, never into the gasket or a bolt.
Holes at 45° to the joint on alternating sides, ending at the joint plane inside the segment.
Water through the ring joint: {P1} first, until the inflow stops.
{P4} seals the joint elastically; low pressure, so that the resin fills the joint without lifting the segment.
Outside operating hours, from the walkway; the track and the cables protected.
Holes at 45° to the joint on alternating sides, clear of the bolts and the gasket groove.
High ground water: {P1} first, until the inflow at the joint stops.
{P4} follows for the permanent, elastic seal of the joint; pressures kept low.
The Gina gasket and the Omega seal are never drilled: the holes go into the concrete of the element beside the joint.
Holes at 45° on alternating sides of the crack, so that each crosses it inside the wall.
Water under the head above: {P1} first, until the inflow stops.
{P4} follows as the elastic, watertight seal of the crack.

points: no drilling: thin components, dense reinforcement or prestressing steel stay untouched
remove loose parts, dust and laitance along the crack
use oil-free compressed air only
adhesive packers bonded centrally over the crack with {EKF}
the crack must stay open under each packer
packer spacing according to the project specification
seal the crack between and around the packers with {EKF}
allow the crack insulation to cure before grouting

extra: Low pressure: the bond of the adhesive packers limits the injection pressure.
For a force-locking bond of dry cracks in concrete: {IH} — not for statically relevant areas.

points: final curing at 20 °C: approx. 5 hours
the surface seal can be removed as necessary for visual reasons

1: Adhesive packers are bonded over the crack with {EKF}; nothing is drilled. In X-ray view the reinforcement stays untouched. Stage “Surface sealed” shows the seal between the packers.
2: Stage “Sealed”: the crack is filled with the resin and the adhesive packers are removed. The surface dries.

SIMT.brief_eyebrow: Operation briefing · Basement wall, axis C
SIMT.brief_sub: A crack runs through the full height of the reinforced concrete wall; the surface is damp, the crack is not water-conducting. AQUAFIN-P4 can be used on dry and damp substrates. Run the complete sequence from the technical data sheet and finish the injection within the pot life of approx. 30 minutes.
brief: Survey the crack and mark five injection points
Drill the injection holes
Clear the holes with oil-free compressed air
Insert the injection packers
Seal packers and crack zone approx. 15 cm wide with ASODUR-EKF
Mix 1 : 1 by volume and grout in AQUAFIN-P4
Remove the packers and plug the boreholes with ASOCRET-M30
keys: drill, blow out, seal, grout, plug

phases.p: Select the marker and mark the five injection points along the crack.
Select the drill. Hold on each mark until the hole reaches its depth. The view into the wall shows the hole passing between the reinforcing bars.
Select the compressed air. Hold on each hole to clear the drilling debris. Oil-free air only.
Select the packer and insert one injection packer into each hole.
Select ASODUR-EKF. Seal packers and crack zone approx. 15 cm wide, working from the bottom upwards.
Mix the resin, then select the injection pump. Grout in from the lowest packer upwards.
Select the packer tool and remove the packers. Then plug each borehole flush with ASOCRET-M30.

done: Surface sealed. The crack insulation cures.
Boreholes plugged flush with the surface.
SIMT.lapse2: The resin cures. Final curing at 20 °C: approx. 5 hours …
mix: Add the hardener to the resin. The hardener must run completely out of the container.
Mix thoroughly, approx. 3 minutes at approx. 300 rpm.
Decant the mass into a clean bucket and stir carefully again.
SIMT.mix_go: The pot life runs: approx. 30 minutes.
SIMT.potOut: Pot life exceeded. Mix a fresh batch.
SIMT.res_title: Crack sealed. The resin cures to soft elastic.
SIMT.res_sub: Clean the tools immediately with suitable solvent; the cleaning agent must have a flash point above +21 °C. Observe applicable safety data sheet!
SIMT.no3d: The simulator needs WebGL and an internet connection to load the 3D library.

steel: {HSF} on the de-rusted steel (SA 2.5): two brush coats, the second after approx. 2 hours. The repair mortar follows approx. 6 hours after the second coat.
Bond coat and mortar, wet in wet
{HSF} is brushed into the matt damp substrate, down to the pores. {BIS540} is applied while the bond coat is still wet, compacted and levelled flush.
Up to 20 mm per application step, greater thicknesses in several layers. {BIS16} closes the surface with 1–6 mm. Keep the mortar damp for at least 3–5 days.
breakout: Loose parts are removed and the substrate is blasted until it is firm, grippy, load-bearing and pore open; the edges are cut square, not feathered.
Bond coat and mortar, wet in wet
{HSF} is brushed into the matt damp substrate, down to the pores. {BIS540} follows while the bond coat is still wet, in steps of up to 20 mm.
{BIS16} closes the surface with 1–6 mm after 24 hours at the earliest. Keep the mortar damp for at least 3–5 days.
surface: On the matt damp substrate {BIS16} is first applied as a scratch coat that fills pores and blowholes, then in the layer thickness wanted.
1–6 mm, struck off within the pot life
Up to 6 mm per application step. Striking off with float or trowel within approx. 60 minutes; felt or sponge finish after a corresponding waiting time.
Protect from rapid drying: keep damp for at least 3–5 days; a cementitious waterproofing slurry can follow after approx. 24 hours.
water: Running water is stopped with FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T; the crack is chased to approx. 20 × 25 mm, U-shaped, and the substrate is roughened and cleaned with pressure water.
The flanks are screened with {IC}; {IM} follows wet in wet, flush in the chase and as a coved fillet of approx. 4 cm at the wall–floor joint.
After 1–3 hours {IM} is reworked with {IC}. The crystals grow into the capillaries; keep damp for at least 3 days.

for levelling pool tank walls, as well as modelling pool edges in swimming pools
for concrete repair
for breakout depths ca. 1–6 mm
for walls, ceilings, floors
adv: frost proof and resistant to thaw
data: Max. layer thickness per application step
class R2; adhesion ≥ 0.8 N/mm²; capillary water absorption ≤ 0.5 kg·m⁻²·h⁻⁰·⁵; resistance to carbonation passed
cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 12 months

IM.sub: Crystalline repair mortar for concrete, waterproofing
IM.role: The waterproofing repair mortar. It fills chased cracks and holes and forms coved fillets, together with the crystalline slurry {IC}.
areas: for water tight filling of open cracks and holes
as coving mortar
suitable for negative water pressure
adv: can also be used on damp substrate
feat: increased active crack healing in concrete
data: Max. layer thickness per application step
cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 18 months

HSF.sub: Flexible contact / bonding slurry and corrosion protection
HSF.role: Two tasks in the system: corrosion protection on the de-rusted reinforcement, and the bond coat under the repair mortar.
areas: as a cementitious bond coat on concrete substrates and repair mortars
as corrosive protection for exposed and abraded reinforcement bars
as a bond coat in concrete restoration
as a contact and bonding slurry for laying tiles and boards with the thick-bed method
as a bond coat for cement bonded screeds
for walls, ceilings, floors; for interior and exterior use
adv: frost proof and resistant to thaw
data: Water addition, contact and bonding slurry
approx. 3 minutes, mix again after an activation time of 5 minutes
Max. layer thickness per application step
approx. 1–2 kg/m²; as bond coat approx. 1.5 kg/m² per mm; as corrosion protection approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm
cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 12 months

assess.title: Have the structure assessed
assess.short: An expert or structural engineer checks the current state before any restoration measure.
assess.overview: Before any concrete restoration measures, the current state must generally be checked by an expert and/or structural engineer. The test report must be made available to the processor before starting the restoration measures.
points: cause and extent of the damage: carbonation, chlorides, cover, cross-section of the reinforcement
the test report decides the repair principle and the extent of the breakout
protect surfaces that are not to be treated

prep.title: Break out and prepare the substrate
prep.short: Remove everything loose; blast the substrate until it is firm, grippy, load-bearing and pore open.
prep.overview: If no previous concrete restoration work has been carried out, a substrate preparation is required, e.g. granulate or shot blasting or ultra-high pressure water jetting (500–2000 bar).
points: requirement for the substrate: firm, grippy, load-bearing, pore open, free of adhesion inhibiting substances
dense and smooth mineral substrates must be roughened (sand, high-pressure water or shot blasting)
suitable substrates: concrete, cement-based screed (CT)

derust.title: De-rust the reinforcement
derust.short: Exposed steel is de-rusted completely, to cleanliness level SA 2.5, free of dust and grease.
derust.overview: The exposed reinforcing steels must be totally de-rusted and must be clear of dust and grease up to the standard cleanliness level SA 2.5 by suitable measures.
points: blast all around the bar, also behind it
exposed reinforcing steels must be pretreated with the corrosion protection {HSF}

protect.title: Coat the reinforcement twice with ASOCRET-HS-FLEX
protect.short: Two brush coats, fully covering; the second after approx. 2 hours.
protect.overview: {HSF} is applied to the reinforcing steel with a brush in two application steps, ensuring full covering.
points: water addition for corrosion protection: approx. 5.5–5.75 l per 25 kg
mixing time ca. 3 minutes; mix again after an activation time of 5 minutes
the second coat is applied after approx. 2 hours waiting time, when the first coat is brushable
consumption approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm layer thickness; approx. 1 mm per application step
pot life approx. 60 minutes at 5–30 °C
protect.warning: The repair mortar {BIS540} can be applied approx. 6 hours after the second coat has hardened.

wet.title: Pre-wet the substrate
wet.short: Dampen 24 hours and 2 hours before; matt damp at the time of application.
wet.overview: Dampen the pre-treated mineral substrate sufficiently 24 hours and 2 hours before application. Pre-moisten the dry mineral substrate so that it is matt damp at the time of application.
points: matt damp: no shiny film of water, no puddles
the bond coat and the mortar follow directly

bond.title: Brush in the bond coat ASOCRET-HS-FLEX
bond.short: One coat with a hard brush, down to the pores, fully covering.
bond.overview: {HSF} is brushed into the prepared substrate with a hard broom in a single coat, down to the pores and such that it is full covering.
points: water addition for the bond coat: approx. 6.75–7.0 l per 25 kg
mixing time ca. 3 minutes; mix again after an activation time of 5 minutes
consumption approx. 1.5 kg/m² per mm layer thickness
pot life approx. 60 minutes
bond.warning: In case of interruptions or after hardening, the bond coat must set completely. Repeat the application including the bond coat after an appropriate waiting time.

fill.title: Re-profile with ASOCRET-BIS-5/40, wet in wet
fill.short: Into the fresh bond coat, compacted and levelled flush; up to 20 mm per step.
fill.overview: The repair mortar {BIS540} is applied while the bond coat is still wet, in the required layer thickness. Then the mortar is compacted and levelled flush with the surface.
points: put approx. 2.8–3.0 l of water into a clean mixing bucket and mix with 25 kg of powder to a homogeneous, lump-free mass
pre-mix for approx. 3 minutes
add the remaining water (in total approx. 3.5–3.75 l) and mix sufficiently; use a forced paddle mixer for larger quantities
apply into the fresh bond coat, compact, level flush with the surface
with large surface applications the layer thickness can be up to max. 20 mm in one application step
for greater layer thicknesses a multiple layer application is recommended
fill.warning: Do not add water or new mortar to mortar that has already set in order to make it workable again (risk of inadequate strength development).
fill.note: Pot life approx. 60 minutes. Consumption approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm. Can be trowelled and sprayed; machine application: Technical Information No. 43.

fine.title: Smooth with ASOCRET-BIS-1/6
fine.short: Scratch coat first, then the layer, 1–6 mm; strike off within the pot life.
fine.overview: On the prepared substrate, {BIS16} is applied beforehand with a scratch coat and then in the desired layer thickness. Striking off is done with a suitable tool (float, trowel) within the pot life.
points: water addition: 5–5.25 l per 25 kg; mixing time ca. 3 minutes; after a settling period of ca. 5 minutes homogenise again
up to 6 mm per application step
the surface can be treated with a felt or sponge board after a corresponding waiting time
consumption approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm; pot life approx. 60 minutes
on {BIS540}: overcoat after 24 hours at the earliest

cure.title: Cure the mortar
cure.short: Protect from rapid drying; keep damp for at least 3–5 days.
cure.overview: After application, the mortar surfaces must generally be protected from rapid drying using suitable measures: keep the surfaces damp for at least 3–5 days using water mist nozzles, wet jute sheets or by covering with film.
points: the film must be attached to the surfaces in such a way that an air exchange is ruled out
direct sunlight, draughts, high temperature fluctuations and low humidity need more attention
if a cementitious waterproofing slurry follows, it can be applied as an alternative curing method after approx. 24 hours
foot traffic after approx. 24 hours

clean.title: Clean tools, store material
clean.short: Rinse tools with water immediately. Store cool and dry.
clean.overview: Rinse tools with water immediately after use.
points: storage: cool, dry, protected from sunlight
min. 12 months in the original container ({IM}: min. 18 months)
promptly use opened containers

wprep.title: Prepare the substrate
wprep.short: Roughen dense surfaces; high-pressure water jetting; finish by cleaning with pressure water.
wprep.overview: A load-bearing substrate is a precondition for a long-lasting bond. Less adhesive and bond-damaging substances must be completely removed.
points: dense and smooth substrates must be roughened (sand, high-pressure water or shot blasting)
high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar) and jets with fixed blasting agents are suitable
the last application step must be cleaning with pressure water jetting
requirement: firm, load-bearing, pore open, clean, absorbent
pre-moisten to matt damp; the formation of puddles must be avoided

plug.title: Stop the water ingress
plug.short: Running water is stopped first, with the plugging mortar FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T.
plug.overview: Water ingress must be stopped in advance with FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T.
points: system “Retrospective concrete waterproofing”: mix the plugging mortar with approx. 25 % water to a pliable consistency, pot life approx. 3 minutes
press the plug into the leaking area and hold until it has hardened, then trowel the surface
plug.note: Cracks that conduct water over their length are injected: see the guide “Crack sealing / injection resins”.

chase.title: Chase the crack open
chase.short: Approx. 20 mm wide and approx. 25 mm deep, U-shaped.
chase.overview: Structural cracks are to be prised open up to a width of approx. 20 mm and a depth of approx. 25 mm.
points: remove loose debris
U-shaped, not V-shaped: the mortar needs flanks to hold on to
consumption for this cross-section: approx. 1.3 kg {IM} per metre

slurry.title: Screen the flanks with AQUAFIN-IC
slurry.short: The crystalline slurry goes on first; the mortar follows wet in wet.
slurry.overview: Screen the edges with {IC}. For coves: screen the substrate with {IC} and then apply {IM} wet in wet.
points: dampen the surface beforehand
{IC}: crystalline waterproofing slurry, penetrates the concrete via the capillaries

im.title: Fill with ASOCRET-IM, form the cove
im.short: Flush into the chased crack; coved fillet approx. 4 cm high, rounded.
im.overview: Seal wet in wet with {IM} flush with the surface. For the cove, apply {IM} wet in wet into the fresh {IC} with an edge height of approx. 4 cm in a rounded form.
points: water addition: 3.75–4.25 l per 25 kg, mix to a homogeneous, lump-free mass
up to 10 mm per application step
pot life approx. 30 minutes at 5–30 °C
consumption approx. 1.7 kg/m² per mm; chased crack or coved fillet approx. 1.3 kg/m
im.warning: Do not use on frozen substrates. {IM} cannot be used as an additive to concrete or plaster.

ic.title: Rework with AQUAFIN-IC
ic.short: After approx. 1–3 hours the mortar is overcoated with the crystalline slurry.
ic.overview: After approx. 1–3 hours, rework {IM} with {IC}. If this is not possible during this period, the surface should be roughened again after totally hardening and then coated with {IC}.
points: system “Retrospective concrete waterproofing”: two coats of {IC}, the second while the first is still tacky

wcure.title: Protect and keep damp
wcure.short: Protect against rapid water removal; keep damp for at least 3 days.
wcure.overview: {IM} must be protected against rapid water removal using suitable protective measures.
points: system “Retrospective concrete waterproofing”: protect from weathering, keep damp for a minimum of 3 days, first dampening after approx. 1 day
the reaction with the free lime in the concrete can result in slight efflorescence: not a defect, it can be brushed off
different colouring depends on the different moisture content in the concrete

steel.name: Spalling over corroding reinforcement
steel.problem: The cover has carbonated or taken up chlorides, the bar rusts, the rust needs more room than the steel and blows the cover off. Rust stains, cracks along the bar, exposed reinforcement.
steel.solution: The full system: break out to sound concrete, de-rust the bar to SA 2.5, two coats of {HSF} as corrosion protection, {HSF} as bond coat, {BIS540} wet in wet, {BIS16} as the fine finish.

breakout.name: Breakouts, honeycombs, damaged edges
breakout.problem: Mechanical damage, poorly compacted zones or broken edges, 5–40 mm deep. The reinforcement is still covered.
breakout.solution: Prepare the substrate, pre-wet, brush in the bond coat {HSF} and re-profile wet in wet with the non-slump repair mortar {BIS540}; {BIS16} closes the surface.

surface.name: Blowholes, rough surfaces, levelling 1–6 mm
surface.problem: Pores, blowholes and unevenness up to 6 mm, on walls, ceilings and floors; pool tank walls that have to be levelled before waterproofing.
surface.solution: {BIS16}: a scratch coat into the matt damp substrate, then the layer of 1–6 mm, struck off within the pot life and finished with a felt or sponge board.

water.name: Water-bearing cracks, holes and coves
water.problem: Water comes through cracks, tie holes or the wall–floor joint of a concrete structure, also against negative water pressure.
water.solution: Stop running water with FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T, chase the crack to 20 × 25 mm, screen with the crystalline slurry {IC} and fill wet in wet with {IM}; coved fillet of approx. 4 cm at the wall–floor joint; overcoat with {IC} after 1–3 hours.

corr: on the de-rusted reinforcement, two brush coats
second coat after approx. 2 h; mortar approx. 6 h after the second coat
bond: brushed into the matt damp substrate, one coat, down to the pores
fill: 5–40 mm, up to 20 mm per step
fine: closes the surface, felt or sponge finish
scratch: the same mortar, pressed into the matt damp substrate
ic1: screens the flanks and the cove substrate
im: fills the chased crack flush; coved fillet approx. 4 cm
approx. 1.3 kg/m (crack, cove); 1.7 kg/m² per mm
ic2: over the mortar and the surface

WPT.rc.title: Retrospective concrete waterproofing
WPT.rc.sub: Crystalline waterproofing: the active ingredients grow into the concrete and seal it from within.
WPT.rc.intro: The rapid mortar {F20} stops the running water, the crystalline repair mortar {IM} fills chased cracks and forms the coves, and the crystalline slurry {IC} is brushed into the matt damp concrete in two coats: its active ingredients penetrate the capillaries, react with the moisture and the free lime and fill the pores with crystals. WPT.rc.adv.label: Advantages
WPT.rc.adv.title: Why the system works
rc.adv.cards: The water becomes the transport medium

The active ingredients of {IC} penetrate the concrete through its capillaries; water entering the component carries them deeper. They react to insoluble crystals that fill the smallest pores and cracks — and go on doing so whenever water arrives.
From the inside, against pressing water
{IC} is watertight against negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar; {IM} is suitable for negative water pressure. Basements, pits and tanks are sealed from the accessible side, without excavation.
CRD-C 48-92: 14 bar. Under EN 1504-2 (principle 2.2, moisture control) the capillary water absorption is w < 0.1 kg/m²·h⁰·⁵ while the coating stays vapour permeable (class I, sD < 5 m).

Hairline cracks that open after the application are sealed by renewed crystal growth ({IC} increased active crack healing). Static cracks and joints wider than 0.4 mm are opened 20 × 25 mm and filled with {IM}.
{IC} is suitable for drinking water containers; the tank is rinsed thoroughly with drinking water before it is filled. Filling of containers is possible after 3 days.
{F20} solidifies after 1–2 minutes, even under water, with a strong bond to concrete and no corrosion-promoting substances: approx. 3 N/mm² after 1 hour, approx. 30 N/mm² after 28 days.

rctank: Made good before it is coated

Water jetting at > 400 bar lays the concrete bare; static cracks over 0.4 mm are chased 20 × 25 mm, their edges screened with {IC} and filled flush with {IM}; the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm follows wet in wet.
Two coats into the damp concrete

{IC} is brushed evenly into the repeatedly wetted, matt damp substrate; the second coat while the first is still sticky; 1.5 kg/m² for accumulated water. It can be sprayed (Technical Information No. 43).

Protected from sun and wind for ≥ 24 hours, kept damp for ≥ 3 days from the day after application; filling possible after 3 days, drinking water tanks rinsed first. Pressurised water after ≥ 7 days; up to a month to the full sealing effect.
rcwall: Where water runs through the joint the opening is chiselled to a dovetail and a plug of {F20} is pressed in by hand until it hardens — after 1–2 minutes, with a noticeable warming, even under water.

The construction joint and the cracks are chased 20 × 25 mm, screened with {IC} and filled flush with {IM}; the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm on a screen of {IC}; {IC} over the fresh mortar after 1–3 hours.

{IC} in two coats into the matt damp concrete, 1.5 kg/m² for pressing water: the crystals grow into the capillaries and hold negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar. Kept damp ≥ 3 days, ventilated, no condensation.
rcpit: Under high water pressure a hose is set into a chiselled depression at the strongest flow and fixed with {F20}: the pressure is relieved while the joint around it is plugged. After drying the hose is removed and its hole plugged.
The wall–floor joint receives a coved fillet of {IM} of approx. 4 cm on a screen of {IC}; holes and chased cracks are filled flush, up to 10 mm per step.
Two coats of {IC} over walls and floor into the matt damp concrete; kept damp ≥ 3 days; deep pits are ventilated for 24 hours and the dew point avoided with dryers, never with direct heating.
rcsew: Aggressive or soft water (hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre) always requires a water analysis; the degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1. Sludge and biofilm are jetted off; cracks are chased and filled with {IM}.
{IC} in two coats into the matt damp concrete, 1.5 kg/m² for accumulated water; in containers the dew point is avoided with condensation dryers — direct heating or blowing warm air is not permitted.

Kept damp for ≥ 3 days at a constant relative humidity > 80 %; in service water tanks at 10–15 °C seven days are generally sufficient. Filling after 3 days; the slurry cannot be overcoated with tiles, plaster or paint.

WPT.ca.title: Crystalline concrete admixture
WPT.ca.sub: Watertight concrete from the mixer: the waterproofing is in the mix from day one.
WPT.ca.intro: The crystalline admixture is dosed into the fresh concrete — liquid with the mixing water ({CL170}, {CL210}) or as a powder onto the aggregates ({CP360}, {CP350}) — and hardens with it. When water reaches the hardened concrete the active ingredient dissolves, reacts with the calcium hydroxide of the cement and grows insoluble crystals in the capillary pores and in cracks: the component itself becomes the waterproofing. No membrane, no separate site trade, no renewal cycle; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal themselves for the life of the structure.
WPT.ca.photoCap: The effect in the section of a wall under water pressure: the denser matrix moves the capillary zone outwards, so water, chlorides and carbon dioxide stay away from the reinforcement. Switch between the reference concrete and the concrete with BETOCRETE.

WPT.ca.adv.label: Advantages
WPT.ca.adv.title: Why the system works
ca.adv.cards: Surface and continuous cracks up to 0.4 mm (tapering down to 0.5 mm) are healed by crystal growth whenever water reaches them — accelerated and increased against untreated concrete, for the life of the component.
Less water from the first day

The sealant integrated in {CL210} and {CP360} (DIN EN 934-2, Table 9) makes the hardened concrete hydrophobic at once: the capillary water absorption falls by more than half before the first crystal has grown.

Reduced chloride ion migration, lower carbonation speed ({CL210}, {CP360}), improved resistance to frost and freeze–thaw: less water carries fewer aggressive substances into the concrete and to the reinforcement.
A longer life for the component
By the BAW method — service life from the chloride migration coefficient and the concrete cover — a test report shows a 2.5-fold service life of the BETOCRETE concrete against the reference recipe.
{CL170} is a concrete plasticiser (DIN EN 934-2, Table 2) with crystalline effect: water saving up to 10 %, a lower w/c ratio, a smoother consistency — dosed with the mixing water in the plant.
{CP350} combines the crystalline effect with a corrosion inhibitor: reduced capillary absorption and chloride migration keep the steel passive. Suitable for drinking water (DVGW W 270 / W 347).

no protection layer, no seams, no adhesion, no excavation for repair: the waterproofing is the concrete

cabase: The slab and the walls are cast in the dosed concrete; the construction joint at the kicker is the classic weak point and gets the crystalline waterstop {CJ5}, cast in with the wall. Working joints: swelling tape {CJ6}; critical joints: the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve.
Dosing where the concrete is made

Liquid {CL170} or {CL210} is dosed with the mixing water by the dosing system of the plant; powder {CP360} / {CP350} onto the aggregates, mixed 30 seconds before water and cement, then 45 seconds more — or 3 kg water-soluble bags into the drum on site.

When the ground water rises the capillaries fill, the active ingredient reacts and the pores close; the inside stays dry and vapour permeable. A crack that opens later, up to 0.4 mm, heals itself; no excavation, no membrane to repair.
capit: The deepest point of the building

The lift pit stands below the ground water table on all sides: slab, walls and the kicker joint are cast in the dosed concrete; the waterstop {CJ5} in the kicker, the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve where the pit cannot be reached later.

Where the concrete arrives by truck, {CP360} or {CP350} goes in as 3 kg water-soluble bags: approx. 1 minute of mixing per m³ of drum content, at least 5 minutes. Crack-width limits by the structural engineer; minimum thickness 15 cm.
The pit stays dry from the first day; the buffers, rails and anchors are fixed to dry concrete. A crack from settlement or shrinkage closes itself when water reaches it.
catank: A tank holds water permanently: the dosed concrete seals from the inside out, with {CL170}, {CP360} or {CP350} — tested for drinking water after DVGW W 270 and W 347. {CL210} is used where drinking water is not involved.
The joint between slab and wall gets the crystalline waterstop {CJ5}; inlets and outlets are cast in; the crystalline structure heals the fine cracks that a filled tank always sees.
Vapour permeable, no lining to renew
There is no coating that could taint the water, lift or age; the crystals are part of the concrete. Cracks up to 0.4 mm heal; the pore structure stays dense for the life of the tank.
cawall: Earth on one side, weather on the other

A retaining wall carries soil and seepage water on its back, frost, de-icing salt and traffic spray on its face. Cast in the dosed concrete, with {CL210} or {CP360} — the hydrophobic sealant lowers the water absorption at once, the crystals follow.

Reduced chloride ion migration and lower carbonation speed keep the reinforcement passive; the frost and freeze–thaw resistance of the concrete is improved. {CL210} shows the highest effectiveness in exposure class XS.
No external membrane, no protection boards, no renewal from the soil side: the drainage stays, the wall seals itself and heals its own cracks up to 0.4 mm.
