WPT.ca.tech.label: Technology
WPT.ca.tech.title: Crystalline waterproofing from inside the mix
WPT.ca.tech.sub: What happens inside a concrete that carries the crystalline admixture from the day it is poured: where the active ingredient sits, what wakes it, how the pores close throughout the depth of the component — and why a crack years later closes itself. Schematic, at the scale of the capillary pores; not to scale.
WPT.ca.tech.player: Micro scale · inside the hardened cement paste, step by step
WPT.ca.tech.aria: 3D animation of the crystalline reaction inside a concrete made with the admixture
WPT.ca.tech.hint: Drag to look round · the offset stays until replay
ca.tech.steps: In the mix from day one

The admixture is dosed into the fresh concrete — 1.75–2.25 % of the cement weight for the liquids {CL170} and {CL210}, 0.75–1.25 % for the powders {CP360} and {CP350} — and distributed through the whole volume by the mixer. When the cement hydrates the active ingredient is locked into the hardened cement paste: in every pore wall, at every depth, not only on a surface.

Hardened cement paste is porous: capillary pores of roughly 0.01 to 10 µm link up into a network. Under ground water or a filled tank this network draws water in by capillary suction and pressure. In a plain concrete that water runs on to the reinforcement and through separating cracks into the building.
The active ingredient dissolves and reacts

The pore water dissolves the active ingredient where it meets it. Deep in the pores it reacts with what every cement hydration leaves behind — calcium hydroxide (portlandite, Ca(OH)₂) — and with the dissolved CO₂: insoluble crystalline phases form. The concrete supplies the second reactant; the crystals are part of the concrete, not a foreign material in it.

Needle-shaped crystals grow from the pore walls into the pore space and interlock. Because the active ingredient is everywhere, growth starts wherever water arrives — at the ground side, along a crack, around an aggregate grain — not from one surface inwards. The micrographs show the acicular clusters packing the capillary pore structure.
The capillaries are blocked — the zone shifts outwards

Where the crystals have grown, the pore is too narrow for liquid water. The capillary zone of the component, the depth to which water is drawn in, moves outwards; ground moisture and pressurised water are conducted much less far into the concrete and stay away from the reinforcement. Water vapour still diffuses: the concrete dries instead of trapping moisture behind a film.

Concrete cracks — shrinkage, settlement, temperature. A surface or continuous crack up to 0.4 mm (tapering down to 0.5 mm) brings water in, and with it the reaction restarts: unreacted active ingredient at the crack faces dissolves and fresh crystals bridge the gap. Crack injections for non-dynamic separating cracks up to 0.4 mm can often be omitted. Movements can reopen a sealed crack — then it heals again.

Less water means less of what the water carries: chloride ion migration is reduced and the carbonation rate is lower ({CL210}, {CP360}), the frost and freeze–thaw resistance improves. The reinforcement stays in the dry core. By the BAW method — service life from the chloride migration coefficient — a test report shows a 2.5-fold service life against the reference concrete.
Permanently active, for the life of the component

Not all of the active ingredient is consumed. What remains lies dormant in the matrix and waits for water — for decades. No film to age, no seam to fail, nothing to renew: the waterproofing is as durable as the concrete itself, and the sealant in {CL210} and {CP360} has been keeping the water absorption low from the first day.

The capillaries are blocked — vapour still passes
A later crack fills with crystals and closes

The composition of the active ingredients is proprietary; the mechanism is that of crystalline waterproofing technology and shows in the micrographs of the needle-shaped crystals in the capillary pore structure and in the tests of the data sheets and test reports: depth of water penetration under pressure (EN 12390-8), crack healing, chloride migration, freeze–thaw–salt, carbonation.
WPT.ca.tech.needs.title: What the technology needs — and what it does not do
ca.tech.needs: Cement ≥ 270 kg/m³ (CEM I), ≥ 290 (CEM II), ≥ 380 (CEM III/A); w/c < 0.55; fly ash ≤ 80 and granulated slag ≤ 100 kg/m³ added to the binder; grain size 16 mm (exceptionally 32 mm); component thickness ≥ 15 cm. CEM III/C is prohibited, CEM III/B for the liquids and {CP350}; lignite fly ash is of limited suitability. Preliminary tests are always necessary.
Water, to work and to keep working
The reaction runs in water: where no water arrives the active ingredient simply waits. That is the point — it reacts exactly where the concrete is loaded.

The admixture does not replace compaction, curing and the crack-width design: the planner and structural engineer set the crack-width limits, the concrete is produced, placed and post-treated to the valid standards. In rare cases the admixture influences the setting — {RUX} controls it.

The construction joint is the classic weak point: {CJ5}, the crystalline metal waterstop, {CJ6}, the swelling tape, and {CJ1}, the injection hose, are the accessories of the system. Moving cracks and joints wider than 0.4 mm are not self-healed — they are injected.

The crystals make the concrete watertight; they do not make it acid-proof. Concretes of exposure class XA3 (DIN EN 206-1 / DIN 1045-2) are excluded. Where the concrete itself is attacked, a resistant coating armours it.

WPT.ca.tech.fld.title: Where the technology pays
WPT.ca.tech.fld.sub: The fields in which BETOCRETE concrete is used today as the economical waterproofing — and to extend the service life of the component.
ca.tech.fld: Foundations, base slabs and basement walls

Watertight concrete without an external membrane: no protection boards, no weather window, no damage during backfill. The construction joints get the crystalline waterstop; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal themselves.
Collection and retaining basins, tanks and containers
Water on the inside, for good: the dosed concrete seals from the inside out and heals the fine cracks a filled tank always sees. {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested for drinking water.
Swimming pools embedded in the ground
Ground water from outside, pool water from inside: the whole section is watertight, vapour permeable and free of a lining that could lift.
Chlorides from de-icing salt are the enemy of the reinforcement: reduced chloride ion migration and lower carbonation speed keep the steel passive; frost and freeze–thaw resistance improve.
Tunnels and concrete pipes, drains and manhole access points
Pre-cast or in-situ: the admixture goes into the mix at the plant, the component arrives watertight. Shotcrete is an application too.
Cooling towers and power stations, water and wastewater structures
Infrastructure that must not leak and cannot be renewed easily: one pour, one component, no renewal cycle. Exposure class XA3 is excluded; aggressive media need an armouring coating.

Soil and seepage water behind, frost and salt in front: the hydrophobic sealant of {CL210} and {CP360} lowers the water absorption at once, the crystals follow. {CL210} shows the highest effectiveness in exposure class XS.
The deepest point of the building, below the ground water, reachable only from the inside: cast watertight from the start, dry from the first day, no pump running for years.

WPT.ca.lcc.why.title: Why the curves separate
ca.lcc.why: No separate trade, no protection layer

The waterproofing becomes an integral part of the component as early as the production of the concrete in the plant. Subsequent liquid waterproofing can be omitted and does not have to be organised, carried out and monitored on site.
The crystals are as durable as the concrete; there is no film to age, so nothing is re-applied. BETOCRETE waterproofing works for a component’s lifetime — renovation cycles can be eliminated.
Crack injections for non-dynamic separating cracks up to 0.4 mm can often be omitted due to the crack-healing ability of the concrete.
Water kept out of the pores means chloride and carbon dioxide kept away from the reinforcement: the service life of the component itself is extended — the largest item of any life-cycle account.
WPT.ca.lcc.note: Model, not a quotation. Nominal costs are summed as they fall due; present values discount every year’s cost at the rate set (ISO 15686-5). Downtime, the risk of leaks and the extended service life of the structure are not priced in — they favour the integral system further. Replace the defaults by the rates of your project.

WPT.pf.title: Protective flooring and coating systems
WPT.pf.sub: Seamless resin floors from the primer to the seal: one system for the garage, the workshop, the hall and the wastewater plant.
WPT.pf.intro: Every protective floor is a system of layers on a prepared concrete substrate: a primer that seals the pores or blocks moisture and oil ({GBM}, {G1270}, {SG3}, {SG3T}, {SG3F}, {SG2}), a scratch coat or mortar where the substrate must be levelled or repaired ({EV200}, {K4031}), the coating that carries the load and the chemicals ({B351}, {V2370}), the seal that gives the surface its finish, colour and slip resistance ({V360}, {V2260} with {ANTI}) and the elastic joint ({IPU}). Two-component epoxy and polyurethane resins that cure by reaction, bonded to the concrete with ≥ 1.5 N/mm², resistant to forklift traffic, oils, acids and alkalis — in layers of 0.1 to 2 mm, walkable after about 12 hours, fully loadable after 7 days.

pfgarage: The aqueous {V360} is primer, levelling compound and seal in one product: diluted as the primer, filled with quartz sand or {FF} for the levelling, rolled in two steps as the seal — walkable after 16 hours, the garage done in two days.
The seal resists the softeners of car tyres, dilute acids and alkalis, heating oil and petrol; it is pigmented in standard RAL colours and vapour permeable, so the slab can still breathe.
With 8–10 % {ANTI} in the last coat the floor reaches slip class R10; the wall–floor joint is closed with {IPU}, elastic and UV-resistant.
pfwork: {GBM} seals the pores and, sanded, keys the coating; {B351} at approx. 1 mm is the pigmented self-levelling floor of the workshop and the commercial unit: approx. 70 N/mm², Shore D approx. 72, resistant to oils, acids and cleaning agents.
{V2260}, the aqueous PU seal, makes the coating light-fast, UV-stable and scratch resistant and gives it the gloss of a showroom; with {ANTI} it is slip resistant.
Breakouts and anchor holes are filled with {K4031}; the field and connection joints are cut, primed and filled with {IPU} — chamfered 45° where vehicles cross.
pfhall: Two coats of primer, sand in between
High loads need a pore-sealed, well-keyed substrate: {GBM} in two steps, the second broadcast with quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm; a scratch coat of {GBM} + sand where the slab is rough.

{B351} filled 2 : 1 with quartz sand, spread at approx. 2 mm and de-aerated: the forklift, the pallet truck and the dropped pallet meet approx. 70 N/mm² and 44 N/mm² flexural; the machine bases are grouted with {EV200} (approx. 109 N/mm²).
The slip-resistant finish — interspersing coat, quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm broadcast, top seal — reaches R11 by test report and up to R12; the joints are filled with {IPU}, 25 % total deformation.
pfdamp: The concrete need not be dry

A young slab, a basement floor on ground water, a floor without a vapour barrier: {SG3} bonds to the matt damp concrete, blocks vapour and negative pressing water up to 3 bar and seals the pores — two coats, the second sanded.
{SG3F} does the same in a fraction of the time: the second coat after approx. 3.5 hours, the coating within 5 days; it also makes the repair mortar that carries load again quickly.
{SG3T}, the thixotropic version, goes up the plinth and the wall and makes the capillary-breaking mortar; above it the floor is coated with {B351} like any dry floor.
pfoil: Oil that has risen through the concrete cannot be coated over: the surface is shot-blasted, then cleaned with {R008} and hot water, scrubbed twice and vacuumed — and not dried off, because the primer must meet the damp, oil-free surface.

{SG2} displaces the water from the capillaries and blocks capillary-rising oil and vapour (sd > 100 m) and water pressure up to 3 bar; quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm over the whole fresh surface gives the key.
On the sanded barrier the thick coat of {B351} with quartz sand, the slip-resistant finish and the joints with {IPU} follow as in any hall; breakouts and machine bases with {EV200}.
pfsewage: Sewage, sulphuric acid down to pH 0–1, sea water, the abrasion of the flow: {V2370} is the sealing coating for sewage treatment plants, sewage pipes, digestion towers and steel sheet piles — exposure class XWW4 after DIN 19753.
Primer on concrete, none on steel

On the cementitious substrate the thixotropic barrier primer {SG3T} goes first, on floor and walls; on steel blasted to Sa 2½ the first layer of {V2370} is the primer. Two layers in alternating colours show the coverage.
Breakouts, gullies and anchors are grouted with {EV200} — watertight to 5 bar from 10 mm; the movement joints are filled with {IPU}, −40 to +80 °C.

pf.lcc.why: The surface does not wear into the concrete
A bare slab dusts, pits and spalls under forklift wheels; every patch is a repair with downtime. The coating takes the wear, and a worn top seal is rolled on again overnight.
Cleaning is a wipe, not a treatment
Sealed pores do not drink oil, coolant or de-icing salt: the floor is cleaned with {R008} and water instead of being ground, stripped or replaced.
The elastic joint with {IPU} keeps water and dirt out of the slab joints; the edges, chamfered, do not break under the wheel.
What stays on the surface does not reach the reinforcement: chlorides and acids kept out of the concrete extend the life of the slab itself — the largest item of any life-cycle account.

WPT.rc.tech.label: Technology
WPT.rc.tech.title: Crystalline waterproofing: how the concrete seals itself
WPT.rc.tech.sub: What happens inside the concrete after {IC} has been brushed on: where the active ingredients travel, what they react with, why the seal is permanent — and what that means over the life of the structure. Schematic, at the scale of the capillary pores; not to scale.
WPT.rc.tech.player: Micro scale · the reaction, step by step
WPT.rc.tech.aria: 3D animation of the crystalline reaction in the capillary pores of the concrete
WPT.rc.tech.hint: Drag to rotate · Shift + drag to pan
rc.tech.steps: Hardened cement paste is porous: capillary pores of roughly 0.01 to 10 µm link up into a network, and micro-cracks join it. Under a head of water this network is the path — from the ground side through the wall into the basement, the pit or the tank. Capillary suction and pressure keep the water moving; it arrives on the inside as damp patches, salt bloom, drops.
The slurry on the matt-damp concrete

After the leaks are plugged with {F20} and the chased cracks and coves are made with {IM}, {IC} is brushed in two coats into the matt-damp, open-pored concrete. It is not a film that has to hold on the surface: it is a reservoir of active ingredients sitting on the mouths of the capillaries.

The active ingredients dissolve in the pore water. Driven by the concentration gradient — and by the moisture that a component under water load always carries — they diffuse along the capillaries into the concrete, even against the direction in which the water flows. The water that was the enemy becomes the transport medium: “foe becomes friend”.
The reaction in the pore walls

Deep in the pores they meet what every cement hydration leaves behind: calcium hydroxide (portlandite, Ca(OH)₂) and unhydrated cement grains. The reaction forms insoluble crystalline calcium silicate hydrate phases — needle-shaped crystals that grow from the pore walls into the pore space and interlock. The concrete itself supplies the second reactant: the crystals are part of the concrete, not a foreign material on it.

Where the crystals have grown, the pore is too narrow for liquid water: neither capillary suction nor the water pressure finds a passage. Water vapour still diffuses through the crystal network — the concrete stays vapour permeable (EN 1504-2 class I, sD < 5 m), so it dries out instead of trapping moisture behind a film. Impermeability to water: 14 bar (CRD-C 48-92); against negative pressing water: 1.5 bar.

Not all of the active ingredients are consumed. What remains lies dormant in the matrix for the life of the structure. When water reaches it again — through a new hairline crack (up to 0.4 mm), a settlement, a freeze–thaw fissure — the reaction restarts and fresh crystals close the new path. The self-healing that plain concrete manages only partly (autogenous healing) becomes reliable and repeatable.
Permanent: the seal is inside the concrete

The barrier is a crystalline structure inside the pore system, not a layer on the surface, so it does not depend on adhesion. The surface may be worn, abraded, tiled over or lose its brushed skin — the crystallised zone below remains and keeps sealing. It cannot peel, puncture, delaminate or age like a membrane, and it resists water pressure from either side.
Over the life of the structure

One application, no renewal cycle: the crystalline zone is as durable as the concrete around it and grows deeper for as long as moisture and unreacted active ingredient meet. Water that stays out is chloride and carbon dioxide that stay out — the reinforcement stays protected (carbonation reducing, chloride-free). The life-cycle comparison below turns this into figures.

WPT.rc.tech.rxn.title: The reaction, in one line
WPT.rc.tech.rxn.hyd: Cement hydration leaves free lime in every concrete:
WPT.rc.tech.rxn.ic: The crystalline waterproofing turns that lime into crystals in the pores:
WPT.rc.tech.rxn.icEq: active ingredients of {IC} + Ca(OH)₂ + H₂O → insoluble crystalline calcium silicate hydrate
WPT.rc.tech.rxn.note: Simplified. The composition of the active ingredients is proprietary; the mechanism is that of crystalline waterproofing technology and shows in penetration tests, in micrographs of the needle-shaped crystals in the pores and in the standardised water permeability tests of the data sheets (EN 12390-8, CRD-C 48-92).
WPT.rc.tech.needs.title: What the technology needs — and what it does not do
rc.tech.needs: Concrete free of films, curing agents, laitance, paint and oil; the pores must be open, the surface saturated but matt — that is what the preparation with the high-pressure jet is for.
Moisture, to work and to keep working
The reaction runs in water: the coats are kept damp for 3 days, and later crystal growth needs water to arrive. In a dry component the active ingredients simply wait.
The crystals seal capillaries and hairline cracks. Voids, honeycombs, open cracks and running leaks are repaired first ({F20}, {IM}); the slurry is the last layer, not a filler.
Moving cracks and joints are injected
Cracks and joints that keep moving, or wider than 0.4 mm, are not self-healed: they are injected with {P1} / {P4} or filled with {IM} before the surface is waterproofed.

The crystals make the concrete watertight; they do not make it acid-proof. Where biogenic sulphuric acid or other aggressive media attack the concrete itself (above the water line of a sewage tank, for instance), a resistant coating protects the concrete — the crystalline seal below keeps the water where it belongs.

WPT.rc.tech.fld.title: Where the technology pays
WPT.rc.tech.fld.sub: Fields in which the crystalline principle solves what a surface layer cannot — from the inside, on damp concrete, for good.
rc.tech.fld: From the inside, tested for drinking water (DVGW W 270 / W 347): no coating that could taint the water, 14 bar on the positive side, vapour permeable so the wall stays healthy. Filling after 3 days.

The crystalline seal keeps the sludge in and the ground water out — after a water analysis of aggressive or soft water. Above the water line, where biogenic acid attacks the concrete, a resistant coating armours the concrete; the seal below stays.

Against negative pressing water from the inside: no excavation, no disturbance of roads, gardens and neighbours. The wall keeps breathing, so plaster and room stay dry; moving cracks are injected first.

Running leaks are stopped with {F20} in minutes, coves and cracks made good with {IM}, the pit sealed with {IC}: back in service quickly, walkable after about 5 hours, without pumps running for years.
Against ground water from the accessible side; vapour permeable; abrasion, cleaning and surface wear do not remove the seal; no protection layer, no seams.
On the positive side: 14 bar, no membrane to protect from ice, debris and ultraviolet light; hairline cracks from temperature and shrinkage seal themselves for the life of the concrete.

WPT.rc.lcc.why.title: Why the curves separate
rc.lcc.why: The crystals are as durable as the concrete; there is no film to age, so nothing is re-applied. The upkeep is inspection.
From the inside there is no excavation, no road closure, no drainage to rebuild, no protection boards. Every renewal of an outside membrane pays that bill again.
Hairline cracks that would need a repair campaign on a film seal themselves: fewer interventions, no downtime of the tank or the pit.

Water kept out of the pores means chloride and carbon dioxide kept away from the reinforcement: the service life of the component itself is extended, which is the largest item of any life-cycle account.

{RB400} in a minimum of two application steps, free of pores, the second after approx. 3 hours: ≥ 2.0 mm dry film on concrete, ≥ 3.0 mm on masonry, ≥ 4.0 mm for pressing water W2.1-E.
Protection and drainage boards bonded with {RB400} and quartz sand 0.1–0.35 mm, buttering-floating. Rainproof after approx. 3 hours, 1 bar after approx. 16 hours, pressurised water after ≥ 1 day.
inner: Salts and rising damp dealt with first
Plaster off 80 cm beyond the damage, joints raked out 20 mm, levelled with {M30}; the retroactive horizontal barrier with {I380} or {AQF} stops the capillary transport.
The rigid slurry, coat by coat
{AQ1K} brushed, trowelled or sprayed into the matt damp substrate, up to 1 mm per step, the second after approx. 6 hours; three steps for pressing water (up to 0.75 bar from the negative side).
Keep damp ≥ 24 hours, no condensation, no direct heating; pressurised water after ≥ 7 days. The THERMOPAL restoration plaster stores salts and lets the wall breathe.
negc: High-pressure water jetting lays the concrete bare; honeycombs broken out and filled with {M30}, the joint chased and filled, sealing cove; then {AQ1K} brushed in as pre-sealing — the rigid slurry keeps the moisture from the rear off the flexible coating.

The construction joint with {RB400} 15 cm on both sides to ≥ 4.0 mm dry film; then two coats over the face to ≥ 3.0 mm for water pressure, ≥ 2.0 mm for soil moisture (WTA 4-6); crack-bridging, radon-tight, watertight against negative pressing water to 0.75 bar.
Keep damp ≥ 3 days in dry rooms, ventilate deep pits, no condensation, no direct heating; 1 bar after approx. 16 hours, pressurised water after ≥ 1 day. Plaster, tiles or a coating may follow.
tank: Jet-cleaned; voids re-profiled with {BIS540} on {HSF}, smoothed with {BIS16}; water-bearing cracks injected. The wall–floor junction with {RB400} and ASO-Dichtband-2000-S.
Two coats over walls and floor
{RB400} by spray, brush or trowel, free of pores; ≥ 2.0 mm dry film for crack widths < 0.2 mm (W2-B), ≥ 4.0 mm for < 1.0 mm. {AQ2K} for chlorinated water, {AQ1K} for process and waste water.
Kept damp, condensation avoided with dryers; {RB400} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 1 day, the slurries after ≥ 7 days. Soft or aggressive water needs a water analysis (EN 1992-1-1).
balcony: ASO-Dichtband-2000 tapes, corners and sleeves bonded in {AQ2K} at the wall–floor joint, drains and intersections; movement joints with ASO-Dichtband-2000-S.
{AQ2K} in two application steps of up to 1 mm, the second after approx. 3–6 hours; 3.5 kg/m² plus 25 % allowance (DIN 18531, DIN 18534). Crack bridging even at −5 °C.
Tiles laid with a tile adhesive of the system list when the waterproofing has completely hardened; no point or linear loads on the coating itself.
park: Concrete damaged by de-icing salt is milled off; the deck is blasted, matt damp; very absorbent substrates primed with {PRIM}.
Scratch coat and first layer, wet in wet
{OS} pressed in as scratch coat and contact layer, the first layer immediately afterwards; up to 3 mm per step, approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm.
Second layer after approx. 3 hours, approx. 5.5 kg/m² in total (OS 5b). Rainproof after 4 hours; chloride and CO₂ barrier, crack bridging class B2 at −20 °C.

planE.title: Determine the water impact class
planE.short: DIN 18533: W1.1-E, W1.2-E, W4-E or W2.1-E — the class sets the dry film thickness.
planE.overview: The material rate depends on the required dry film thickness corresponding to the water impact class (material rate table of the technical data sheet). Ground moisture and non-pressurised water (W1.1-E, W1.2-E): ≥ 2.0 mm on concrete, ≥ 3.0 mm on masonry work; moderate pressing water ≤ 3 m (W2.1-E): ≥ 4.0 mm; splash water at the wall base (W4-E): ≥ 2.0 mm.
points: W1.1-E: highly permeable subsoil or back-filling, minimum 50 cm above the design water level; W1.2-E: water-logging avoided through drainage
W2.1-E: backwater or flood water up to 3 m; loose/fixed flange constructions or tested house entry systems for pipe penetrations
the waterproofing must be protected against weathering and mechanical damage in accordance with DIN 18533; drainage in accordance with DIN 4095

prepE.title: Prepare the substrate
prepE.short: Even, load-bearing, pore open, fully grouted; edges chamfered, corners rounded; depressions levelled; matt damp.
prepE.overview: Requirement for the substrate: even, free of adhesion inhibiting substances, sealed in the surface, pore open, load-bearing, extensively fully grouted. Depressions > 5 mm, mortar pockets, plaster grooves in brickwork, open butt or bed joints, damaged areas, large-pored substrates or uneven masonry work must be levelled in advance with {M30}.
points: before any application, remove all loose or poorly bonded layers from the wall footing and the transition to the splash water plinth down to the cementitious substrate
edges are to be chamfered and corners are to be rounded
level indentations < 5 mm with {M30} / {AQ1K} or a mixture of {RB400} and quartz sand 0.1–0.35 mm (approx. 6 kg to 24 kg)
high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar) and blasting are suitable measures; the last step is cleaning with pressure water
pre-moisten the dry substrate so that it is matt damp at the time of application; extremely absorbent and slightly sandy substrates are primed with {PRIM}, which must have reacted fully
moisture penetration from the rear must be avoided; for waterproofing with moisture from the rear, pre-seal with {AQ1K} or ASODUR-SG3-thix

cove.title: Install the sealing cove with ASOCRET-M30
cove.short: Bonding slurry of AQUAFIN-1K or ASOCRET-M30, then the cove, edge height 4–6 cm, rounded, wet in wet.
cove.overview: Base slab–wall transition: pre-screen with {AQ1K} or {M30} in a consistency that is able to screen. While still wet, install a sealing cove with an edge height of at least 4 cm made of {M30} and round it off. After drying, carry out the waterproofing.
points: {M30}: water 4.5–5.25 l per 25 kg, mixing time approx. 3 minutes, maturing 5 minutes, homogenise again; pot life approx. 45 minutes
consumption of the sealing cove approx. 3 kg/m
the cementitious sealing cove can be overcoated after approx. 3 hours with the waterproofing system
alternatively the fillet is formed with ASO-Dichtband-2000-S (system page)
in the area of structural movement joints the waterproofing is reinforced with ADF-Dehnfugenband or ASO-Dichtband-2000-S

pipe.title: Seal the pipe penetrations
pipe.short: AQUAFIN-RB400 with the notched trowel, the pipe sleeve bonded free from folds and fully overcoated.
pipe.overview: For the watertight formation of pipe penetrations, the system components of the ASO-Dichtmanschetten (sleeves) or ADF-Rohrmanschette are used in accordance with their technical data sheets: {RB400} is applied with a 4 mm notched trowel and smoothed, the sleeve is bonded free from folds and subsequently fully overcoated.
points: in water impact class W2.1-E, suitable loose/fixed flange constructions or tested house entry systems must be used
on PVC, gunmetal and stainless steel flanges the sleeves are installed without voids or wrinkles and integrated seamlessly into the waterproofing
direct contact with metals such as copper, zinc and aluminium is avoided by a pore-sealed primer of ASODUR-GBM in two steps

mixRB.title: Mix AQUAFIN-RB400
mixRB.short: Liquid component into the bucket, powder in, 3 minutes; mature 5 minutes; homogenise again.
mixRB.overview: Put the liquid component into a clean mixing bucket and mix with the powder component to produce a homogeneous, lump-free mass (mix ratio A : B = 1.5 : 1 by weight). The mixing time is approx. 3 minutes. After a settling period of approx. 5 minutes, thoroughly homogenise the compound again.
points: stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm with a suitable mixing paddle
depending on the application technique (screen or spray), do not add more than max. 0.24 l water per 24 kg; water is added after mixing
pot life approx. 45 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C
do not add water or new material to material that has already set

coatE1.title: Apply the first coat of AQUAFIN-RB400
coatE1.short: Brush, trowel or spray, free of pores; an even thickness with the coating-thickness or notched trowel, then smoothing.
coatE1.overview: Apply {RB400} in a minimum of two application steps ensuring it is free of pores. An even layer thickness is achieved using a coating thickness trowel or notched trowel and then smoothing. The material rate depends on the required dry film thickness corresponding to the water impact class.
points: can be trowelled off and applied with a brush; machine application after Technical Information No. 43
in case of strong sunlight, work against the movement of the sun in shaded areas
protect surfaces that are not to be treated
the waterproofing must not be affected by water during binding: the effect of water from behind can lead to spalling in case of frost

coatE2.title: Apply the second coat after approx. 3 hours
coatE2.short: When the first coat can no longer be damaged by reworking; to the dry film thickness of the class.
coatE2.overview: The second application step (and following) can take place when the first application step can no longer be damaged by reworking — overcoat after approx. 3 hours. Total dry film thickness ≥ 2.0 mm (concrete, W1-E/W4-E), ≥ 3.0 mm (masonry), ≥ 4.0 mm (W2.1-E).
points: rainproof on inclined surfaces after approx. 3 hours; standing water must be avoided
sealing against pressing water (1 bar) after approx. 16 hours; withstands pressurised water after ≥ 1 day

transitions of watertight concrete components (immersion depth ≤ 3 m, opening ≤ 1.0 mm): 15 cm on both sides of the joint, two steps, 4 mm dry film with a 6–8 mm notched trowel; or the ASO-Dichtband system overcoated ≥ 2.5 mm
{RB400} as a surface coating must not be exposed to point or linear loads

board.title: Bond the protection and drainage boards
board.short: AQUAFIN-RB400 mixed with quartz sand 0.1–0.35 mm, buttering-floating with the notched trowel; perimeter insulation fully bonded.
board.overview: The waterproofing must be protected against weathering influences and mechanical damage using suitable protective measures in accordance with DIN 18533. For the bonding of suitable protection/drainage boards and perimeter insulation boards, {RB400} is mixed with quartz sand 0.1–0.35 mm (approx. 6 kg per 24 kg) and applied with a suitable notched trowel using the buttering-floating method.
points: depending on the water impact class, bonding is either spot application or covering the whole area
perimeter insulation is installed butt-jointed and offset in accordance with the manufacturer, fully bonded with {RB400}
alternatively bonding is carried out with the 2-component bituminous thick layer coating COMBIDIC-2K-CLASSIC or COMBIDIC-2K-PREMIUM
drainage is carried out in accordance with DIN 4095

cureE.title: Cure, protect, backfill
cureE.short: Keep damp for at least 3 days in dry conditions; ventilate pits; protect against mechanical damage before backfilling.
cureE.overview: The material cures very well in areas with high humidity. In relatively dry areas, keep the coating damp for at least 3 days. In poorly ventilated rooms and deep pits, adequate ventilation should be provided for 24 hours.
points: the waterproofing must not be affected by water during binding
protect the fresh coating from rain, frost and direct sunlight; standing water must be avoided
backfill only against the protected waterproofing (DIN 18533)

cleanS.title: Clean tools, store material
cleanS.short: Clean tools immediately after use with a suitable solvent. Store frost-free, 5–40 °C.
cleanS.overview: Clean tools immediately after use with suitable solvent. Store in a frost-free, cool and dry place: at min. 5–40 °C for 12 months in the original container. Promptly use opened containers.
points: observe the applicable safety data sheets of both components
very low emission — EMICODE EC 1PLUS: positive evaluations within DGNB, LEED, BREEAM, HQE

planI.title: Assess the exposure and the substrate
planI.short: WTA 4-6: which water acts from behind, how much salt is in the masonry — the class sets the number of coats.
planI.overview: Retroactive waterproofing of building components in direct ground contact in accordance with WTA datasheet 4-6. The slurries withstand negative pressing water up to 0.75 bar. Soil moisture and non-pressurised water: > 2.0 mm dry film; standing seepage water / pressure water: > 3.0 mm ({AQ2K}: 5.3 kg/m²; {AQ1K}: three application steps in the classic system).
points: the classic system with {AQ1K} is for substrates that are not at risk of cracking; for substrates that are subsequently prone to cracking use {RB400} (the flexible system with radon protection) or {AQ2K}
before use the existing test certificates and the WTA datasheet “Subsequent waterproofing of components in contact with the ground” must be observed
in rooms with high humidity and insufficient ventilation, condensation on the surface must be avoided with condensation dryers; direct heating or blowing warm air is not permitted
planI.src: AQ1K · AQ2K · RB400 · M30 · system page

prepI.title: Remove the plaster, prepare the masonry
prepI.short: Plaster off 80 cm beyond the damage, salt-laden joints raked out 20 mm, jetted clean, levelled with ASOCRET-M30, matt damp.
prepI.overview: The damaged plaster is removed at least 80 cm beyond the damaged area; salt-laden joints are scraped out approx. 20 mm deep and the surfaces cleaned mechanically. Depressions, mortar pockets, plaster grooves, open joints and uneven masonry work are levelled in advance with {M30}; a sealing groove/fillet is formed at the floor–wall transition.
points: requirement: load-bearing, even, pore open, sealed in the surface, free of adhesion inhibiting substances
high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar); the last step is cleaning with pressure water
ESCO-FLUAT converts sulphate and chloride salts into less soluble compounds (system page)
pre-moisten to matt damp, no puddles; very absorbent substrates are primed with {PRIM}, which must be dry before the next step
{M30}: 3–30 mm in one step, approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm; sealing cove approx. 3 kg/m; overcoat after approx. 3 hours

barrier.title: Install the retroactive horizontal barrier
barrier.short: AQUAFIN-i380 injection cream (or AQUAFIN-F) in a row of drill holes; holes resealed with ASOCRET-M30.
barrier.overview: System “Basement waterproofing: the classic system”: {AQF} creates the retroactive horizontal damp-proof barrier against capillary rising damp; the flexible and the day system use the injection cream {I380}. The drilled holes are resealed with {M30}.
points: the barrier stops the capillary transport in the wall; the slurry then waterproofs the face against water from behind
products of the subgroups “Injection” and “Mortars and restoration plasters” — follow their technical data sheets

mix1K.title: Mix AQUAFIN-1K
mix1K.short: Approx. 6.7 l of water per 25 kg, mix approx. 3 minutes, lump-free.
mix1K.overview: Put approx. 6.7 l of water per 25 kg into a clean mixing bucket and mix with the powder component to produce a homogeneous, lump-free mass. Mixing time approx. 2–3 minutes.
points: stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm with a suitable mixing paddle
water addition approx. 26–27 %
pot life approx. 60 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C ({AQ1KP}: approx. 30 minutes)
do not add water or new mortar to mortar that has already set (risk of inadequate strength development)

coatI1.title: Apply the first coat of AQUAFIN-1K
coatI1.short: Brush, trowel or spray into the matt damp substrate, free of pores; up to 1 mm per step.
coatI1.overview: Apply {AQ1K} in a minimum of two application steps ensuring it is free of pores. An even layer thickness is achieved using a coating thickness trowel or notched trowel and then smoothing. Max. layer thickness per application step: up to 1 mm ({AQ1KP}: 2 mm).
points: the substrate may be matt damp; the formation of puddles must be avoided
consumption approx. 1.75 kg/m² per mm; in total approx. 3.5–5.3 kg/m²
can be trowelled off and applied with a brush; machine application after Technical Information No. 43

coatI2.title: Apply the second coat after approx. 6 hours
coatI2.short: When the first coat can no longer be damaged; never more than approx. 2 kg/m² in one step.
coatI2.overview: The second application step (and following) can take place when the first application step can no longer be damaged by reworking: overcoat after approx. 6 hours ({AQ1KP}: after approx. 90 minutes, even under unfavourable ambient conditions).
points: an application thickness of more than 2 kg/m² in one application step can lead to cracking
an even layer thickness with the coating thickness trowel or notched trowel, then smoothing

coatI3.title: Third coat for pressing water
coatI3.short: Standing seepage or pressing water: three application steps, approx. 5.3 kg/m².
coatI3.overview: System “Basement waterproofing: the classic system”: {AQ1K} is applied as retroactive interior waterproofing in three layers for pressure water scenarios. WTA 4-6, standing seepage water / pressure water: > 3.0 mm dry film thickness ({AQ2K}: 5.3 kg/m²).
points: the upper limit of the consumption range (approx. 5.3 kg/m²) corresponds to the pressing water case
watertightness against negative pressing water up to 0.75 bar

cureI.title: Keep damp, protect
cureI.short: After hardening keep the surface damp for ≥ 24 hours; protect from rapid drying; no condensation.
cureI.overview: After the coating has hardened, keep the surface damp for ≥ 24 hours. Protect the fresh coating from rain, wind, frost and direct sunlight. In rooms with high humidity and/or insufficient ventilation, dropping below the dew point (condensation) on the surface must be avoided by suitable measures such as condensation dryers.
points: direct heating or uncontrolled blowing of warm air is not permitted
foot traffic after approx. 24 hours; withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days

plaster.title: Restoration plaster system
plaster.short: THERMOPAL-SP splatterdash, THERMOPAL-SR24 (or THERMOPAL-ULTRA) restoration plaster, THERMOPAL-FS33 finish.
plaster.overview: System “Basement waterproofing: the classic system”: after the interior waterproofing, the splatterdash coat {THSP} for adhesion, the restoration plaster {THSR} and, optionally, the finish coat THERMOPAL-FS33. The flexible system uses {THU}.
points: the restoration plaster stores salts and lets the wall breathe: vapour permeable, climate regulating
products of the subgroup “Mortars and restoration plasters” — follow their technical data sheets

cleanW.title: Clean tools, store material
cleanW.short: Clean tools thoroughly with water after use. Store cool and dry, min. 12 months.
cleanW.overview: Clean tools thoroughly with water after use. Store in a cool and dry place: min. 12 months in the original container. Promptly use opened containers.
points: {AQ1KP}: store frost-free
protect surfaces that are not to be treated

planC.title: Assess the wall and the water
planC.short: Where the concrete lets water through: joints, honeycombs, tie holes; WTA 4-6 — water pressure sets ≥ 3.0 mm dry film.
planC.overview: Retroactive waterproofing from the inside in accordance with WTA datasheet 4-6: {RB400} and {AQ1K} withstand negative pressing water up to 0.75 bar. The material rate table of {RB400} for WTA 4-6: soil moisture and non-percolating water ≥ 2.0 mm dry film (≥ 2.4 kg/m²), water pressure ≥ 3.0 mm (≥ 3.6 kg/m²); transitions of concrete components without a tape ≥ 4.0 mm. Concrete lets water through where it is not dense — construction joints, honeycombing, tie holes — and along cracks.
points: {RB400} is flexible and crack-bridging (> 2 mm after PG MDS/FPD) and radon-tight — the choice for a concrete wall that may still move
moisture penetration from the rear must be kept off the flexible coating: pre-seal with {AQ1K} (RB400 data sheet)
water-bearing cracks are sealed first by injection — see the guide “Crack sealing / injection resins”
{AQ1K} in three application steps is the rigid alternative for substrates not prone to cracking

prepC.title: Lay the concrete bare
prepC.short: Old paint, lime runs and laitance off by high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar); honeycombs broken out to sound concrete; matt damp.
prepC.overview: A load-bearing substrate is the precondition for a lasting bond: less adhesive and bond-damaging substances — old coatings, lime leaching, laitance — are removed completely. High-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar, < 2000 bar) and jets with fixed blasting agents are suitable; the last step is cleaning with pressure water jetting. Honeycombed zones are broken out to sound, dense concrete; the substrate is even, pore open, sealed in the surface and matt damp at the time of application.
points: requirement: load-bearing, even, pore open, sealed in the surface, free of adhesion inhibiting substances
pre-moisten a dry substrate so that it is matt damp; the formation of puddles must be avoided
in poorly ventilated rooms provide adequate ventilation

repairC.title: Fill the defects, form the sealing cove
repairC.short: Honeycombs, tie holes and the chased construction joint filled with ASOCRET-M30; cove of ASOCRET-M30 on an AQUAFIN-1K bonding slurry.
repairC.overview: Depressions > 5 mm, mortar pockets, damaged areas and large-pored substrates are levelled in advance with {M30} (3–30 mm in one step). At the base slab–wall transition: pre-screen with {AQ1K} or {M30} in a consistency that is able to screen and, while still wet, install a sealing cove of {M30} with an edge height of at least 4 cm; after drying carry out the waterproofing.
points: {M30}: watertight multi-mortar, water 4.5–5.25 l per 25 kg, pot life approx. 45 minutes, overcoat after approx. 3 hours
edges are to be chamfered and corners rounded
the construction joint: chased, cleaned and filled flush; the joint band of {RB400} follows over it

presealC.title: Pre-seal with AQUAFIN-1K
presealC.short: One coat of AQUAFIN-1K brushed into the matt damp concrete — the rigid slurry keeps the moisture from the rear off the flexible coating.
presealC.overview: Moisture penetration from the rear and intermittent moisture loading from the negative side must be kept off {RB400}; for waterproofing with moisture penetration from the rear, pre-sealing with {AQ1K} is recommended (RB400 data sheet). {AQ1K} is applied by brush into the matt damp substrate, up to 1 mm per step, approx. 1.75 kg/m² per mm; overcoat after approx. 6 hours.
points: {AQ1K}: watertight against negative pressing water up to 0.75 bar (WTA 4-6)
an application thickness of more than 2 kg/m² in one step can lead to cracking
pot life approx. 60 minutes; clean tools with water

jointC.title: Waterproof the construction joint
jointC.short: AQUAFIN-RB400 at least 15 cm on both sides of the joint, two steps with the 6–8 mm notched trowel, smoothed: 4.0 mm dry film.
jointC.overview: Transitions of watertight concrete building components with an immersion depth of up to 3 m (max. opening width 1.0 mm): apply the waterproofing to the prepared substrate to a minimum of 15 cm on both sides of the joint; processing in two application steps, total dry film thickness 4 mm; an even layer thickness is achieved using a 6 to 8 mm notched trowel and then smoothing. Alternatively the transition is sealed with the ASO-Dichtband system (then ≥ 2.5 mm).
points: the joint band lies under the two full-area coats
construction joints, horizontal and vertical, as well as intersections of waterproof and other concrete components

coatC1.title: Apply the first coat of AQUAFIN-RB400
coatC1.short: Trowel or brush over wall and floor strip, free of pores; even thickness with the coating-thickness trowel, then smoothing.
coatC1.overview: Apply {RB400} in a minimum of two application steps ensuring it is free of pores. An even layer thickness is achieved using a coating thickness trowel or notched trowel and then smoothing. The material rate depends on the required dry film thickness (WTA 4-6: ≥ 3.0 mm for water pressure, ≥ 2.0 mm for soil moisture).
points: approx. 1.1 mm wet film per 1 mm dry film; approx. 1.2 kg/m² per mm dry
the second application step when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking — after approx. 3 hours
pot life approx. 45 minutes; do not add more water than max. 0.24 l per 24 kg

coatC2.title: Apply the second coat to the class
coatC2.short: When the first can no longer be damaged; spray or trowel, smoothed; ≥ 3.0 mm dry film in total for water pressure (WTA 4-6).
coatC2.overview: The second (and following) application step takes place when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking. Water pressure from the negative side (WTA 4-6): ≥ 3.0 mm dry film, ≥ 3.6 kg/m²; soil moisture and non-percolating water: ≥ 2.0 mm, ≥ 2.4 kg/m². {RB400} can be sprayed; the fresh coat is smoothed with the flat trowel.
points: rainproof after approx. 3 hours, resistant to 1 bar pressurised water after approx. 16 hours
watertight against negative pressing water to 0.75 bar

cureC.title: Keep damp, protect
cureC.short: In dry rooms keep the coating damp for at least 3 days; ventilate deep pits for 24 hours; no condensation, no direct heating.
cureC.overview: The material cures very well in areas with high humidity. In relatively dry areas, keep the coating damp for at least 3 days. In poorly ventilated rooms and deep pits, adequate ventilation should be provided for 24 hours; dropping below the dew point (condensation) on the surface is avoided with condensation dryers. Direct heating or uncontrolled blowing of warm air is not permitted.
points: foot traffic after approx. 24 hours; withstands pressurised water after ≥ 1 day
a plaster, tiles or a coating may follow on the cured waterproofing when the room is to be finished

planT.title: Determine the container class
planT.short: DIN 18535: W1-B fill level ≤ 5 m, W2-B ≤ 10 m; crack width < 0.2 mm: 2.0 mm dry film; < 1.0 mm: 4.0 mm.
planT.overview: The water exposure class of a container depends on the filling level: W1-B ≤ 5 m, W2-B ≤ 10 m, W3-B > 10 m. {RB400}: W2-B with crack width < 0.2 mm ≥ 2.0 mm dry film (≥ 2.4 kg/m²); crack width < 1.0 mm ≥ 4.0 mm (≥ 4.8 kg/m², special agreement necessary). {AQ2K} and {AQ1K}: tanks and pools > 2.0 mm, 3.5 kg/m².
points: {AQ1K}: W1-B, process and waste water tanks, repair of sulphate-damaged substrates; {AQ2K}: W1-B and W2-B, resistant to chlorinated water; {RB400}: W1-B and W2-B
in containers or with aggressive or soft water (hardness < 30 mg CaO per l) a water analysis is always required; the degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1
when used in swimming pool surrounds the pool water must comply with DIN 19643 ({AQ2K})
the specifications of the general building authority test certificates for MDS and FPD must be observed

prepT.title: Jet clean, repair, smooth
prepT.short: High-pressure water jetting; cracks repaired, voids levelled with ASOCRET-BIS-5/40 on ASOCRET-HS-FLEX, smoothed with ASOCRET-BIS-1/6.
prepT.overview: System “Process water containers”: cracks are assessed and sealed; voids are levelled with {BIS540} (up to 40 mm in one application) on an {HSF} bonding coat wet in wet; the surface is smoothed with {BIS16} (max. 6 mm per layer) and finished with a felt or sponge board. Then the substrate is even, load-bearing, pore open and matt damp.
points: high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar); the last step is cleaning with pressure water
in the case of substrates damaged by de-icing salt, remove down to the neutral area (milling)
water-bearing cracks are injected first — see the guide “Crack sealing / injection resins”
the concrete restoration system is described in the guide “Concrete restoration”

joint.title: Seal the wall–floor junction and the joints
joint.short: AQUAFIN-RB400 at the junction, ASO-Dichtband-2000-S bonded without voids or folds, overcoated 15 cm on both sides.
joint.overview: At wall–floor transitions and connecting joints, {RB400} is applied and the joint sealing tape ASO-Dichtband-2000-S is bonded without voids or folds. Transitions of watertight concrete components (immersion depth ≤ 3 m, opening ≤ 1.0 mm): waterproofing 15 cm on both sides of the joint in two steps to 4 mm dry film with a 6–8 mm notched trowel; or the bonded joint sealing tape overcoated at least 15 cm on both sides, minimum dry film thickness 2.5 mm.
points: alternatively a sealing cove of {M30} (edge height 4–6 cm) on a bonding slurry of {AQ1K} or {M30}
for movement and connecting joints use the ASO-Dichtband system components in accordance with their technical data sheets
floor drains and intersections must be provided with suitable flange elements

coatT1.title: Apply the first coat
coatT1.short: Spray, brush or trowel over walls and floor, free of pores; an even thickness with the coating-thickness trowel.
coatT1.overview: Apply the waterproofing in a minimum of two application steps ensuring it is free of pores. An even layer thickness is achieved using a coating thickness trowel or notched trowel and then smoothing. System “Process water containers”: minimum two coats of {RB400} by spray, brush or trowel across all surfaces.
points: {RB400}: mix ratio 1.5 : 1, mixing 3 minutes, maturing 5 minutes, pot life approx. 45 minutes
{AQ2K}: mix ratio 2.5 : 1, pot life approx. 60 minutes, max. 1 mm per step
{AQ1K}: approx. 6.7 l water per 25 kg, pot life approx. 60 minutes, max. 1 mm per step

coatT2.title: Apply the second coat
coatT2.short: When the first coat can no longer be damaged: RB400 after approx. 3 h, 2K/M-PLUS 3–6 h, 1K 6 h.
coatT2.overview: The second application step can be carried out when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking: {RB400} after approx. 3 hours, {AQ2K} after approx. 3–6 hours, {AQ1K} after approx. 6 hours. The total dry film thickness follows from the container class and the crack width.
points: an application thickness of more than 2 kg/m² in one step can lead to cracking ({AQ1K}, {AQ2K})
the waterproofing as a surface coating must not be exposed to point or linear loads

cureT.title: Cure before filling
cureT.short: Keep damp; avoid condensation with dryers; pressurised water after ≥ 1 day (RB400) or ≥ 7 days (1K, 2K/M-PLUS).
cureT.overview: In service water tanks temperatures around +10 to +15 °C are usually expected: to ensure complete hydration of the cement the coating is kept damp for a sufficiently long period (constant relative humidity > 80 %) and protected against drying — 7 days are generally sufficient ({AQ1K}). {RB400} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 1 day (1 bar after approx. 16 hours), {AQ1K} and {AQ2K} after ≥ 7 days.
points: dropping below the dew point (condensation) on the surface must be avoided with condensation dryers; direct heating or uncontrolled blowing warm air is not permitted
the waterproofing must not be affected by water during binding
{RB400}: in relatively dry areas keep the coating damp for at least 3 days; ventilate poorly ventilated rooms for 24 hours

fill.title: Fill the container
fill.short: After curing; with aggressive or soft water a water analysis is required.
fill.overview: The container is filled after the waiting times of the technical data sheet. If applied in containers or in case of water loading with aggressive or soft water featuring hardness < 30 mg CaO per l, a water analysis is always required; the degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1.
points: resistant to concrete-damaging water in accordance with DIN 4030 (XA2)
{AQ2K}: resistant to contact with chlorinated water; pool water in accordance with DIN 19643

planB.title: Bonded waterproofing: class and thickness
planB.short: DIN 18534 W0-I to W3-I and DIN 18531: > 2.0 mm dry film, approx. 3.5 kg/m² plus 25 % allowance.
planB.overview: {AQ2K} as bonded waterproofing with tiles and boards for water impact classes W0-I to W3-I (DIN 18534) and for balconies, loggias, arcades (DIN 18531) and terraces: dry film thickness > 2.0 mm, wet film approx. 2.2 mm, consumption 3.5 kg/m². Possible additional consumption on uneven substrates must be considered: a thickness allowance of at least 25 % in accordance with DIN 18531, 18534, 18535.
points: W3-I: surfaces around swimming pool perimeters, showers in sports facilities, industrial kitchens and laundries

system components after AbP AIV: joint sealing tapes ASO-Dichtband-2000, -2000-S, corners, sleeves ASO-Dichtmanschette-Boden/-Wand; tile adhesives AK7P, ASODUR-EKF, CRISTALLIT-FLEX, LIGHTFLEX, MONOFLEX (-fast, -FB, -white, -XL), SOLOFLEX, UNIFIX-S3 (-fast)
relevant regulations: DIN 18531, DIN 18534, DIN 18535

prepB.title: Prepare the substrate, prime
prepB.short: Even, load-bearing, fully grouted; highly absorbent substrates primed with ASO-Unigrund; depressions levelled; matt damp.
prepB.overview: Requirement for the substrate: even, free of adhesion inhibiting substances, sealed in the surface, pore open, load-bearing, extensively fully grouted. Highly absorbent and slightly sanding substrates must be primed with ASO-Unigrund-GE, -K, -S or -PLUS; the primer must have reacted fully before the subsequent work steps. Pre-moisten the dry substrate so that it is matt damp at the time of application.
points: suitable substrates: concrete, masonry work, plasters P II and P III, cement-based screed, old firmly adhering bituminous substrates
depressions > 5 mm and uneven substrates are levelled with {M30}; on uneven substrates pre-sealing can also take place with {M30}
in the case of substrates damaged by de-icing salt, remove down to the neutral area (milling)
moisture penetration from the rear and intermittent moisture loading from the negative side must be avoided

tape.title: Insert the joint sealing tapes and sleeves
tape.short: ASO-Dichtband-2000 system in the wall–floor joint, corners and sleeves, bonded in AQUAFIN-2K/M-PLUS.
tape.overview: Use the ASO-Dichtband-2000 system along with the required pre-formed pieces to form movement and connecting joints as well as to integrate intersections and assembly parts. Bond joint sealing tapes, joint-tape edges or connections with the waterproofing material and fill in the overlap area and the edge zone with filler.
points: in the area of structural movement joints the waterproofing is reinforced with ADF-Dehnfugenband or ASO-Dichtband-2000-S
floor drains and intersections must be provided with suitable flange elements; check linear drainage systems for suitability in advance
on PVC, gunmetal and stainless steel flanges, ASO-Dichtmanschetten or ADF-Pipe-Gasket are installed without voids or wrinkles

mix2K.title: Mix AQUAFIN-2K/M-PLUS
mix2K.short: 50–60 % of the liquid first, powder in, the rest of the liquid; 3 minutes; mature; homogenise.
mix2K.overview: Fill approx. 50–60 % of the liquid component into a clean mixing bucket and mix with the powder component to produce a homogeneous, lump-free mass. Finally add the rest of the liquid component and mix sufficiently. Mix ratio A : B = 2.5 : 1 by weight. The mixing time is approx. 3 minutes; after a settling period of approx. 5 minutes, thoroughly homogenise the compound again.
points: depending on the application technique (slurry and spray technique) add max. 0.5 l water per 35 kg, after mixing
pot life approx. 60 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C
wet film thickness approx. 1.1 mm yields 1 mm dry film thickness

coatB1.title: Apply the first coat of AQUAFIN-2K/M-PLUS
coatB1.short: Trowel, brush or spray; up to 1 mm per step, free of pores; even thickness with the notched trowel, then smoothing.
coatB1.overview: Apply {AQ2K} in a minimum of two application steps ensuring it is free of pores. Max. layer thickness per application step: up to 1 mm. An even layer thickness is achieved using a coating thickness trowel or notched trowel and then smoothing.
points: consumption bonded with tiles/boards: > 2.0 mm dry film, approx. 2.2 mm wet, 3.5 kg/m²
can be trowelled off; machine application after Technical Information No. 43
in case of strong sunlight work against the movement of the sun in shaded areas

coatB2.title: Apply the second coat after approx. 3–6 hours
coatB2.short: To > 2.0 mm total dry film thickness; never more than 2 kg/m² in one step.
coatB2.overview: The second application step (and subsequent ones) can be carried out after approx. 3–6 hours. An application thickness of more than 2 kg/m² in one application step can lead to cracking.
points: foot traffic after approx. 24 hours
the waterproofing layer must be completely hardened at the time of the laying work

tiles.title: Lay the tiles
tiles.short: With one of the tile adhesives of the system list, after the waterproofing has completely hardened.
tiles.overview: Tiles or boards are laid with one of the tile adhesives listed in the system components section (e.g. MONOFLEX, SOLOFLEX, UNIFIX-S3, CRISTALLIT-FLEX, LIGHTFLEX). The waterproofing layer must be completely hardened at the time of the laying work.
points: apply the sealing sleeves in accordance with their technical data sheet; floor drains and intersections with suitable flange elements
the waterproofing as a surface coating must not be exposed to point or linear loads
frost, de-icing salt, UV and age resistant

joints.title: Grout, form the movement joints
joints.short: Movement and connecting joints with the ASO-Dichtband system and an elastic sealant; the coating may be plastered or painted.
joints.overview: Movement and connecting joints are formed with the ASO-Dichtband-2000 system. Where it stays exposed, {AQ2K} may be plastered and coated with vapour permeable, solvent-free dispersion facade paints or dispersion silicate paints (not pure silicate paints); silicon resin and acrylate-based paints may also be used.
points: tile grouts and joint sealants of the SCHOMBURG tile system — see the product group “Tile / Natural Stone / Screed Installation”

planP.title: OS 5b surface protection
planP.short: Underground garages and car parks: chloride and carbonation barrier, crack bridging at −20 °C, approx. 5.5 kg/m².
planP.overview: {OS} is the approved surface protection system according to OS 5b and EN 1504-2 for underground garages and multi-storey car parks: a protective coating against chloride attack and carbonation, for the renovation and protection of concrete surfaces prone to cracking. Consumption after OS 5b and EN 1504-2: approx. 5.5 kg/m².
points: crack bridging DIN EN 1062-7: static class A4 (2.0 mm) at +20 °C; dynamic class B2 at −20 °C and after 2000 h of UV weathering
water vapour permeability class I (Sd > 50 m); CO₂ permeability Sd > 200 m
suitable substrate: concrete with a tensile adhesion strength of 1.5 N/mm²

prepP.title: Prepare the deck
prepP.short: Salt-damaged concrete milled off to the neutral zone, blasted or jetted, matt damp; primed where very absorbent.
prepP.overview: Requirement for the substrate: even, free of adhesion inhibiting substances, sealed in the surface, pore open, load-bearing, extensively fully grouted. In the case of substrates damaged by de-icing salt, the substrate must be removed down to the neutral area, e.g. by milling. Pre-moisten the dry substrate so that it is matt damp at the time of application.
points: extremely absorbent and slightly sandy substrates must be primed with {PRIM}
moisture penetration from the rear and intermittent moisture loading from the negative side must be avoided
the concrete restoration of the deck (breakouts, reinforcement) follows the guide “Concrete restoration”

mixOS.title: Mix AQUAFIN-OS
mixOS.short: Liquid component into the bucket, powder in, 3 minutes; mature 2 minutes; homogenise again.
mixOS.overview: Put the liquid component into a clean mixing bucket and mix with the powder component to produce a homogeneous, lump-free mass (mix ratio A : B = 2 : 1 by weight). The mixing time is approx. 3 minutes. After a settling period of approx. 2 minutes, thoroughly homogenise the compound again.
points: stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm with a suitable mixing paddle
pot life approx. 30 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C

scratch.title: Scratch coat and contact layer
scratch.short: AQUAFIN-OS pressed into the substrate with the trowel before the first layer.
scratch.overview: Apply {OS} as a scratch coat and contact layer before the first application. Immediately afterwards, the first layer of sealant is applied wet on wet.
points: the scratch coat closes pores and blowholes and gives the contact to the concrete
tools: trowel, serrated or layer-thickness trowel, flat trowel, brush, spray equipment

coatP1.title: First layer wet in wet
coatP1.short: Immediately after the scratch coat; up to 3 mm per application step, approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm.
coatP1.overview: Immediately after the scratch coat, the first layer of {OS} is applied wet on wet. Max. layer thickness per application step: up to 3 mm; consumption approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm.
points: can be trowelled off and applied with a brush; machine application after Technical Information No. 43
protect surfaces that are not to be treated; in strong sunlight work in shaded areas

coatP2.title: Second layer after approx. 3 hours
coatP2.short: When the first layer can no longer be damaged; total approx. 5.5 kg/m² for OS 5b.
coatP2.overview: The second application step (and following) can take place when the first application step can no longer be damaged by reworking — overcoat after approx. 3 hours. The waiting time between layers depends on temperature, humidity and other ambient conditions. Total consumption after OS 5b and EN 1504-2: approx. 5.5 kg/m².
points: rainproof after 4 hours
the waterproofing must not be affected by water during binding

cureP.title: Protect, then open to traffic
cureP.short: Rainproof after 4 hours; no point or linear loads on the coating; may be painted with vapour permeable paints.
cureP.overview: {OS} as a surface coating must not be exposed to point or linear loads. It may be coated with vapour permeable, solvent-free dispersion facade paints or dispersion silicate paints; silicon resin and acrylate-based paints may also be used.
points: direct contact with metals such as copper, zinc and aluminium is avoided by a pore-sealed primer of ASODUR-GBM in two steps
the completed OS 5b system protects against chloride ingress and carbonation and bridges cracks at −20 °C

ext.name: Basement wall in ground contact, from the outside
ext.problem: Ground moisture, seepage water and — with poorly permeable subsoil or backwater — pressing water act on the outside of the basement wall and on the wall–slab joint (DIN 18533: W1.1-E, W1.2-E, W2.1-E; W4-E at the wall base).
ext.solution: The system “External waterproofing to basements — mineral-based”: substrate levelled with {M30}, sealing cove of {M30} on a bonding slurry of {AQ1K}, pipe penetrations with the sleeve, two coats of {RB400} to the dry film thickness of the class (2.0–4.0 mm), protection and drainage boards bonded with {RB400} and quartz sand, backfilled.

inner.name: Retroactive waterproofing from the inside, WTA 4-6
inner.problem: An existing basement wall takes up water from the soil behind it: damp patches, salt efflorescence, plaster falling off, water pressing from the negative side. The outside cannot be reached.
inner.solution: The classic system: plaster removed, joints raked out and levelled with {M30}, sealing fillet, a retroactive horizontal barrier with {I380} or {AQF}, then {AQ1K} in two application steps — three for pressing water (up to 0.75 bar from the negative side) — and the restoration plaster system THERMOPAL. {AQ1KP} when the next coat cannot wait; {RB400} for substrates prone to cracking and for radon.

negc.name: Concrete basement wall, from the inside
negc.problem: An existing in-situ concrete basement wall lets water through where the concrete is not dense: a construction joint with lime leaching and seepage, honeycombing at the base, formwork tie holes; the old paint flakes off. The outside cannot be dug up, so the waterproofing has to hold pressing water from the negative side (WTA 4-6, up to 0.75 bar).
negc.solution: Substrate laid bare by high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar), honeycombs broken out to sound concrete and filled with {M30}, the joint chased and filled, sealing cove of {M30}; pre-sealing with {AQ1K} against moisture from the rear; the construction joint with {RB400} 15 cm on both sides to ≥ 4.0 mm; then two coats of {RB400} to ≥ 3.0 mm dry film (WTA 4-6, water pressure) — flexible, crack-bridging and radon-tight; kept damp while it cures. {AQ1K} in three application steps is the rigid alternative for substrates not prone to cracking.

tank.name: Tanks, basins and process water containers
tank.problem: Concrete tanks hold water permanently (DIN 18535: W1-B fill level ≤ 5 m, W2-B ≤ 10 m): leaching, cracks, voids and honeycombs let water through; process, waste or soft water attacks the concrete.
tank.solution: The system “Process water containers”: jet-cleaned, cracks sealed, voids re-profiled with {BIS540} on {HSF}, smoothed with {BIS16}; the wall–floor junction with {RB400} and ASO-Dichtband-2000-S; two coats of {RB400} (2.0 mm dry film for crack widths < 0.2 mm, 4.0 mm for < 1.0 mm); pressurised water after ≥ 1 day. Alternatives: {AQ2K} where chlorinated water is involved, {AQ1K} for process and waste water tanks.

balcony.name: Balcony and terrace: bonded waterproofing under tiles
balcony.problem: Rain, standing water and frost act on the balcony slab (DIN 18531) and on the wall–floor joint; the slab moves and cracks; tiles are laid directly on the waterproofing (DIN 18534, W0-I to W3-I).
balcony.solution: {AQ2K} as bonded waterproofing: substrate levelled with {M30} and primed with ASO-Unigrund, ASO-Dichtband-2000 tapes and sleeves in the joints, two coats to > 2.0 mm dry film (3.5 kg/m² plus 25 % allowance), crack bridging even at −5 °C; the tiles follow with the tile adhesives of the system list when the waterproofing has hardened.

park.name: Car park deck: OS 5b surface protection
park.problem: De-icing salt, chlorides, carbonation and moving cracks attack the trafficked concrete of underground garages and multi-storey car parks; the reinforcement corrodes once the chlorides reach it.
park.solution: {OS}, the approved OS 5b system after EN 1504-2: substrate milled to the neutral zone and prepared, a scratch coat and the first layer wet in wet, the second layer after approx. 3 hours, approx. 5.5 kg/m² in total. Chloride and CO₂ barrier, crack bridging class A4 static and B2 dynamic at −20 °C, UV resistant.

level: depressions > 5 mm, joints and uneven masonry levelled; edges chamfered, corners rounded
cove: on a bonding slurry of {AQ1K} or {M30}, wet in wet, rounded
sleeve: sleeve bonded in {RB400} with the 4 mm notched trowel, free from folds, fully overcoated
c1: brush, trowel or spray, free of pores; even thickness with the coating-thickness trowel
approx. 1.1 mm wet per 1 mm dry
A 1.5 : B 1, max. 0.24 l water / 24 kg
c2: when the first can no longer be damaged; to the dry film thickness of the class
rainproof after approx. 3 h, 1 bar after approx. 16 h, boards after ≥ 1 day
board: bonded with {RB400} + quartz sand 0.1–0.35 mm (approx. 6 kg per 24 kg), buttering-floating
spot or full-area bonding by class
levelI: joints raked out approx. 20 mm and filled, depressions levelled, fillet at the wall–floor joint
approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm; fillet approx. 3 kg/m
barrier: injection cream in a row of drill holes, holes resealed with {M30}
c1i: brush, trowel or spray into the matt damp substrate, free of pores
second coat after approx. 6 h ({AQ1KP}: 90 min)
c2i: when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking
third coat for pressing water, else curing
c3i: classic system: three layers for pressure water; > 3.0 mm in total
plaster: THERMOPAL-SP splatterdash, THERMOPAL-SR24, optional THERMOPAL-FS33 finish
repair: {BIS540} on {HSF} for voids, {BIS16} for the surface, felt finish (guide “Concrete restoration”)
tape: ASO-Dichtband-2000-S in {RB400} at the wall–floor junction and construction joints, no voids or folds
≥ 2.5 mm dry film over the tape
c1t: spray, brush or trowel over walls and floor, free of pores
approx. 1.1 mm wet per 1 mm dry
c2t: to the dry film thickness of the container class and the crack width
pressurised water after ≥ 1 day; keep damp
levelB: depressions > 5 mm with {M30}; highly absorbent substrates primed with ASO-Unigrund
tapeB: ASO-Dichtband-2000 tapes, corners and sleeves bonded in {AQ2K}
c1b: trowel, brush or spray, free of pores; even thickness with the notched trowel
A 2.5 : B 1, max. 0.5 l water / 35 kg
c2b: never more than 2 kg/m² in one step
tiles: laid with a tile adhesive of the system list (MONOFLEX, SOLOFLEX, UNIFIX-S3 …)
prim: {PRIM} where the substrate is extremely absorbent or slightly sandy; matt damp otherwise
fully reacted before the scratch coat
scratch: {OS} pressed into the substrate as contact layer
in the total of approx. 5.5 kg/m²
c1p: wet in wet on the scratch coat
c2p: when the first can no longer be damaged
repairC: honeycombs broken out to sound concrete and filled, tie holes filled, the construction joint chased and filled with {M30}; cove at the wall–floor joint on a bonding slurry of {AQ1K}
approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm; cove approx. 3 kg/m

F20.role: The plugging mortar of the system: pressed by hand into the dovetailed opening where the water runs, it solidifies after 1–2 minutes — even under water — with a clearly noticeable warming, and swells against the concrete. Under high water pressure it fixes the drain hose that relieves the pressure while the leak is plugged around it.

for sealing water-bearing holes, cracks, fissures in concrete, masonry work and natural stone structures
