planR.title: Assess the water and the concrete
planR.short: Water load sets the material rate; water quality, cracks and what may follow on the coating are checked first.
planR.overview: The material rate of {IC} follows the water load: 0.75 kg/m² in one layer for soil moisture and non-accumulating seepage water, 1.2 kg/m² in two layers for non-pressurised water, 1.5 kg/m² in two layers for accumulated water. The slurry is watertight against negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar and to 14 bar on the positive side (CRD-C 48-92); it is suitable for drinking water (DVGW W 270, W 347).
points: static cracks and construction joints wider than 0.4 mm are opened to 20 mm width and 25 mm depth and repaired with {IM}; dynamic cracks are not filled with mortar
water ingress is stopped in advance with {F20} (or FIX 10-S plugging cement); voids are repaired with the ASOCRET-BIS system or {IM}
aggressive or soft water (hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre) always requires a water analysis; the degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1
{IC} cannot be overcoated with tiles, plaster, bonded screeds or paint, and cannot be used as an additive to concrete or plaster
concrete with fly ash: discolouration or a reduced reaction may occur — contact the technical service; different colouring depends on the moisture content of the concrete
movement and connecting joints are formed watertight with ASO-Dichtband system components

prepR.title: Prepare the substrate
prepR.short: Firm, load-bearing, pore open, absorbent; smooth areas roughened; jetted at > 400 bar; wetted repeatedly to matt damp.
prepR.overview: The substrate must be firm, load-bearing, pore open, free of adhesion inhibiting substances and absorbent. Smooth surface areas are mechanically roughened to achieve a good penetration depth. Less adhesive and bond-damaging substances are completely removed: high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar) and jets with fixed blasting agents are suitable; the last step is cleaning with pressure water jetting.
points: dampen the surfaces to be sealed with clean water beforehand; repeated moistening alters the absorption behaviour and favours the growth of the crystals
the surface must be matt damp at the time of application; the formation of puddles must be avoided
dense and smooth substrates for {IM} are roughened with sand, high-pressure water or shot blasting
for {F20}: loose pieces of plaster and masonry removed; the leak position chiselled to a dovetail for better anchoring

openR.title: Open cracks and damaged areas
openR.short: Static cracks and joints chased to 20 mm wide and 25 mm deep; loose debris removed; leaks chiselled to a dovetail.
openR.overview: Loose debris is removed from the cracked areas. Defective construction joints and visible static cracks over 0.4 mm are opened to a width of up to 20 mm and a depth of 25 mm so that {IM} can fill them flush. Where water runs out, the opening is chiselled to a dovetail shape for the better anchoring of the {F20} plug.
points: crack width 20 mm, depth 25 mm (system page: at least 20 mm and 25 mm)
the chased edges are screened with {IC} before the mortar goes in
voids and honeycombs are broken out to sound concrete and filled with {F20} or {IM}, larger ones with the ASOCRET-BIS system

mixF20.title: Mix FIX-20-T
mixF20.short: Approx. 200–250 g of water per kg, mixed for at least a minute in small quantities: pot life approx. 2 minutes.
mixF20.overview: Pour approx. 200–250 g of water per kg of {F20} with the powder component into a clean mixing bucket and mix to a homogeneous, lump-free mass. Solidification starts after 1–2 minutes and the pot life is approx. 2 minutes — mix only what can be placed at once.
points: mixing time at least approx. 1 minute; protective gloves
at low temperatures use warm water and pre-warmed powder; at high temperatures cool water and cooled powder — the powder must not exceed +23 °C
the material can be used as mortar or alternatively in dry form
appropriate preliminary tests must be carried out; {F20} must not be mixed with plaster or brought into contact with plaster

plugR.title: Plug the water leak
plugR.short: A plug of FIX-20-T pressed into the dovetailed opening by hand and held until it hardens — after 1–2 minutes, with a noticeable warming.
plugR.overview: Form plugs with the mortar and press them into the area where the water runs; hold by hand until the material has hardened. Hardening is preceded by a clearly noticeable warming. The plugged area is trowelled smooth immediately. {F20} solidifies even under water and swells against the concrete: chloride-free, with a strong bond and free of corrosion-promoting substances.
points: consumption approx. 2 kg per litre of void
compressive strength approx. 3 N/mm² after 1 hour, approx. 15 N/mm² after 24 hours, approx. 30 N/mm² after 28 days
protect surfaces that are not to be treated from the effects of {F20}

drainR.title: Set a drain under high water pressure
drainR.short: A hose set in the strongest flow and fixed with FIX-20-T relieves the pressure; the hole is plugged after the hose is removed.
drainR.overview: If the water pressure is high, a drain is installed using water hoses or pipes: the water pressure is minimised, which makes tamping easier. A depression is chiselled out in the area of the strongest water flow, the hose or pipe is fixed in place with {F20} mortar and the surrounding leak is plugged. After drying the hose is removed and the hole is plugged with mortar as described.
points: the drain runs while the joint around it is plugged with {F20}
remove the hose or pipe after drying; plug the hose hole with a {F20} plug pressed in by hand
the plugged areas are afterwards made good with {IM} and coated with {IC}

mixIM.title: Mix ASOCRET-IM
mixIM.short: 3.75–4.25 l of water per 25 kg, approx. 3 minutes to a homogeneous, lump-free filler consistency; pot life approx. 30 minutes.
mixIM.overview: Add water (3.75–4.25 l per 25 kg) to a clean mixing bucket and mix with 25 kg of the powder component to produce a homogeneous, lump-free mass of filler consistency. Stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm with a suitable mixing paddle.
points: mixing time approx. 3 minutes; pot life approx. 30 minutes at approx. 5–30 °C
grain size < 1 mm; up to 10 mm per application step
rinse tools with water immediately after use

fillR.title: Fill the cracks and holes with ASOCRET-IM
fillR.short: Edges screened with AQUAFIN-IC, the chased crack filled flush with ASOCRET-IM wet in wet, up to 10 mm per step.
fillR.overview: Structural cracks prised open to approx. 20 mm width and 25 mm depth: the edges are screened with {IC} and sealed wet in wet with {IM} flush with the surface. {IM} can be applied with a layer thickness of up to 10 mm per application step. The mortar is capillary active and supports the self-repair of the concrete; it must be protected against rapid water removal.
points: consumption approx. 1.3 kg per metre of U-shaped crack (20 × 25 mm); approx. 1.7 kg/m² per mm of layer
after approx. 1–3 hours the mortar is reworked with {IC}; if this is not possible during this period, the surface is roughened after total hardening and then coated
faulty areas and voids are repaired with {F20} or alternatively {IM}; larger voids with the ASOCRET-BIS system
do not use on frozen substrates; the reaction with the free lime of the concrete can result in slight efflorescence — not a defect, brushed off

coveR.title: Form the coved fillet
coveR.short: ASOCRET-IM on a screen of AQUAFIN-IC, wet in wet, edge height approx. 4 cm, rounded; AQUAFIN-IC over it after 1–3 hours.
coveR.overview: The substrate at the wall–floor joint is screened with {IC}; the {IM} is then applied wet in wet with an edge height of approx. 4 cm in a rounded form. After approx. 1–3 hours the fillet is reworked with {IC}. If this is not possible during this period, the surface is roughened after total hardening and then coated.
points: consumption approx. 1.3 kg per metre (edge height 38 mm)
pointing trowel; the fillet is protected against rapid water removal
the fillet forms part of the crystalline system: {IM} is capillary active with increased crack healing

mixIC.title: Mix AQUAFIN-IC
mixIC.short: 6.75–8 l of water per 25 kg, stirred vigorously for approx. 3 minutes, matured, mixed again; pot life approx. 60 minutes.
mixIC.overview: Depending on the desired consistency, pour 6.75–8 l of water per 25 kg into a clean mixing bucket and add enough powder while stirring vigorously until the mortar is homogeneous and clump-free (approx. 27–32 % water). After a maturing time of approx. 3–5 minutes mix again.
points: stirrer approx. 500–700 rpm with a suitable mixing paddle
pot life approx. 60 minutes at a substrate and application temperature of approx. 5–30 °C
liquid consistency; density approx. 1.6 kg/dm³
for spraying see Technical Information No. 43

coatR1.title: Brush in the first coat
coatR1.short: AQUAFIN-IC brushed evenly into the matt damp concrete with the wide brush or broom, or sprayed, free of pores.
coatR1.overview: The surfaces are dampened once more with clean water so that they are matt damp without puddles; {IC} is applied in a minimum of two application steps, ensuring it is free of pores, brushed evenly and worked into the substrate meticulously. Consumption approx. 1 kg per m² and mm.
points: wide brush, roofer’s broom or spray equipment; machine application after Technical Information No. 43
brush the slurry into the chased and filled details and over the fresh fillet as well (after 1–3 hours)
protect surfaces that are not to be treated from the effects of {IC}

coatR2.title: Apply the second coat wet in sticky
coatR2.short: The second coat while the first is still sticky and has not dried out; to the material rate of the water load.
coatR2.overview: Apply the second layer while the first layer is still sticky and has not yet dried out: drying of the first layer must be avoided. The total rate follows the water load: 0.75 kg/m² in one layer for soil moisture and non-accumulating seepage water; 1.2 kg/m² in two layers for non-pressurised water; 1.5 kg/m² in two layers for accumulated water.
points: increased material consumption for uneven surfaces is excluded from these rates
foot traffic after approx. 5 hours; withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days
movement and connecting joints: ASO-Dichtband system components in accordance with their data sheets

cureR.title: Keep the coating damp
cureR.short: Protected from sun, wind, rain and frost for ≥ 24 hours; kept damp for ≥ 3 days from the day after application — jute sheets, water mist.
cureR.overview: The fresh coating is protected against weathering influences for ≥ 24 hours. The waterproofing layer must be kept damp for ≥ 3 days: the initial dampening takes place one day after application and is repeated at set intervals; in case of strong solar radiation or wind, water-soaked jute sheets are recommended. The material cures very well in areas with high humidity; in relatively dry areas the coating is kept damp for at least 3 days.
points: in poorly ventilated rooms and deep pits adequate ventilation is provided for 24 hours

in rooms with high humidity or insufficient ventilation (e.g. water containers) dropping below the dew point can occur on the surface: avoid it with condensation dryers — direct heating or uncontrolled blowing of warm air is not permitted
in service water tanks at approx. +10 to +15 °C the coating is kept damp at a constant relative humidity > 80 % and protected against drying; 7 days are generally sufficient for complete hydration
backfilling of a building pit can take place 3 days after coating

fillR2.title: Fill the container
fillR2.short: Filling after 3 days; drinking water tanks rinsed thoroughly first; pressurised water after ≥ 7 days; the slurry stays active.
fillR2.overview: Filling of containers is possible after 3 days. Drinking water tanks are rinsed out thoroughly with drinking water before filling. {IC} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days and may require at least one month to achieve its maximum sealing characteristics, depending on temperature, humidity, type of cement and concrete composition. When properly applied, it is permanently active.
points: the reaction with the free lime in the concrete can result in slight efflorescence: not a defect, removed with a broom
a different colouring depends on the different moisture content in the concrete
cracks that develop later, up to 0.4 mm, are sealed by renewed crystal growth

dryR.title: Dry pit, active coating
dryR.short: The pit stays dry; the crystals keep growing wherever water arrives — permanently active.
dryR.overview: {IC} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 7 days; the maximum sealing effect can take up to one month. The coating is vapour permeable and permanently active: cracks up to 0.4 mm that develop later are sealed again. Efflorescence from the free lime of the concrete is brushed off.
points: negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar
the pit stays ventilated until the coating has cured; no direct heating
the coating cannot be overcoated with tiles, plaster, bonded screeds or paint

crystalR.title: How the crystals seal the concrete
crystalR.short: Active ingredients penetrate the capillaries with the water, react with moisture and free lime and fill the smallest pores and cracks with crystals.
crystalR.overview: Once applied to the concrete surface, the active ingredients from the waterproofing material penetrate inside the building component and cause a brisk crystal growth. The smallest pores and cracks become filled with crystals and impermeable to capillary water. “Foe becomes friend”: water penetrating the component behaves as a transport medium for the active ingredients and takes them deep into the substrate.
points: the coating remains permanently active and seals cracks of up to 0.4 mm that develop later
vapour permeable (class I), carbonation reducing, chloride-free
the same mechanism in the repair mortar {IM} (capillary active, increased crack healing) and the plugging mortar {F20} (crystalline sealing effect)

aggR.title: Analyse aggressive and soft water
aggR.short: Hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre or aggressive water: a water analysis is always required; degree of attack after EN 1992-1-1.
aggR.overview: If {IC} is applied in containers or in case of water loading with aggressive or soft water featuring a hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre, a water analysis is always required. The degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1 (Eurocode 2).
points: sewage, sludge and septic tanks are among the fields of application of {IC}
in containers dropping below the dew point is avoided with condensation dryers
the coating cannot be overcoated with tiles, plaster, bonded screeds or paint

cleanR.title: Clean the tools, store the material
cleanR.short: Tools rinsed with water immediately after use; bags and pails stored cool and dry.
cleanR.overview: Tools are rinsed with water immediately after use. {IC} is stored cool and dry for min. 12 months in the original container, {IM} cool, dry and protected from sunlight for min. 18 months, {F20} likewise for min. 12 months. Opened containers are used promptly. Observe the applicable safety data sheets.
points: {IM} and {IC} cannot be admixed as an additive to concrete or plaster
surfaces that are not to be treated are protected from the effects of the mortars
observe the applicable safety data sheets

rctank.name: Drinking and service water tank, from the inside
rctank.problem: A concrete tank holds water permanently: a water-bearing crack and a leaking construction joint let it through, lime leaches out along them, the concrete carbonates. The tank has to be tight, and — for drinking water — the coating must be suitable for it.
rctank.solution: The tank is drained and jetted; static cracks over 0.4 mm and the joint are chased 20 × 25 mm, screened with {IC} and filled flush with {IM}; the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm follows wet in wet. Two coats of {IC} — 1.5 kg/m² for accumulated water — are brushed into the matt damp concrete and kept damp for 3 days; the tank is rinsed and filled after 3 days. Tested for drinking water (DVGW W 270 / W 347), 14 bar (CRD-C 48-92), permanently active.

rcwall.name: Basement wall from the inside, negative pressing water
rcwall.problem: Ground water presses through a construction joint of an in-situ concrete basement wall: the joint leaks, lime leaches out, at its foot the water runs in. The outside cannot be dug up, so the waterproofing has to hold the pressure from the negative side.
rcwall.solution: The running water is stopped with a plug of {F20} pressed into the dovetailed opening; the joint and the cracks are chased 20 × 25 mm and filled with {IM} on a screen of {IC}, the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm at the floor; then two coats of {IC} (1.5 kg/m²) brushed into the matt damp concrete — watertight against negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar, the crystals growing into the capillaries. Kept damp ≥ 3 days, ventilated, no condensation.

rcpit.name: Lift pit with active water ingress
rcpit.problem: The pit of a lift shaft lies below the ground water level: water enters under pressure at the wall–floor joint and through an old anchor hole, stands in the pit and cannot be pumped away for good. Access only from the inside, in a confined and poorly ventilated space.
rcpit.solution: A drain hose set into a chiselled depression at the strongest flow and fixed with {F20} relieves the pressure while the joint is plugged with {F20}; after drying the hose is removed and its hole plugged. The coved fillet of {IM} of approx. 4 cm on a screen of {IC}, then two coats of {IC} over walls and floor (1.5 kg/m²). Kept damp ≥ 3 days, the pit ventilated for 24 hours — the pit stays dry, the coating stays active.

rcsew.name: Sewage and sludge tank, aggressive water
rcsew.problem: Sewage, sludge and septic tanks hold aggressive, often soft water: sludge and biofilm cover the concrete, cracks and the inlet leak, the humid, poorly ventilated container condenses. The concrete must be sealed against the water and the water kept away from the concrete.
rcsew.solution: A water analysis first (hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre; degree of attack after EN 1992-1-1). Sludge and biofilm are jetted off; cracks are chased and filled with {IM}, larger voids re-profiled with the ASOCRET-BIS system; then two coats of {IC} (1.5 kg/m²) into the matt damp concrete — chloride-free, carbonation reducing, vapour permeable. Condensation is avoided with dryers, the coating is kept damp ≥ 3 days at a relative humidity > 80 %; filling after 3 days.

planA.title: Design the watertight concrete
planA.short: Exposure, water load and crack-width limits by the engineer; a recipe within the requirements of the data sheet; the component at least 15 cm thick.
planA.overview: The planner and the structural engineer define the exposure classes, the water load and — decisive for the self-healing — the crack-width limits of the component: the crack expansion limitations must be complied with under any circumstances, contrary designs are verified after the corresponding verification and suitability. The concrete is a watertight concrete after DIN EN 206 / DIN 1045-2 within the requirements of the data sheet: cement ≥ 270 kg/m³ (CEM I), ≥ 290 (CEM II), ≥ 380 (CEM III/A; {CP360} also CEM III/B ≥ 400); w/c ratio < 0.55; fly ash ≤ 80 and granulated slag ≤ 100 kg/m³ added to the binder; grain size 16 mm, in exceptional cases 32 mm; component thickness not less than 15 cm.
points: concretes of exposure class XA3 (DIN EN 206-1 / DIN 1045-2) are excluded; CEM III/C cements are prohibited, CEM III/B for {CL170}, {CL210} and {CP350}
lignite fly ash is of limited suitability; as the share of Portland cement and the dosage fall, the crystallisation may slow down

unless otherwise agreed, the manufacturer is responsible for the concrete mix design; concrete ordered by properties after DIN EN 206 may contain admixtures after DIN EN 934-2 — without a CE mark the recipe would become a concrete composition and the responsibility passes to the customer
for drinking water structures: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested after DVGW W 270 and W 347
the construction joints are planned with the system accessories: {CJ5}, {CJ6}, {CJ1}

testA.title: Carry out the preliminary tests
testA.short: The functionality of the recipe including the admixture is verified in an initial test; the dosing level follows the w/c ratio and the cement content.
testA.overview: The functionality of the concrete mix design including BETOCRETE is verified as part of an initial test; preliminary tests must always be carried out — also when other admixtures are combined with it. The dosing level of the data sheet follows the w/c ratio: liquid 1.75 % (< 0.4), 1.85 % (> 0.4–0.5), 2.00 % (> 0.5–0.55) of the cement weight, never above 2.25 %; powder 0.75 / 0.80 / 0.90 % ({CP360}) or 0.75 / 0.80 / 0.95 % ({CP350}), never above 1.25 %. For a cement content of ≥ 400 kg/m³ 7.00 kg/m³ (liquid) or 3.50 kg/m³ (powder) is sufficient.
points: the dosage depends on the cement content and the w/c ratio of the recipe; the table serves as a guide
in rare cases the admixture can influence the solidification behaviour of the concrete: the system-compatible retarder {RUX} is available for controlling the concrete
{CL170}: water saving up to 10 % — the water content of the recipe is adjusted in the initial test
the quantity of a liquid admixture is deducted from the mixing water

doseP.title: Dose the liquid admixture in the plant
doseP.short: BETOCRETE-CL dosed with the mixing water or into the finished mix by the dosing system of the plant; mixed for more than 45 seconds; deducted from the mixing water.
doseP.overview: Liquid BETOCRETE is dosed directly into the concrete mix via the dosing system of the concrete plant — with the mixing water or into the finished concrete mixture — without additional work steps and precisely, with automated pump technology. The mixing time in the concrete plant is more than 45 seconds. The quantity of the admixture is deducted from the mixing water.
points: dosing approx. 1.75–2.25 % of the cement weight; never above 2.25 %
application temperature approx. 8–40 °C; stir the admixture after storage of more than one month
colour change of the admixture above +30 °C is harmless
IBC (1,100 kg {CL170} / 1,040 kg {CL210}), 220 kg drums and 25 kg cans; storage frost-free at 8–40 °C

doseC.title: Dose the powder admixture in the plant
doseC.short: BETOCRETE-CP dosed onto the aggregates and mixed for at least 30 seconds before water and cement are added; then mixed for at least 45 seconds.
doseC.overview: {CP360} and {CP350} must be dosed onto the aggregates and mixed for at least 30 seconds before adding the water and the cement. Then the mixing is finished for at least 45 seconds until the concrete is ready for use. The powder is supplied in watertight foil bags (17 kg {CP360}, 20 kg {CP350}) for metering into the mixer.
points: dosing approx. 0.75–1.25 % of the cement weight; never above 1.25 %
application temperature min. 5 °C
for a cement content of ≥ 400 kg/m³ a dosing level of 3.50 kg/m³ is sufficient
storage cool, dry and protected from sunlight, min. 24 months; opened containers are used promptly

truckA.title: Dose into the mixer truck on site
truckA.short: Powder as 3 kg water-soluble bags, liquid poured into the drum; approx. 1 minute of mixing per m³ of drum content, at least 5 minutes.
truckA.overview: Where the admixture is added on site, the powder goes into the drum of the mixer truck as 3 kg water-soluble bags and liquid BETOCRETE-CL is poured directly into the mixing drum. The mixing time is approx. 1 minute per m³ of drum content, but at least 5 minutes. For the liquid the quantity is deducted from the mixing water.
points: water-soluble bags of {CP360} and {CP350}: 192 per pallet, also as a cardboard version ({CP360})
water-soluble paper bags may increase the water demand ({CP360})
the number of bags per load follows from the cement content of the load and the dosing level
the mixing time is counted after the last bag has gone in

jointA.title: Detail the construction joints
jointA.short: The crystalline waterstop AQUAFIN-CJ5 in the kicker; the swelling tape AQUAFIN-CJ6 on working joints; the injection hose AQUAFIN-CJ1 as reserve.
jointA.overview: The construction joint is the classic weak point in waterproofing. The system accessories for the construction joint provide the solution: in addition to grouting and expanding waterstops, the crystalline construction metal waterstop {CJ5} offers a high level of safety. It extends the circulation of the water on the possible path through the cracked joint; its cementitious coating forms a high adhesion bond with the concrete, so that the probability of cracking is reduced; the metal waterstop is ready to use and not prone to processing errors — no film has to be peeled off; if there is a crack in the construction joint, crystal formation is induced by the metal waterstop and the cracks are sealed.
points: {CJ5} is fixed to the reinforcement in the kicker before the wall is poured and cast in by the wall
working joints: the swelling joint tape {CJ6} on the hardened concrete
critical joints: the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve, injected only if the joint leaks
movement joints are not construction joints: they are formed with the joint tapes of the ASO-Dichtband system †

placeA.title: Place, compact and finish the concrete
placeA.short: As watertight concrete to the valid standards: full compaction, no segregation, no added water on site; the admixture does not replace the craft.
placeA.overview: Concrete with BETOCRETE must be produced, applied and post-treated in accordance with the currently valid standards. The admixture changes neither the placing nor the compaction: the concrete is placed in layers, fully compacted, and no water is added on site †. The crystalline effect works in a dense concrete — honeycombs and voids are not sealed by crystals but repaired.
points: no additional water on site: it raises the w/c ratio beyond the recipe †
fully compacted, placed in layers without cold joints †
{CL170} gives a smoother consistency at a lower water content; the water saving is part of the recipe, not an allowance on site
honeycombs and voids are broken out and repaired with the ASOCRET-BIS system before the component is loaded †

cureA.title: Cure the concrete
cureA.short: Kept damp and protected to the valid standards; crystals may appear on the surface, depending on the composition — not a defect.
cureA.overview: The curing of the concrete follows the currently valid standards for watertight concrete: the surfaces are protected against drying out, wind, sun and frost and kept damp †. BETOCRETE-modified concretes may show crystals on the surface, depending on the composition; the colour and the moisture content of the concrete have no bearing on the function.
points: curing to the standards: the crystalline effect needs the dense concrete the curing produces †
crystals on the surface are not a defect
the formwork is struck when the strength allows †
the surfaces are not coated before they have been assessed: cracks wider than 0.4 mm and moving cracks are injected

crackA.title: Control the cracks
crackA.short: Crack-width limits by the planner and engineer; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal themselves; wider or moving cracks are injected.
crackA.overview: The crack expansion limitations must be complied with by the planner, engineer and structural engineer under any circumstances; contrary designs are verified after the corresponding verification and suitability. Surface and continuous cracks up to 0.4 mm (tapering down to 0.5 mm) heal themselves by crystal growth when water reaches them. Movements in the concrete component — traffic loads, temperature differences — can cause sealed crystalline cracks to open again; they heal again when water arrives.
points: crack injections for non-dynamic separating cracks up to 0.4 mm can often be omitted due to the crack-healing ability
cracks wider than 0.4 mm and dynamic cracks are injected: {P1}, {P4}, {IH}
the injection hose {CJ1} in a critical joint is the reserve

serviceA.title: The component in service
serviceA.short: The ground water presses, the pores close, the inside stays dry; the reserve of active ingredient stays in the matrix for life.
serviceA.overview: When the water load arrives the active ingredient dissolves in the pore water, reacts with the calcium hydroxide of the hydration and grows insoluble crystals in the capillary pores: the capillary zone shifts outwards, the reinforcement lies in the dry core, moisture leaves the inside face as vapour only. The more compact pore structure reduces the chloride ion migration and the carbonation rate and improves the frost and freeze–thaw resistance. The reserve of unreacted active ingredient remains in the matrix for the life of the component.
points: the sealant of {CL210} and {CP360} has been reducing the water absorption by more than half from the first day
water-retaining structures: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested for drinking water
the component is as watertight as the concrete is sound: the recipe, the compaction and the joints decide

notesA.title: Observe the limits of the data sheets
notesA.short: No XA3, no CEM III/C; preliminary tests; the retarder RUXOLITH-T5 where the setting is affected; safety data sheets.
notesA.overview: The data sheets set the limits: concretes of exposure class XA3 are excluded; CEM III/C cements are prohibited (CEM III/B also for {CL170}, {CL210} and {CP350}); lignite fly ash is of limited suitability; the crack expansion limitations are complied with. In rare cases the admixture can influence the solidification behaviour of the concrete — the system-compatible retarder {RUX} is available for controlling the concrete. Preliminary tests must always be carried out.
points: observe the applicable safety data sheets
liquids: stir after storage of more than one month; store frost-free at 8–40 °C; a colour change above +30 °C is harmless
powders: store cool, dry and protected from sunlight for min. 24 months; use opened containers promptly
as the share of Portland cement and the dosage fall, the crystallisation may slow down ({CL210})

waterA.title: Choose the product for drinking water
waterA.short: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested after DVGW W 270 and W 347; {CL210} is used where drinking water is not involved.
waterA.overview: For tanks and structures in contact with drinking water the admixture must be suitable for it: {CL170}, {CP360} and {CP350} are tested after the DVGW worksheets W 270 (microbiological) and W 347 (hygienic) and suitable for drinking water. {CL210} is not tested for drinking water and is used for the other water-retaining and ground-contact structures.
points: the test reports after W 270 and W 347 are available for download with the product
no lining to taint the water, lift or age: the crystals are part of the concrete
the filled tank is vapour permeable to the outside and watertight to the inside

saltA.title: Frost, de-icing salt and chlorides
saltA.short: Reduced chloride ion migration, lower carbonation speed, improved freeze–thaw resistance; {CL210} is most effective in exposure class XS.
saltA.overview: Components exposed to frost, de-icing salt or sea water need a concrete that keeps the chlorides away from the reinforcement: BETOCRETE reduces the chloride ion migration and improves the frost and freeze–thaw resistance; {CL210} and {CP360} also lower the carbonation speed. {CL210} shows the highest effectiveness in exposure class XS. The test reports of {CL210} cover freeze–thaw–salt resistance, chloride migration, carbonation and the depth of water penetration under pressure.
points: the German Federal Institute for Hydraulic Engineering (BAW) derives the service life from the chloride migration coefficient and the concrete cover: a test report shows a 2.5-fold service life for a BETOCRETE concrete against the reference
{CP350} adds a corrosion inhibitor where the steel is at risk
exposure class XA3 (chemical attack) is excluded for all four products

cabase.name: Base slab and walls below ground
cabase.problem: A basement stands in the ground: soil moisture and ground water press against the slab and the walls, the construction joint at the kicker is the weak point, and the cracks that every slab and wall develop would carry the water inside. An external membrane needs a weather window, protection boards and an excavation for every repair.
cabase.solution: Slab and walls are cast in watertight concrete with BETOCRETE — {CL170} or {CL210} dosed with the mixing water at the plant, {CP360} as water-soluble bags where the truck is dosed on site. The crystalline waterstop {CJ5} stands in the kicker, the swelling tape {CJ6} on working joints, the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve. When the ground water rises the pores close; cracks up to 0.4 mm heal themselves; the inside stays dry and vapour permeable. Technical drawings TD 5.10.01a and 5.10.01b.

capit.name: Lift pit below the ground water
capit.problem: The pit of a lift shaft is the deepest point of the building, below the ground water table on all sides, reachable only from the inside: slab, walls and kicker joint carry pressing water from the first day, and the buffers, rails and anchors must be fixed to dry concrete.
capit.solution: The pit is cast in BETOCRETE concrete — {CP360} or {CP350} as 3 kg water-soluble bags into the drum of the mixer truck on site, approx. 1 minute of mixing per m³ and at least 5 minutes — with the crystalline waterstop {CJ5} in the kicker and the injection hose {CJ1} as reserve where the pit cannot be reached later. Crack-width limits by the structural engineer; component thickness ≥ 15 cm. The pit stays dry; a crack from settlement or shrinkage closes itself. Technical drawing TD 5.10.02.

catank.name: Water tank, drinking water
catank.problem: A tank holds water permanently from the inside: joints between slab and wall, inlets and the fine cracks of a filled tank would leak, and a lining could taint the water, lift or age. For drinking water the admixture itself must be suitable.
catank.solution: Slab and walls in BETOCRETE concrete with {CL170}, {CP360} or {CP350} — tested for drinking water after DVGW W 270 and W 347; {CL210} where drinking water is not involved. The waterstop {CJ5} in the joint between slab and wall, inlets and outlets cast in. The crystals seal from the inside out and heal cracks up to 0.4 mm; there is no coating to renew. Technical drawing TD 5.10.03.

cawall.name: Retaining wall, frost and de-icing salt
cawall.problem: A retaining wall carries soil and seepage water on its back and frost, de-icing salt and traffic spray on its face: chlorides migrate to the reinforcement, carbonation advances, freeze–thaw opens the surface. A membrane on the soil side cannot be renewed without excavation.
cawall.solution: The wall is cast in BETOCRETE concrete with {CL210} or {CP360}: the integrated sealant lowers the water absorption at once, the crystals follow wherever water arrives; reduced chloride ion migration and carbonation, improved freeze–thaw resistance — {CL210} shows the highest effectiveness in exposure class XS; {CP350} adds a corrosion inhibitor. The swelling tape {CJ6} on the working joints, the drainage behind the wall stays. Technical drawing TD 5.10.04.

planF.title: Assess the floor and choose the system
planF.short: Exposure, loads, chemicals, slip class and the moisture of the substrate decide the system: the six subgroups are chosen together — primer, levelling, coating, finish, joints and repairs.
planF.overview: Before the first bucket is opened the floor is assessed: the mechanical load (foot traffic, cars, pallet trucks, forklifts, impacts), the chemical load (oils, tyre softeners, cleaning agents, acids, sewage), the slip class required by the use (R10 … R12), the colour, and above all the substrate — its strength, its residual moisture and whether vapour or oil rise through it. From this the system is composed across the subgroups: a pore-sealing primer ({GBM}, {G1270}) on dry concrete, a barrier primer ({SG3}, {SG3F}, {SG3T}) on damp or young concrete, {SG2} after {R008} on oil-contaminated concrete; the levelling with scratch coats and {EV200}; the coating — {B351} thin or thick, {V360} as the aqueous seal, {V2370} against chemicals; the finish with quartz sand, {ANTI} or {V2260}; the joints with {IPU}; the repairs with {K4031} and {EV200}.
points: substrate: load-bearing, firm, grippy, ≥ 1.5 N/mm² tensile adhesion (concrete min. C20/25, screed min. CT-C25-F6), prepared after DIN EN 14879-1
dry substrates (≤ 4 CM-% for the resin coatings and seals, ≤ 5 CM-% for {V360}, ≤ 6 CM-% for {V2370}) take the standard primers; matt damp, young or vapour-loaded substrates take the barrier primers
the slip class is produced by the finish: {ANTI} in the seal (R10 / R11) or quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm broadcast under the top seal (R11, up to R12)
joints of the slab are taken through the coating and filled elastic; machine bases and breakouts are grouted before the coating
a trial area where the substrate is in doubt; the applicable safety data sheets are observed
planF.src: brochure · GBM · SG3 · SG2 · B351 · V360W · V2370

prepF.title: Prepare the substrate
prepF.short: Shot-blasted or ground to an open-pored, grippy surface; laitance, coatings and loose parts removed; vacuumed dust-free; ≥ 1.5 N/mm².
prepF.overview: The substrate must be load-bearing, firm, grippy, dust-free and open-pored: laitance, sinter layers, old coatings, separating agents and loose parts are removed by shot blasting (or grinding, milling) so that the aggregate is exposed and the pores open; the surface is vacuumed dust-free immediately before the primer. The surface tensile strength is at least 1.5 N/mm² (concrete min. C20/25, screed min. CT-C25-F6; plaster P III a/b at least 0.8 N/mm²). The preparation follows DIN EN 14879-1:2005, section 4.2 et seq.; the substrate temperature is 10–35 °C and at least 3 °C above the dew point.
points: shot blasting is the standard preparation for floors: dust-free, uniform, no water into the slab †
oil crusts are removed mechanically before the cleaning with {R008}
cracks, breakouts and hollow spots are made good before the primer ({K4031}, {EV200}); cracks are closed beforehand, e.g. with {GHS} ({V360})
the joints of the slab are cut clean and kept free for {IPU}
the primer follows on the day of the preparation so that no new dust and no moisture settle †

moistF.title: Check the residual moisture and the dew point
moistF.short: Residual moisture by the CM method: ≤ 4 CM-% for the resin systems, ≤ 5 for {V360}, ≤ 6 for {V2370}; above that the barrier primers; the substrate at least 3 °C above the dew point.
moistF.overview: The residual moisture of the substrate is measured with the CM device: the resin coatings and seals need ≤ 4 CM-%, {V360} ≤ 5 CM-%, {V2370} ≤ 6 CM-%. A substrate that is matt damp, young, without a vapour barrier or under ground water is primed with the barrier primers {SG3}, {SG3F} or {SG3T} (floor, wall, overhead) — they bond to damp concrete and block vapour and negative pressing water up to 3 bar; oil-contaminated and damp concrete takes {SG2}. The climate is checked throughout the work: substrate and air 10–35 °C (10–30 °C for {V2260} and {V2370}), at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 80 % (65 % for {V360}).
points: no sealed water film on the substrate; damp substrates are matt damp, not wet
below the dew point distance the resin blushes and the bond fails: the dew point is measured, not estimated †
the barrier primers are not an allowance for standing water: hydrostatic pressure above 3 bar is a waterproofing task
the material temperature ideally +15 °C: cold material is viscous, warm material shortens the pot life
moistF.src: SG3 · SG2 · SG3-thix · V360W · V2260 · V2370

cleanF.title: Clean the oil-contaminated concrete
cleanF.short: {R008} diluted with tap water, sprayed, scrubbed criss-cross until brownish, left for 10 minutes, scrubbed again, rinsed with hot water and vacuumed — repeated until no oil remains; the surface is not dried off.
cleanF.overview: After the oil crusts have been removed mechanically and the surface has been shot-blasted, the cleaning concentrate {R008} is diluted with tap water as the data sheet prescribes, sprayed onto the surface and scrubbed in criss-cross until the solution turns brownish; it is left for approx. 10 minutes, scrubbed again, rinsed with hot clear water (60–80 °C) and picked up with a wet vacuum. The procedure is repeated until no oil remains. The surface is not dried off: the primer {SG2} (or {SG3T}) must meet the damp, oil-free concrete.
points: {R008} is solvent-free and phosphate-free; approx. 70–250 ml of concentrate per m² depending on the dilution
the brownish colour of the solution shows the oil going into the emulsion
hot water rinses the emulsion out of the pores; a wet vacuum takes it up — it is not left to dry back in †
the same concentrate cleans the finished floor in service

repairF.title: Repair breakouts, holes and cracks
repairF.short: Breakouts and holes filled with {K4031} or {EV200}; anchors set in {K4031}; cracks closed before the coating; the mortar flush with the slab.
repairF.overview: Breakouts, holes and hollow spots are made good before the primer, so that the coating meets a level, closed substrate: small repairs and anchor holes with the thixotropic epoxy adhesive {K4031} (drill holes at least 6 mm larger than the anchor, cleaned, filled, the anchor set with rotary movements), larger breakouts, gullies and cavities with the flowable epoxy mortar {EV200} in 10–200 mm. Cracks are closed beforehand (e.g. with {GHS}). The repairs are overcoated within their windows — {K4031} after 16–24 hours, {EV200} after 12–72 hours without primer.
points: {K4031}: mixing ratio 2 : 1, pot life approx. 60 minutes, adhesive open time at least 90 minutes; ≥ 2 N/mm² on concrete and steel
{EV200}: ≥ 2 N/mm², watertight to 5 bar from 10 mm; approx. 1.9 kg/m² per mm
hollow sounding areas are cut out to sound concrete and filled †
the surface of the repair is sanded if the overcoat window has passed

primeF.title: Prime with ASODUR-GBM
primeF.short: {GBM} mixed 100 : 50, rolled into the open pores in one or two steps until the surface is pore-sealed, approx. 0.30–0.50 kg/m² per step; quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm broadcast onto the fresh last coat.
primeF.overview: The component A is stirred, the component B added completely and both mixed for approx. 3 minutes with a slow stirrer (approx. 300 rpm) at an ideal material temperature of +15 °C; the mix is poured into a clean container and stirred again. {GBM} (100 : 50 parts by weight, pot life approx. 35 minutes) is applied with the roller or the rubber squeegee and back-rolled in one or two steps until the surface is pore-sealed — approx. 0.30–0.50 kg/m² per step depending on the absorbency. Quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm is broadcast onto the fresh last coat as the key for the coating; the loose sand is swept and vacuumed after hardening. The coating follows after min. approx. 12 hours and within 24 hours.
points: {G1270} (approx. 130 mPa·s, 100 : 27) is the alternative where the substrate must be impregnated and consolidated
keep damp off for approx. 4–6 hours after application
foot traffic after approx. 12 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days; approx. 70 N/mm² compressive

The hardened film blocks vapour and negative pressing water up to 3 bar (methane barrier tested) and gives ≥ 1.5 N/mm² on concrete from dry to matt damp.

fastF.short: {SG3F}: the same barrier, overcoated after approx. 3.5 hours — two coats in one shift; pot life approx. 15–20 minutes; the coating within 5 days.

It bonds to the damp concrete, displaces the water from the capillaries of the surface and blocks capillary-rising oil and vapour (sd > 100 m, class III) as well as negative water pressure up to 3 bar; it is radon tight. Quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm is broadcast over the whole fresh surface; the loose sand is removed when cured, and the coating follows after approx. 12–24 hours.

points: on oil-contaminated substrates after the pre-treatment with {R008} and warm water (approx. 50–70 °C), not dried off
the capillary-breaking mortar: resin mix : quartz sand 1 : 4.17 by weight (e.g. 6 kg + 25 kg)
approx. 80 N/mm² compressive; EMICODE EC 1PLUS
steel that is not coated within 4 hours of cleaning is primed with {SG3T} before {EV200}

scratchF.title: Level with the scratch coat
scratchF.short: The primer resin mixed 1 : 1 by weight with quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm (2–3 % {FF} on slopes), spread on the fresh primer with the scratch filler method, approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm, sanded while fresh.
scratchF.overview: Rough, pitted or uneven substrates are levelled with a scratch coat before the coating: the primer resin ({GBM}, {G1270} or {SG3}) mixed 1 : 1 by weight with kiln-dried quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm — with 2–3 % {FF} on vertical and sloping surfaces so that it does not run — spread in one step with the scratch filler method on the fresh or sanded primer and broadcast with quartz sand while fresh. Approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm of thickness; the coating follows after 12–24 hours.
points: thicker levelling (5–30 mm mortar, 11–150 mm screed) with the epoxy screed 3 : 25 — resin : quartz sand Ø 0.06–3.5 mm
with {V360} the levelling is made with the seal itself: 1 : 0.5 with quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.35 mm up to 2 mm, pinholes with approx. 3 % {FF}
a sanded scratch coat is swept and vacuumed before the coating
where the slab is level and closed the scratch coat is omitted

mortarF.title: Grout machine bases and breakouts with ASODUR-EV200
mortarF.short: {EV200}, the flowable three-component epoxy mortar, 10–200 mm in one skin, self-compacting, without primer; approx. 65 N/mm² after 24 hours, 109 N/mm² after 7 days; approx. 1.9 kg/m² per mm.
mortarF.overview: Machine bases, crane rails, railing and support posts, anchors, gullies, cavities and breakouts are grouted with {EV200}: the components A and B are mixed, the filler C added and all three mixed for approx. 3 minutes (5.04 : 1.66 : 23.3 parts by weight, pot life approx. 120 minutes); the mortar is poured in 10–200 mm in one skin (above 200 mm in several skins), flows and compacts itself. No primer is needed on concrete; ≥ 2 N/mm² on concrete from dry to matt damp and on steel; watertight to 5 bar from 10 mm; approx. 65 N/mm² compressive after 24 hours and approx. 109 N/mm² after 7 days.
points: foot traffic after approx. 12 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days; Bfl-s1 up to 75 mm
cleaned steel is coated within 4 hours, otherwise primed with {SG3T}
for a slip-resistant mortar surface quartz sand 0.5–1.0 mm is broadcast after approx. 120 minutes, the excess removed and the surface sealed
overcoat min. approx. 12 hours, max. 72 hours without primer
GISCODE RE 30; the safety data sheets are observed

coatThinF.title: Coat with ASODUR-B351, thin coat
coatThinF.short: {B351} mixed 100 : 24, spread with the trowel in one pass at approx. 1 mm (approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm) and rolled criss-cross with the spiked roller; walkable after 12 hours, full load after 7 days.
coatThinF.overview: The pigmented, self-levelling epoxy floor coating {B351} is mixed 100 : 24 parts by weight for approx. 3 minutes at an ideal material temperature of +15 °C (pot life approx. 30 minutes), poured onto the sanded primer, spread with the notched trowel or the rubber squeegee in one pass at approx. 1 mm and rolled criss-cross with the spiked roller to release the air. Approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm. The coating is kept free of damp for approx. 4–6 hours, walkable after approx. 12 hours, overcoated within 12–24 hours and fully resilient after approx. 7 days.
points: approx. 70 N/mm² compressive, approx. 44 N/mm² flexural, Shore D approx. 72, Bfl-s1, ≥ 1.5 N/mm²
resistant to oils, tyre softeners, dilute acids and alkalis and cleaning agents; standard RAL colours or transparent
the spiked roller is run while the coating still flows: too late it leaves marks †
batches are planned to the pot life so that every pass is joined wet in wet †

coatThickF.title: Coat with ASODUR-B351, thick coat
coatThickF.short: {B351} with + 50 parts by weight of quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm (resin : sand 2 : 1), spread at approx. 2 mm — approx. 1.2 kg/m² {B351} + 0.6 kg/m² sand per mm; de-aerated with the spiked roller.
coatThickF.overview: For high mechanical loads — forklifts, pallet trucks, impacts — {B351} is filled: after the components A and B have been mixed, 50 parts by weight of kiln-dried quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm are stirred in (resin : sand 2 : 1). The thick coat is spread with the trowel at approx. 2 mm — approx. 1.2 kg/m² of {B351} and 0.6 kg/m² of sand per mm — and rolled criss-cross with the spiked roller. The times are those of the thin coat: pot life approx. 30 minutes, walkable after approx. 12 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days.
points: the thick coat lies on the two-step sanded primer of {GBM} or on the sanded barrier primer
the quartz sand is kiln-dried; damp sand foams the resin †
where the slab is rough a scratch coat under the thick coat saves material
the slip-resistant finish follows on the hardened thick coat

slipF.title: Make the surface slip resistant
slipF.short: An interspersing coat of {B351} (300–400 g/m²), quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm broadcast to excess (approx. 1.5 kg/m²), the loose sand removed after hardening, the top seal of {B351} rolled criss-cross (400–800 g/m²): R11, up to R12.
slipF.overview: Where the floor is wet or oily in use the surface is made slip resistant: an interspersing coat of {B351} is rolled onto the hardened coating (approx. 300–400 g/m²), quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm is broadcast to excess while fresh (approx. 1.5 kg/m²), the loose sand is swept and vacuumed after hardening, and the top seal of {B351} is rolled criss-cross (approx. 400–800 g/m²). The floor reaches slip class R11 by test report, up to R12 depending on the sand and the seal. In the aqueous seals {ANTI} produces the slip resistance instead.
points: the top seal is rolled thin and even: a thick seal fills the profile †
a transparent top seal keeps the colour of the coating
the cleaning of a profiled floor is planned with the scrubber-drier: the coarser the profile, the harder the cleaning †
walkable after approx. 12 hours; full resilience after approx. 7 days

vprimeF.title: Prime with ASODUR-V360W, diluted
vprimeF.short: {V360} mixed 100 : 20, diluted with 8–10 % water (max. 10 %), rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller, approx. 0.15 kg/m²; the seal after 16–48 hours.
vprimeF.overview: The water-emulsified epoxy {V360} is its own primer: the component A is stirred, the component B added and both mixed for approx. 3 minutes (100 : 20 parts by weight, pot life approx. 40 minutes); 8–10 % water is stirred in (not more than 10 %) and the primer rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller onto the dry (≤ 5 CM-%), prepared substrate — concrete, cement and calcium sulphate screeds, magnesia screed, sanded mastic asphalt — approx. 0.15 kg/m². The seal follows after min. 16 hours and within 48 hours.
points: substrate and air 10–35 °C, at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 65 %
cracks are closed beforehand, e.g. with {GHS}
≥ 2.8 N/mm² on dry concrete
the garage, the cellar, the warehouse: two days from the primer to the walkable floor

vlevelF.title: Level with ASODUR-V360W
vlevelF.short: Pinholes and recesses filled with {V360} + approx. 3 % {FF}; unevenness up to 2 mm levelled with {V360} + 50 % quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.35 mm; sanded with 100 grit and vacuumed after hardening.
vlevelF.overview: Pinholes and small recesses are filled with {V360} thickened with approx. 3 % {FF}; unevenness up to 2 mm is levelled with a scratch coat of {V360} and quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.35 mm (resin mix : sand 1 : 0.5 by weight). After hardening the levelling is sanded with 100 grit and vacuumed, and the seal follows within the overcoat window of 16–48 hours — beyond it the surface is sanded again.
points: approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm of the levelling
the levelling is thin: the aqueous system is a seal, not a floor screed
a smooth, closed surface shows every pinhole under the satin seal — the levelling is worth the hour †

vsealF.title: Seal with ASODUR-V360W
vsealF.short: {V360} rolled criss-cross in one to two steps, approx. 0.30–0.35 kg/m² per step: pigmented, satin, vapour permeable; resistant to tyre softeners, dilute acids and alkalis, heating oil and petrol; walkable after 16 hours.
vsealF.overview: The seal is mixed like the primer, undiluted, and rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller in one to two steps, approx. 0.30–0.35 kg/m² per step; the second step after min. 16 hours and within 48 hours. The hardened seal is pigmented in the standard RAL colours (approx. 7032, 7030, 7035, 1001, 7040), satin and vapour permeable, so that the slab can still breathe; it resists the softeners of car tyres, dilute acids and alkalis, heating oil and petrol. Walkable after approx. 16 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days.
points: {ANTI} at 8–10 % by weight in the last step for slip class R10
approx. 1.4 g/cm³ ready to use; approx. 2,800 mPa·s
the garage floor is driven on after 7 days; tyres are not turned on the spot in the first weeks †
the wall–floor joint is closed with {IPU}

antiF.title: Stir in ASO-Antislide
antiF.short: {ANTI}, the spherical glass granulate of 90–150 µm, stirred into the premixed seal at 8–10 % by weight (max. 170 g/m² in the sealing layer): R10 with {V360}, R11 with {V2260}.
antiF.overview: For a slip-resistant aqueous seal the ready-to-use glass granulate {ANTI} is stirred into the premixed, low-viscosity seal at approx. 8–10 % by weight — not more than 170 g/m² in the sealing layer — and the seal is rolled as usual. The granulate is stirred up during the work so that it does not settle in the bucket. By test report the floor reaches R10 with {V360} and R11 with {V2260}.
points: grain size > 90 to 150 µm, bulk density approx. 1.35 g/cm³, transparent / matt
the slip-resistant seal with {V2260}: approx. 120 g/m²
the granulate goes into the last step only; the primer and the first step stay smooth
stored cool and dry; minimum 36 months

puF.title: Seal with ASODUR-V2260
puF.short: {V2260}, the aqueous two-component PU seal, mixed 100 : 20 with approx. 5 % water, rolled in one step on the cured coating, approx. 80–150 g/m²: transparent, glossy, light-fast, UV-stable, scratch resistant.
puF.overview: The showroom and the workshop get the glossy, easy-to-clean finish: {V2260} is mixed 100 : 20 parts by weight with approx. 5 % water for approx. 3 minutes and left to mature for approx. 2 minutes (pot life approx. 25–35 minutes at 10–30 °C), then rolled thin and even in one step with the nylon fur roller onto the cured, clean coating — approx. 80–150 g/m². The transparent seal is glossy, light-fast and UV-stable, scratch and abrasion resistant, with good migration resistance; EMICODE EC 1PLUS. Full resilience after approx. 7 days.
points: substrate 10–30 °C, dry (≤ 4 CM-%), at least 3 °C above the dew point
overcoat windows by temperature: +30 °C 2–3 to 12 hours; +20 °C 4–15 to 24 hours; +10 °C 9–13 to 48 hours
with 8–10 % {ANTI} slip class R11
stored frost-free at 10–30 °C; 12 months

v2370F.title: Coat the sewage structure with ASODUR-V2370
v2370F.short: {V2370} mixed 7 : 1, two layers in alternating colours on the primed concrete (approx. 400–500 g/m² per layer); on steel blasted to Sa 2½ the first layer is the primer; XWW4, sulphuric acid pH 0–1.
v2370F.overview: On the cementitious substrate primed with {SG3T} — and directly on steel blasted to Sa 2½ (DIN 55982), where the first layer acts as the primer — the sealing coating {V2370} is applied in two layers: mixed 7 : 1 parts by weight for approx. 3 minutes, rolled or sprayed at approx. 400–500 g/m² per layer on concrete, the second layer in the alternating colour (pebble grey, red, black) so that the coverage shows. The pot life follows the temperature (approx. 90–110 minutes at +10 °C, 45–55 at +20 °C, 22–28 at +30 °C), as do the overcoat windows (+10 °C: 24–36 to 48 hours; +20 °C: 12–16 to 24 hours; +30 °C: 6–8 to 12 hours) and the full resilience (10, 7 or 3 days). The coating is elastifying (Shore A approx. 80), stray-current insulating and resistant to sewage, sea water and sulphuric acid down to pH 0–1 — exposure class XWW4 after DIN 19753.
points: substrate 10–30 °C, dry (≤ 6 CM-%), at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 80 %

the chemical resistance table of the data sheet rates petrol, heating oil, alcohols, esters, formaldehyde, acetic acid, sulphuric acid 20 %, amines, surfactants and de-icing salt for 8 hours, 72 hours and 14 days
the coating is protected from moisture until it has hardened
breakouts and gullies are grouted with {EV200} before the coating; the movement joints are filled with {IPU}

jointF.title: Fill the joints with INDUFLEX-PU
jointF.short: Field, connection and wall joints 10–30 mm wide, depth after width : depth 1 : 0.8, backed with a closed-cell cord, primed and filled with {IPU}; edges chamfered 45° under vehicle traffic; approx. 100 ml/m at 10 × 8 mm … 750 ml/m at 30 × 24 mm.
jointF.overview: The field joints, connection joints and wall joints of the floor are taken through the coating and filled elastic: the joint 10–30 mm wide, the depth after the rule width : depth 1 : 0.8 (e.g. 15 × 12 mm, 20 × 16 mm), set with a closed-cell, rot-resistant backing cord approx. 20 % wider than the joint, the flanks primed (e.g. {SG3F}, approx. 200 g/m² absorbent, 150 g/m² non-absorbent, the joint filled after 3.5–48 hours) and filled with the one-component, moisture-curing polyurethane {IPU}, pressed against the flanks and smoothed. On components with vehicle traffic the edges are chamfered 45° (approx. 5 mm); the chamfer is not filled.
points: Shore A approx. 40, recovery > 90 %, permissible total deformation 25 %, service temperature −40 to +80 °C
skin formation after 60–90 minutes; 80 % of the final Shore A after 2 days at +23 °C; full loadability after 14 days at approx. +20 °C
substrate and air approx. 5–40 °C, at least 3 °C above the dew point
consumption: approx. 100 ml/m at 10 × 8 mm, 180 at 15 × 12, 320 at 20 × 16, 500 at 25 × 20, 750 at 30 × 24 mm
a movement joint is not coated over: a coating bridges a joint only until the slab moves †

cureF.title: Cure and protect the floor
cureF.short: Kept free of damp for 4–6 hours, walkable after approx. 12 hours (16 hours for {V360}), fully resilient after approx. 7 days; joints loadable after 14 days; protected from traffic until then.
cureF.overview: The resins cure by reaction, not by drying: the fresh layers are protected from moisture for approx. 4–6 hours (contact with water leaves white marks and a weak surface), the floor is walked only after approx. 12 hours ({V360}: 16 hours; the non-sanded barrier primer only with clean overshoes), and it carries its full load — the forklift, the car, the chemicals — after approx. 7 days ({V2370}: 10, 7 or 3 days by temperature). The joints of {IPU} reach their full loadability after 14 days. In the meantime the floor is kept closed to other trades or protected with boards †.
points: the curing follows the temperature: cold slows it, warm shortens the pot life
the overcoat windows are kept: a layer that has waited too long is sanded before the next
the first cleaning only after full resilience, with the cleaning agent of the data sheet ({R008})
keep damp off for approx. 4–6 hours ({GBM}, {B351})

serviceF.title: The floor in service
serviceF.short: Closed, seamless, easy to clean: oil, tyre softeners, cleaning agents and dilute acids stay on the surface; the forklift meets 70 N/mm²; the joints move; the floor is cleaned with {R008} and re-sealed when it wears.
serviceF.overview: The finished floor is closed and seamless: the primer has sealed the pores of the concrete, the coating carries the load (approx. 70 N/mm² compressive, Shore D approx. 72 for {B351}; approx. 109 N/mm² for the grouted bases), the seal takes the chemicals — oils, tyre softeners, cleaning agents, dilute acids and alkalis; {V2370} the sewage and the sulphuric acid — and the elastic joints follow the movement of the slab. Dust is gone, spills are wiped up, the floor is cleaned with the scrubber-drier and {R008}. When the top seal wears after years of traffic it is sanded and re-sealed: the system is renewed from the top, not replaced.
points: the barrier primers keep working underneath: vapour and oil stay in the slab
the slip class is kept by the cleaning: a floor coated with dirt and oil is slippery whatever its profile †
inspection of the joints and the edges with the annual cleaning †
a floor coating is wear protection: it is renewed from the top

notesF.title: Observe the limits of the data sheets
notesF.short: Substrate and air 10–35 °C (10–30 °C for {V2260}, {V2370}), at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 80 % (65 % for {V360}); pot lives and overcoat windows; storage frost-free; safety data sheets.
notesF.overview: The data sheets set the working limits: substrate and air temperature 10–35 °C (10–30 °C for {V2260} and {V2370}), at least 3 °C above the dew point and a relative humidity of at most 80 % (65 % for {V360}); no water is added to the resins (except the prescribed dilution of {V360} and {V2260}); the pot lives (15–20 minutes for {SG3F}, 30 for {B351}, 35 for {GBM} and {SG3}, 40 for {V360}, 60 for {SG2} and {K4031}, 120 for {EV200}) and the overcoat windows are kept; the material is stored frost-free, cool and dry at 10–25 °C (12–24 months, {ANTI}, {FF}, {QS} and {R008} longer); opened containers are used promptly. The applicable safety data sheets, the GISCODE and the EMICODE of the products are observed.
points: the ideal material temperature is +15 °C; the containers are brought to temperature before the work
the mixing: component A stirred, component B added completely, approx. 3 minutes at approx. 300 rpm, decanted and stirred again
the data sheets are the valid document: this guide follows the issues of 21/06/2023 – 14/05/2026
a trial area where the substrate, the colour or the slip class are in doubt
notesF.src: GBM · SG2 · SG3 · SG3-superfast · B351 · V360W · V2260 · V2370 · EV200 · K4031

pfgarage.name: Garage and cellar floor
pfgarage.problem: The floor of a garage, a cellar or a small warehouse dusts under the tyres and the boxes, drinks the oil drip and the water the car brings in, stains and is never clean. The slab is dry and sound, the budget and the time are small — the floor must be done over a weekend and look finished.
pfgarage.solution: The aqueous seal {V360} does the whole floor in two days: diluted with 8–10 % water as the primer, filled with {FF} for the pinholes and with quartz sand for the levelling, rolled criss-cross in two steps as the satin, pigmented, vapour-permeable seal — walkable after 16 hours, resistant to tyre softeners, heating oil, petrol and dilute acids. {ANTI} in the last step gives R10; the wall–floor joint is closed with {IPU}.

pfwork.name: Workshop and commercial floor
pfwork.problem: A workshop, a laboratory, a sales or commercial unit: trolleys, tools, oils and cleaning agents on a dry concrete slab that must become a smooth, coloured, easy-to-clean floor — glossy in the showroom, slip resistant where it is washed — with the joints of the slab taken through and the anchor holes of the old machines filled.
pfwork.solution: The pore-sealing primer {GBM} (or {G1270}), sanded; a scratch coat where the slab is rough; the self-levelling coating {B351} at approx. 1 mm, de-aerated with the spiked roller — approx. 70 N/mm², Shore D approx. 72, Bfl-s1; the glossy PU top seal {V2260}, with {ANTI} for R11; the joints cut and filled with {IPU}, chamfered under vehicle traffic; holes and anchors with {K4031}.

pfhall.name: Hall and logistics floor
pfhall.problem: A production or logistics hall: forklifts and pallet trucks on small hard wheels, dropped pallets, pallet racking on anchors, the machine bases that must be grouted, the wet zone at the loading door — and a floor that is cleaned with the scrubber-drier every night. The coating must carry the point loads and the impacts for years.
pfhall.solution: {GBM} in two steps, the second sanded, levels and seals the slab; the machine bases and the rail grouting with {EV200} (approx. 109 N/mm² after 7 days); the thick coat of {B351} filled 2 : 1 with quartz sand at approx. 2 mm; the slip-resistant finish — interspersing coat, quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm, top seal — for R11 to R12; the field and connection joints with {IPU}, 25 % total deformation, edges chamfered 45°.

pfdamp.name: Damp and young concrete
pfdamp.problem: The slab is young and will not dry in time, a basement floor stands on ground water, a floor has no vapour barrier: the residual moisture is above 4 CM-% and vapour presses from below — a standard primer would lift. The programme does not allow weeks of drying, and the floor must be coated like a dry floor afterwards.
pfdamp.solution: The barrier primer {SG3} bonds to the matt damp concrete and blocks vapour and negative pressing water up to 3 bar in two coats, the second sanded; {SG3F} where only 3.5 hours between the coats can be spared; {SG3T} up the plinth and the wall and for the capillary-breaking mortar. On the sanded barrier the coating of {B351}, the slip-resistant finish and the joints with {IPU} follow as on any dry floor.

pfoil.name: Oil-contaminated concrete
pfoil.problem: A workshop or a machine hall whose concrete has drunk oil for decades: the oil rises through the capillaries, no primer bonds, every coating lifts. The surface is damp from the cleaning, the breakouts of the old machine bases are open — and the new floor must carry forklifts.
pfoil.solution: After shot blasting the surface is cleaned with {R008} and hot water — sprayed, scrubbed until brownish, rinsed, vacuumed, repeated — and not dried off; the special primer {SG2} bonds to the damp, oil-free concrete and blocks capillary-rising oil and vapour (sd > 100 m) and water to 3 bar, sanded over the whole surface. Then the hall floor: breakouts and bases with {EV200}, the thick coat of {B351} with quartz sand, the slip-resistant finish, the joints with {IPU}.

pfsewage.name: Wastewater plant and sewage tank
pfsewage.problem: The tanks, channels and digestion towers of a sewage treatment plant: sewage, sulphuric acid formed by the biogenic corrosion down to pH 0–1, sea water, the abrasion of the flow and the stray currents of the plant attack concrete and steel — the sheet piles, the gullies, the anchors. The coating must be chemically resistant, elastifying and closed on both materials.
pfsewage.solution: The thixotropic barrier primer {SG3T} on floor and walls of the cementitious substrate; breakouts, gullies and anchors grouted with {EV200}, watertight to 5 bar; the sealing coating {V2370} in two layers in alternating colours — on steel blasted to Sa 2½ the first layer is the primer — exposure class XWW4 after DIN 19753, Shore A approx. 80, stray-current insulating; the movement joints with {IPU}, −40 to +80 °C.

hseText: Observe the safety data sheets of the products; wear the personal protective equipment they prescribe (gloves, goggles, respiratory protection with organic-vapour filters for resins, dust masks for powders).
Ensure ventilation in enclosed rooms; keep ignition sources away from solvent-containing products; keep the products away from drains and watercourses.

CMP.pf.products[0].why: One resin for priming, scratch coats, mortars (5–30 mm) and epoxy screeds (11–150 mm): fewer products on site, one mixing rule (1 : 1 with sand for the scratch coat, approx. 3 : 25 for the screed).
Published tensile adhesion ≥ 1.5 N/mm² on concrete that is dry to matt damp; the comparable primers state a dry substrate (≤ 4 % moisture, no rising damp) as the condition.
Flexural strength approx. 35 N/mm² (DIN EN 196-1) against approx. 15 N/mm² published for the Sikafloor-156 mortar — the figures are not from identical test bodies and are quoted as printed.
Pot life approx. 35 minutes at a simple 100 : 50 mixing ratio.

Published as watertight against negative pressing water up to 3 bar; the comparable products are described for damp or green concrete without a stated pressure rating.
Overcoating window of 12 hours to 5 days gives the schedule room; the following resin layers bond to the sanded second coat.
The same resin serves as scratch coat and mortar binder (1 : 1 and approx. 3 : 25 with quartz sand).

Overcoatable after 12 hours (24 hours for Sikafloor-264 N at +20 °C): two coats in two days.
Reaction to fire Bfl-s1 and slip resistance R11 to R12 with quartz sand are published in the technical data sheet.
One product from the thin roller coat (0.4–0.5 kg/m²) to the self-smoothing thick coat (2 : 1 with quartz sand) and the broadcast slip system.

Slip resistance R10 with ASO-Antislide stirred into the last coat, by test report.

CMP.pf.products[4].why: An elastic epoxy (Shore A approx. 80) for the sealing of tanks, channels and pits — it follows the small movements of the concrete; the comparable epoxy coatings are rigid (Shore D 80–82).

The published chemical-resistance list names the media of the wastewater plant by name (acids, alkalis, fuels, oils, solvents, formaldehyde); Sikafloor-381 and Mapecoat I 24 refer to lists on request.
Pot life 45–55 minutes at +20 °C with a 7 : 1 ratio — the longest working time of the four.
Applied directly on blasted steel without a primer; on concrete over ASODUR-SG3-thix.

CMP.pf.products[5].why: Shore A approx. 40 with 25 % permissible deformation: firm enough for the wheels of forklifts and trolleys, elastic enough for the field and wall joints of the slab.
Service temperature −40 to +80 °C, published; Sikaflex PRO-3 is published to +70 °C.
Tear resistance approx. 9.0 N/mm² and recovery > 90 % — the joint returns after the load.
Edges chamfered under vehicle traffic and a width : depth of 1 : 0.8 are specified in the technical data sheet, so the detail is designed, not improvised.

CMP.inj.products[0].why: A true two-component, non-foaming elastic resin (1 : 1 by volume): the seal is a solid, soft-elastic body of resin in the crack — the single-component competitors (SikaInject-232, Nitofill PU150) foam with water and seal with a foam.
Shore A approx. 47 after 21 hours and final curing in approx. 5 hours at +20 °C: the component can be loaded the same day.
Viscosity approx. 125 mPa·s reaches the fine branches of the crack; comparable in class to Sika Injection-201 CE (~100 mPa·s) and well below the 300–650 cps of the single-component resins.
Consumption approx. 1.1 kg per litre of voids is published, so the quantity can be estimated from the crack volume.

Foams to up to approx. 40 times its volume, at the top of the range published by the comparable products (20–45×).
Designed as the first step of the two-step injection: the foam stops the water, AQUAFIN-P4 then seals the crack permanently through the same packers.

E-modulus approx. 20 GPa, the lowest of the four published values (26 GPa Mapegrout Thixotropic, ≥ 29 GPa SikaEmaco S 5400): a stiffness closer to the parent concrete, so the repair follows the structure rather than fighting it.
Starts at 5 mm (Sika MonoTop-4012 from 6 mm, Mapegrout Thixotropic from 10 mm) — thin breakouts are repaired with the same mortar.
Consumption approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm against approx. 1.9 kg for the comparable mortars.

Up to 6 mm in one step on walls and floors; Sika MonoTop-3020 and Planitop 200 stop at 5 and 3 mm per coat.
Pot life approx. 60 minutes for large areas of fine smoothing.
Classified to EN 1504-3 (R2) like the repair mortar it closes — one standard across the system; Planitop 200 is classified as an EN 1504-2 coating.

One-component and cement-based: brushed into the matt damp substrate, the repair mortar follows wet in wet.

Working time approx. 30 minutes for the chase and the cove in one pass; the rapid plugs set within 1–3 minutes and are meant for the running leak only (in the SCHOMBURG system FIX-20-T takes that role).
Published consumption per metre of chase and cove (approx. 1.3 kg/m) — the quantity follows the drawing.
AQUAFIN-IC follows wet in wet after 1–3 hours: one crystalline system from the crack to the surface.

One component — water is the only addition (SikaTop Seal-107 is a two-component kit).
Pot life approx. 60 minutes and overcoating after approx. 6 hours; the system build-up is given in kg/m² for the water load, so the quantity follows the exposure class.

Crack bridging published on three methods (EN 14891 > 0.75 mm, PG MDS/FPD 0.4 mm, ASTM C836 > 2.6 mm) — the figures are comparable method by method; Vandex BB75E-Z publishes < 0.8 mm, Sikalastic-152 ~1.2 mm (EN 1062-7).
Both pressure directions published: 2.5 bar positive and 0.75 bar negative (WTA 4-6); the comparison products publish either a positive value or none.
CO₂ diffusion Sd > 200 m at 2 mm: protects the reinforcement against carbonation as well as the structure against water.

CMP.wp.products[2].why: A bitumen-free thick coating tested to the German regulation for bitumen thick coatings (PG MDS/FPD) — the category that replaces bitumen on the outside of basements under DIN 18533; Mapelastic 2KR Plus is the only comparison product in the same category and publishes no figures on its page.
Crack bridging to 2 mm and 5 bar at 3 mm dry film, rainproof after approx. 3 hours on slopes, pressing water after approx. 16 hours — the excavation can be closed the next day.
Light: approx. 1.1 kg/m² per mm (density approx. 1.1 kg/dm³) — fewer kilograms carried for the same thickness than the 1.2–2.0 kg/m² per mm of the cementitious membranes.
Negative pressure value published (0.75 bar, WTA 4-6) for the inside of the pit as well.

CMP.wp.products[3].why: Classified as an OS 5b surface protection system (Rili-SIB / DIN V 18026) — the German class for crack-bridging protection of concrete; none of the comparison sheets claims the class.
Dynamic crack bridging class B2 at −20 °C after 2,000 hours of UV weathering is published — the behaviour in winter and after ageing, not only the static value at +20 °C.
CO₂ diffusion Sd > 200 m against 104 m (Sikalastic-6100 FX) and > 50 m (SikaTop-550 Seal): a carbonation brake of twice the thickness-equivalent.
Consumption for the OS 5b build-up is published as a system value (approx. 5.5 kg/m²).

CMP.rc.products[0].why: The negative pressure resistance is a published figure (1.5 bar) and the impermeability a test value (14 bar, CRD-C 48-92); the comparable sheets describe "either side" application without a negative value, and only Krystol T1 publishes a CRD-C 48 result.
EN 1504-2 values measured, not declared as classes: capillary absorption w < 0.1 kg/m²·h⁰·⁵ and Sd < 5 m.
Working time approx. 60 minutes — twice to three times the 20–30 minutes of the crystalline slurries compared.
Consumption by water load from 0.75 kg/m² (one coat) to 1.5 kg/m² (two coats), with drinking-water testing to DVGW W 270 / W 347.

CMP.rc.products[2].why: Swellable: the plug expands as it sets and locks into the dovetailed chase against the running water.

Strength development published at 1 hour, 24 hours and 28 days (approx. 3 / 15 / 30 N/mm²) and consumption per litre of void (approx. 2 kg/l) — the comparable plugs publish strength at 7 days or in psi, and no yield per void.
Working time approx. 2 minutes: long enough to press the plug and hold it, short enough to stop the flow.
Part of the crystalline system: the plug is overcoated with ASOCRET-IM and AQUAFIN-IC, no separate waterstop product line.

CMP.ca.products[0].why: Two effects from one liquid: the crystalline waterproofing and a plasticising effect that reduces the water demand of the mix — the comparable liquids are pore blockers or crystalline admixtures without a stated plasticising action.
Minimum cement content 270 kg/m³ (CEM I), published; Sika WT-100 L requires 350 kg/m³ and a w/c ≤ 0.45.
Dosed with the mixing water at the plant or into the truck on site, with the mixing time per m³ stated — the procedure is written for the Taiwanese ready-mix practice (truck dosing).
Minimum binder contents are published per cement type (CEM I / II / III), so the recipe check is part of the data sheet.

CMP.ca.products[1].why: Crystalline and hydrophobic in one powder: the pores are blocked by crystal growth and made water-repellent, two mechanisms against capillary water.
Dosage approx. 0.75–1.25 % of the cement — in water-soluble bags for the mixer truck, with the mixing time per m³ stated.
Minimum cement content from 270 kg/m³ (CEM I) is published; Sika WT-200 P and Idrocrete KR 1000 require 350 kg/m³.
The data sheet names the CEM types and blends for which the dosage applies; the comparable sheets give a general dosage per m³ or per 100 kg of cementitious material.
